lessons.title: Honors: If I had known: si + pluperfect subjunctive
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 14 sorted conditions into three kinds and left the third one for later: the condition
that is contrary to fact in the past. "If I had known, I would have come." It's the sentence of
regrets, near misses and alternative histories, and you already have half of it: the conditional
perfect from lesson 11 (*habría venido*). This lesson adds the other half, the **pluperfect
subjunctive** (*hubiera sabido*), and shows the combinations you'll hear: the standard one, the
very common *hubiera… hubiera*, the mixed conditions that join a past cause to a present result,
and *ojalá* for regrets.

There is no drill form for the pluperfect subjunctive: it's built from *hubiera*, which you can
already make (lesson 13), and the participles you know. Practice it here in sentences.

## The form: hubiera + participle

The pluperfect subjunctive is the imperfect subjunctive of *haber* + a participle. The participle
never changes.

| | *haber* (imperfect subjunctive) | + participle |
|---|---|---|
| (que) yo | hubiera | sabido |
| tú | hubieras | llegado |
| él, ella, usted | hubiera | hecho |
| nosotros | hubiéramos | visto |
| (vosotros) | (hubierais) | dicho |
| ellos, ellas, ustedes | hubieran | ido |

The *-se* version (*hubiese, hubiésemos*) means the same and is common in writing; recognize it.
Pronouns go before *hubiera*, never between it and the participle: *Si me lo hubieras dicho*
(If you had told me), not ~~*Si hubieras me lo dicho*~~. Irregular participles are the usual ones
(lesson 09): *hecho, dicho, visto, puesto, escrito, vuelto, roto, abierto, muerto, resuelto*.

## The past contrary-to-fact sentence

*Si* + pluperfect subjunctive sets a condition that didn't happen; the main clause says what
would have followed, in the conditional perfect:

- *Si hubiera sabido que estabas enfermo, habría ido a verte.* — If I'd known you were sick, I
  would have gone to see you. (I didn't know, so I didn't go.)
- *Si hubiéramos salido antes, no habríamos perdido el vuelo.* — If we'd left earlier, we wouldn't
  have missed the flight.
- *¿Qué habrías hecho tú si te hubieran ofrecido ese trabajo?* — What would you have done if
  they'd offered you that job?

As in lesson 14, either clause can come first, with a comma when *si* comes first, and the
conditional never goes after *si*: ~~*Si habría sabido…*~~ → *Si hubiera sabido…*

![Two paths from one moment in the past. The real path, drawn solid, goes from "No sabía que había examen" through "No estudié" to "Reprobé". The imagined path, drawn dashed, branches from the same start: "Si hubiera sabido…", then "habría estudiado", then a fork: "y habría aprobado" (a result in the past) and "y ahora tendría la beca" (a result now: a mixed condition).](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

### Hubiera in both halves

In everyday speech, in Mexico and across the Spanish-speaking world, the main clause very often
uses *hubiera* + participle too:

*Si hubiera sabido, hubiera venido.* = *Si hubiera sabido, habría venido.*

The RAE and ASALE's *Nueva gramática* accepts the *-ra* form there as an alternative to
*habría*; it is normal in speech and in many writers. The *-se* form in the main clause (*…,
hubiese venido*) also turns up, especially in writing from Spain, but it is much rarer and usage
guides disagree about it: don't use it yourself. *Habría* is the safest choice in formal writing and in an
exam; *hubiera… hubiera* is what you'll hear most at the kitchen table.

### Mixed conditions

Real life often mixes times: a past cause with a present result, or a present fact that would
have changed the past. Spanish just uses the form each half needs. This is called a **mixed
conditional**:

| Past condition → present result | Present condition → past result |
|---|---|
| *Si hubiera estudiado medicina, ahora sería doctora.* — If I'd studied medicine, I'd be a doctor now. | *Si fuera más organizado, no habría perdido las llaves.* — If I were more organized, I wouldn't have lost my keys. |
| *Si no hubiéramos vendido la casa, ahora viviríamos en el centro.* — If we hadn't sold the house, we'd live downtown now. | *Si hablara inglés, me habrían dado el puesto.* — If I spoke English, they'd have given me the job. |

Words that point to the present help: *ahora, hoy, a estas horas* (by now, at this time): *Si no
hubiera llovido, a estas horas ya estaríamos en la playa* (If it hadn't rained, we'd be at the
beach by now).

### Ojalá and como si with the past

*Ojalá* + pluperfect subjunctive is a regret about the past, "I wish I had…":

- *Ojalá hubiera estudiado más.* — I wish I had studied more.
- *Ojalá no le hubiera dicho nada.* — I wish I hadn't said anything to her.

Compare lesson 13: *Ojalá tuviera tiempo* (I wish I had time: now) vs *Ojalá hubiera tenido
tiempo* (I wish I'd had time: then). And *como si* + pluperfect subjunctive is "as if something
had happened": *Me miró como si hubiera visto un fantasma* (She looked at me as if she'd seen a
ghost; *el fantasma* is lesson 04's).

## Shortcuts and regret words

- *De haberlo sabido* (Had I known; literally "of having known it") replaces a whole *si*
  clause: *De haberlo sabido, no habría venido.* It's a fixed phrase in speech; *de haber* +
  participle works with other verbs in a formal style: *De haber llegado antes, lo habríamos
  visto.*
- *Por poco* (almost, nearly) takes the present tense for a past near miss, which surprises
  English speakers: *Por poco me caigo* (I nearly fell). The preterite (*Por poco me caí*) is
  also heard, but the present is the everyday form: *Por poco perdemos el camión* (We nearly
  missed the bus).
- *De otro modo* (otherwise): *Salimos temprano; de otro modo, no habríamos llegado.*
- *Equivocarse* (*me equivoqué*; to make a mistake, to be wrong) and *la equivocación* (a mistake,
  an error of judgment): *Me equivoqué de camión. Fue una equivocación.* A1's *equivocado* is the
  adjective (*Estás equivocado*).
- *Salvarse* (to be saved, to escape): *Si no hubiera llevado el casco, no se habría salvado*
  (If he hadn't been wearing his helmet, he wouldn't have survived; *el casco* is lesson 05's).
- *Culpar* (to blame), often *culpar a alguien de algo*: *Me culpó del error.*
- *El remordimiento* (remorse, a guilty conscience) and *arrepentido* (sorry, regretful: *Estoy
  arrepentida*), the adjective of lesson 11's *arrepentirse*.

## Worked examples

### Example 1: from facts to a regret

Facts: *No revisé el pronóstico. Fui a la montaña sin chamarra. Me dio gripa.*

1. Find what didn't happen and turn it into the *si* clause: I didn't check → *Si hubiera revisado
   el pronóstico…*
2. Say what would have followed, in the conditional perfect: *…habría llevado una chamarra.*
3. Chain a second step if you want: *Si hubiera llevado una chamarra, no me habría dado gripa.*
4. Add a regret with *ojalá*: *Ojalá hubiera revisado el pronóstico.*

### Example 2: choosing past or present for the result

Facts: *Marta no aceptó la beca en Chile hace cinco años. Hoy trabaja en Toluca.*

- Past result: *Si hubiera aceptado la beca, habría vivido en Santiago.* (Then.)
- Present result: *Si hubiera aceptado la beca, ahora trabajaría en Chile.* (Now: mixed.)
- With *a estas horas*: *A estas horas estaría dando clases en Santiago.*

Both results are correct; the time word decides. Check: is the result about then (*habría* +
participle) or about now (*-ría*)?

### Example 3: a story of a near miss

> El jueves por poco pierdo el avión a Mérida. Me equivoqué de terminal y llegué a la puerta
> cuando ya estaban cerrando. Si no hubiera corrido como loca, me habría quedado en tierra. Si
> hubiera revisado el boleto la noche anterior, no habría pasado nada. De haberlo sabido, habría
> salido una hora antes. La empleada me miró como si nunca hubiera visto a nadie tan despeinado.
> Al final me salvé, pero no culpo a nadie: fue una equivocación mía. Y si no me hubiera subido a
> ese avión, ahora no estaría escribiendo esto desde una hamaca.

Translation: "On Thursday I nearly missed my plane to Mérida. I went to the wrong terminal and got
to the gate when they were already closing it. If I hadn't run like crazy, I'd have been left
behind. If I'd checked my ticket the night before, nothing would have happened. Had I known, I'd
have left an hour earlier. The employee looked at me as if she had never seen anyone so
disheveled. In the end I made it, but I don't blame anyone: it was my own mistake. And if I hadn't
gotten on that plane, I wouldn't be writing this from a hammock now."

Find the forms: *por poco pierdo* (present for a near miss), three *si* + *hubiera* sentences
(two with *habría* + participle, the last one mixed: *ahora no estaría escribiendo*), *de haberlo sabido*, *como si
nunca hubiera visto*. *Quedarse en tierra* means to miss your flight or boat.

## Common mistakes

- The conditional after *si*: ~~*Si habría sabido*~~ → *Si hubiera sabido.*
- The imperfect subjunctive when you mean the past: *Si estudiara, aprobaría* is "if I studied
  (now), I'd pass"; for last semester's exam: *Si hubiera estudiado, habría aprobado.*
- Splitting *hubiera* and the participle with a pronoun: → *Si me lo hubieras dicho.*
- *Por poco* + preterite in English style: *Por poco me caí* is possible, but *Por poco me caigo*
  is what most people say.
- *Equivocarse de* + noun means "to get the wrong one": *Me equivoqué de número* (I dialed the
  wrong number), not ~~*Me equivoqué el número*~~.

## Key points

- Pluperfect subjunctive = *hubiera, hubieras, hubiera, hubiéramos, hubieran* + participle
  (*hubiese* also); no drill form.
- Past contrary to fact: *Si hubiera sabido, habría venido.* In speech, also *…, hubiera venido.*
- Mixed: *Si hubiera estudiado, ahora sería…; Si fuera más organizado, no habría perdido…*
- *Ojalá hubiera…* = I wish I had…; *como si hubiera…* = as if (it) had…
- *De haberlo sabido, por poco* + present, *de otro modo, a estas horas, equivocarse (de), culpar
  (de), salvarse, arrepentido, el remordimiento.*

lessons.title: Honors: Utopías y distopías: what would the world be like if…?
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This module has given you the language of the unreal: *ojalá* and *como si* (lesson 13), *si*
clauses (14), and with honors 16h1 the past that didn't happen. Science fiction lives on exactly
these forms. Every story of the future begins with a question, *¿Cómo sería el mundo si…?*
(What would the world be like if…?), and every good one answers it in detail.

This lesson reads an original science-fiction story in two short parts and pulls the grammar out
of it: hypotheticals, *como si*, and the future perfect of lesson 11 (*Para 2150 habremos
colonizado otro planeta*). First, the two ideas the story plays with: utopia and dystopia.

## Utopia and dystopia

The word *utopía* comes from a book. In 1516 the English humanist Thomas More (in Spanish, *Tomás
Moro*) published, in Latin, a short work describing an imaginary island called Utopia, whose
society he set against the Europe of his time. It was first printed in Leuven (in today's
Belgium). The name is built from Greek and is usually explained as "no place"; it also sounds like
"good place" (*eu-topia*), and that double meaning stuck. Today *una utopía* is an ideal society,
or any plan that is too perfect to be possible: *Un mundo sin pobreza parece una utopía* (A world
without poverty seems like a utopia).

*La distopía* is the opposite: a society that looks orderly or even happy, but is unjust,
controlled or frightening. Two English novels shaped the idea in the twentieth century: Aldous
Huxley's *Brave New World* (1932), known in Spanish as *Un mundo feliz*, and George Orwell's
*Nineteen Eighty-Four* (1949), *1984* in Spanish. The adjective is *distópico*: *una película
distópica*.

![Two panels side by side. On the left, labeled utopía: a bright city under a yellow sun, with gardens on the roofs, a solar panel on one of them, a tree, two people on the grass and a small robot carrying a basket. On the right, labeled distopía: a gray city of identical towers, security cameras on poles, a giant screen showing one face, and six identical people standing in a line.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The words of the genre are often cognates. *Futurista* (futuristic) is the same for both genders:
*una ciudad futurista*. *El robot* (plural *los robots*) is a machine; *el androide* is a robot
shaped like a person. *El clon* (plural *los clones*) is a clone and *clonar* is to clone.
*Colonizar* (*colonicé*) is to colonize; a planet where people can live is *habitable*. *La
humanidad* is humanity, *sobrevivir* is to survive, and *la supervivencia* is survival.

## The story, part 1: La colonia Esperanza

Read it once for the plot, then again with the notes below it.

> Me llamo Ixchel y nací en Esperanza, la primera colonia humana fuera del sistema solar. Mis
> abuelos salieron de la Tierra en 2089, cuando el planeta ya casi no era habitable. Mi abuela
> siempre decía: "Si no nos hubiéramos ido, no habríamos sobrevivido". Yo la escuchaba como si me
> contara un cuento de hadas.
>
> En Esperanza nadie trabaja más de cuatro horas al día. Los robots limpian las calles, los
> androides enseñan en las escuelas y cuidan a los enfermos, aunque casi nadie se enferma. La
> comida crece en jardines sobre los techos. No hay dinero, ni cárceles, ni desempleo. Los adultos
> viven como si fueran eternos: tienen ciento veinte años y parecen de cincuenta.
>
> En la escuela nos enseñan que Esperanza es la utopía que la humanidad siempre buscó. "Si Tomás
> Moro nos viera", dice la maestra androide, "pensaría que su isla era real". Y nos recuerda que
> para el año 2200 habremos colonizado tres planetas más.
>
> A veces me pregunto qué haría si viviera en la Tierra de antes, con su ruido, sus guerras y sus
> problemas. Creo que me aburriría menos. Pero eso no se lo digo a nadie.

Translation: "My name is Ixchel and I was born in Esperanza, the first human colony outside the
solar system. My grandparents left Earth in 2089, when the planet was almost no longer habitable.
My grandmother always said, 'If we hadn't left, we wouldn't have survived.' I listened to her as
if she were telling me a fairy tale. / In Esperanza nobody works more than four hours a day.
Robots clean the streets; androids teach in the schools and look after the sick, although almost
nobody gets sick. Food grows in gardens on the roofs. There's no money, no prisons, no
unemployment. The adults live as if they were eternal: they're a hundred and twenty and look
fifty. / At school they teach us that Esperanza is the utopia humanity always looked for. 'If
Thomas More saw us,' says our android teacher, 'he'd think his island was real.' And she reminds
us that by the year 2200 we will have colonized three more planets. / Sometimes I wonder what I
would do if I lived on the Earth of the past, with its noise, its wars and its problems. I think
I'd be less bored. But I don't tell anyone that."

Notes: *Si no nos hubiéramos ido, no habríamos sobrevivido* (16h1) is a past condition; *como si
me contara* and *como si fueran eternos* are lesson 13's *como si*; *Si Tomás Moro nos viera,
pensaría…* and *qué haría si viviera…* are lesson 14's hypotheticals; *habremos colonizado* is the
future perfect (lesson 11): finished before 2200. *Un cuento de hadas* is a fairy tale; *la
guerra* is war.

## The story, part 2: Lo que no se veía

> Un día, buscando a mi gato, bajé por una escalera que no aparecía en ningún mapa. Abajo había
> una fábrica enorme y caliente. Cientos de personas trabajaban sin descanso, y todas tenían la
> misma cara: la cara de mi vecino Tomás.
>
> Uno de ellos me miró como si nunca hubiera visto a una niña. "¿Quiénes son ustedes?", le
> pregunté. Me contestó en voz baja que eran clones, que los habían clonado para hacer el trabajo
> que los robots no podían hacer, y que nunca habían salido de allí.
>
> Subí corriendo. Esa noche le conté todo a mi abuela. Me escuchó en silencio y después me dijo
> que ya lo sabía, que todos los adultos lo sabían. "La supervivencia tiene un precio", me
> explicó. "Si la gente supiera la verdad, Esperanza no duraría ni un año".
>
> No dormí. Pensé que, si nadie hacía nada, en cien años la colonia habría construido diez
> fábricas más. Y entendí que una utopía para unos puede ser una distopía para otros. Mañana voy a
> volver a la escalera. Si los clones quieren salir, les voy a abrir la puerta.

Translation: "One day, looking for my cat, I went down a staircase that wasn't on any map.
Below there was a huge, hot factory. Hundreds of people were working without a break, and they
all had the same face: the face of my neighbor Tomás. / One of them looked at me as if he had
never seen a girl. 'Who are you?' I asked him. He answered quietly that they were clones, that
they had been cloned to do the work the robots couldn't do, and that they had never been out of
there. / I ran upstairs. That night I told my grandmother everything. She listened in silence
and then told me she already knew, that all the adults knew. 'Survival has a price,' she
explained. 'If people knew the truth, Esperanza wouldn't last even a year.' / I didn't sleep. I
thought that if nobody did anything, in a hundred years the colony would have built ten more
factories. And I understood that a utopia for some can be a dystopia for others. Tomorrow I'm
going back to the staircase. If the clones want to get out, I'm going to open the door for
them."

Notes: *como si nunca hubiera visto* is *como si* + pluperfect subjunctive (16h1). The clone's
answer is reported speech (lesson 16): *"Somos clones; nos clonaron…; nunca hemos salido" → me
contestó que eran clones, que los habían clonado…, que nunca habían salido*. *Si la gente
supiera…, no duraría* is hypothetical: the grandmother is sure people don't know. *Pensé que, si nadie hacía nada, … habría construido* is a thought reported from the past
(lesson 16): Ixchel thought *"Si nadie hace nada, en cien años la colonia habrá construido…"*,
a real condition, so *hace* shifts to the indicative *hacía* (not a subjunctive) and the future
perfect *habrá construido* shifts to the conditional perfect *habría construido*.
The last sentence is a real condition, *si* + present + *ir a*: Ixchel now thinks it may happen.

## Worked examples

### Example 1: turning a "what if" into sentences

Question: *¿Cómo sería la vida si los robots hicieran todo el trabajo?*

1. Keep the *si* clause from the question, in the imperfect subjunctive: *Si los robots hicieran
   todo el trabajo…*
2. Answer in the conditional, one idea per sentence: *…tendríamos más tiempo libre. Nadie haría
   trabajos peligrosos.*
3. Add the downside, still hypothetical: *Pero si nadie trabajara, ¿de dónde sacaríamos el
   dinero?*
4. Close with an opinion and the present: *Creo que sería una utopía solo si todos compartiéramos
   la riqueza.* (*Solo si*, "only if", follows the rules of *si*.)

### Example 2: three futures, three forms

Each sentence about the year 2150 says something different:

- *En 2150 colonizaremos Marte.* — a prediction (future).
- *Para 2150 habremos colonizado Marte.* — finished before that date (future perfect, lesson 11).
- *Si colonizáramos Marte, ¿quién viviría allí?* — an imagined situation (hypothetical).

And looking back from the story's point of view: *Si mis abuelos se hubieran quedado en la
Tierra, yo no habría nacido en Esperanza* (past, 16h1).

### Example 3: a short discussion text

> ¿Vivirías en una ciudad perfecta si tuvieras que renunciar a tu libertad? Yo no. Si todo
> estuviera decidido por una computadora, la vida sería cómoda, pero no sería mía. Por otro lado,
> entiendo a quienes dicen que sí: si mi familia no tuviera agua ni trabajo, quizás pensaría
> distinto. Para mí, la verdadera utopía no es un lugar sin problemas, sino un lugar donde
> podamos resolverlos juntos.

Translation: "Would you live in a perfect city if you had to give up your freedom? I wouldn't. If
everything were decided by a computer, life would be comfortable, but it wouldn't be mine. On the
other hand, I understand people who say yes: if my family had no water or work, maybe I'd think
differently. For me, the true utopia isn't a place without problems, but a place where we can
solve them together."

Notice *donde podamos* (lesson 08: a place we're looking for, not one we know) and *sino* after a
negative (but rather).

## Common mistakes

- *Si* + conditional in a question: ~~*¿Qué pasaría si los robots tendrían…?*~~ → *si los robots
  tuvieran…*
- *Como si* + present: ~~*Vive como si es eterno*~~ → *como si fuera eterno.*
- Confusing the future perfect and the conditional perfect: *Para 2200 habremos colonizado* (we
  will have) vs *habríamos colonizado* (we would have).
- Forgetting the plural forms: *los robots, los clones* (not ~~*los clons*~~), *las utopías*.
- Writing *distopía* without its accent: the stress is on *-pí-*: *dis-to-PÍ-a*, like *u-to-PÍ-a*.

## Key points

- *Utopía* (More, 1516: "no place", also "good place") and *distopía* (Huxley, *Un mundo feliz*,
  1932; Orwell, *1984*, 1949).
- Science fiction uses all of this module's forms: *¿Cómo sería el mundo si…? Si fuera…, sería…;
  como si fueran eternos; si no nos hubiéramos ido, no habríamos sobrevivido.*
- Future perfect for "by then": *Para 2200 habremos colonizado tres planetas.*
- *El robot, el androide, el clon, clonar, colonizar, habitable, la humanidad, la supervivencia,
  sobrevivir, futurista.*

lessons.title: Even though it's expensive: concession, cause and consequence
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This module is about arguing a point: why something happens, what follows from it, and what you
accept along the way. In A2 you linked ideas with *porque, como, por eso, así que* and *aunque*.
Now that you know the subjunctive (lessons 01–08) and the imperfect subjunctive (13–16), *aunque*
can carry a real difference in meaning, and you can add the formal links that opinion texts, the
news and the DELE B1 writing tasks use. The theme is climate change, a step on from A2's recycling.

These linking words are **[[connectors]]**: they show how two ideas relate. This lesson covers
concession ("although"), cause ("because") and consequence ("so").

## *Aunque* with the indicative or the subjunctive

A **[[concessive clause]]** admits something that might stop the main idea, and then says the main
idea holds anyway: *Aunque llueve, salimos.* Spanish lets the mood carry part of the meaning.

### Indicative: a fact you assert

You present the information as true and as news to
the listener.

- *Aunque llueve, vamos a salir.* — Even though it's raining, we're going out. (It is raining:
  I'm telling you.)

### Subjunctive: a possibility you don't know about

The speaker doesn't know whether it's true
(often about the future), and it makes no difference.

- *Aunque llueva mañana, vamos a salir.* — Even if it rains tomorrow, we're going out.
- *Aunque no me inviten, voy a ir.* — Even if they don't invite me, I'm going.

### Subjunctive: a fact you wave away

This use surprises English speakers. You may
both know it's true, but you put it aside: "fine, it is; so what?"

- *Aunque sea caro, vale la pena.* — Expensive or not, it's worth it. (*valer la pena*, lesson 11)
- *—Ese carro gasta mucha gasolina. —Aunque gaste mucha, me encanta.* — "That car uses a lot of
  gas." "It may use a lot, but I love it."

So with a known fact both moods are correct, with a change in tone: *Aunque es caro, lo compro*
gives the price as information; *Aunque sea caro, lo compro* waves it away.

### Imperfect subjunctive: an unlikely case

With lessons 13–14's forms, usually with a conditional:
*Aunque tuviera dinero, no compraría ese carro.* — Even if I had the money, I wouldn't buy that
car.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  accTitle: Indicative or subjunctive after aunque
  accDescr: A decision chart. Start with the question: is the clause after aunque something you present as true and new to the listener? If yes, use the indicative, as in Aunque llueve, salimos. If no, ask: is it a possibility you don't know about, or a fact you wave away as unimportant? If either, use the present subjunctive, as in Aunque llueva mañana, saldremos, and Aunque sea caro, vale la pena. If it is unlikely or unreal, use the imperfect subjunctive with a conditional, as in Aunque tuviera dinero, no lo compraría.
  Q1{"Do you present it as a true fact, new to the listener?"}
  Q1 -- yes --> I["Indicative: Aunque llueve, salimos."]
  Q1 -- no --> Q2{"What kind of idea is it?"}
  Q2 -- "a possibility you don't know about" --> S1["Present subjunctive: Aunque llueva mañana, saldremos."]
  Q2 -- "a known fact you wave away" --> S2["Present subjunctive: Aunque sea caro, vale la pena."]
  Q2 -- "unlikely or unreal" --> S3["Imperfect subjunctive + conditional: Aunque tuviera dinero, no lo compraría."]
```

The *aunque* clause can also come second: *Vamos a salir aunque llueva.* No comma is needed then.

## Other ways to concede

- *A pesar de* + a noun or an infinitive (despite, in spite of): *A pesar de la sequía, el
  gobierno no cerró las fábricas.* *A pesar de estar cansada, terminé el
  informe.* With *el*: *a pesar del calor*.
- *A pesar de que* + a clause works like *aunque*, with either mood: *A pesar de que hace
  calor, no prendemos el aire acondicionado.*
- *Por mucho que* (however much, no matter how much) usually takes the subjunctive: *Por mucho
  que recicles, el problema no se resuelve solo en casa.* For a past fact, the indicative is
  normal: *Por mucho que insistí, no me hicieron caso.* (*hacer caso* = to pay attention, to
  listen) With a noun, *mucho* agrees: *por mucha agua que ahorres*.
- *Aun así* (even so) starts a new sentence or clause after the concession: *Los paneles
  solares son caros; aun así, cada vez más familias los instalan.* — Solar panels are expensive;
  even so, more and more families are installing them. (*aun* means "even" here and has no
  accent.)

## Cause: why it happens

You know *porque* (in the middle of the sentence) and *como* (at the start). Three more formal
conjunctions take the indicative and give a reason that the listener knows or will accept:

- *Ya que* (seeing as, since): *Ya que tenemos tiempo, vamos caminando.* — Seeing as we have
  time, let's walk.
- *Puesto que* (since; more formal): *Puesto que el agua es un recurso limitado, hay que
  cuidarla.* — Since water is a limited resource, we have to look after it.
- *Dado que* (given that; formal): *Dado que las emisiones siguen subiendo, la temperatura
  también sube.*

All three can open the sentence (as *como* does) or follow the main clause (as *porque* does): *Hay
que cuidar el agua, ya que es un recurso limitado.*

With a noun, use *debido a* or *a causa de* (because of, due to), or A2's *por*:

- *El vuelo se canceló debido a la tormenta.*
- *Muchas especies desaparecen a causa de la deforestación.*

Don't put *que* after *debido a* or *a causa de* before a noun: *debido a la lluvia*, not
~~*debido a que la lluvia*~~. (*Debido a que* + a full clause does exist: *debido a que llovió*.)

## Consequence: what follows

- A2's *así que* and *por eso* are the everyday choices.
- *Por lo tanto* (therefore) and *por consiguiente* (consequently) are more formal and
  common in writing. They usually follow a semicolon or a period and take a comma: *El ecosistema
  es muy frágil; por lo tanto, está prohibido acampar.* (*frágil* = fragile; *acampar* = to camp)
- *De modo que* (or *de manera que*) has two meanings, and the mood tells them apart:
  - with the indicative, a result: *Se acabó el agua, de modo que nos bañamos con cubeta.* — The
    water ran out, so we washed with a bucket. (*la cubeta* = bucket, Mexico)
  - with the subjunctive, a purpose (like *para que*, lesson 06): *Explícalo despacio, de modo
    que todos lo entiendan.* — Explain it slowly, so that everyone understands.
- *De ahí que* (hence, that's why) is usually followed by the subjunctive even though it gives a
  result. You'll meet it in writing; just recognize it: *Ha llovido muy poco; de ahí que haya
  escasez de agua.* (*la escasez* = shortage, lesson 14)

*La consecuencia* is the result (*como consecuencia* = as a result), and *provocar* means to
cause (*provoqué*): *El calor provocó incendios forestales.*

## A chain of causes

News about *el cambio climático* (climate change) is full of these links. Each arrow below
could be written with a different connector.

![A chain of five boxes joined by arrows. Box 1: Quemamos combustibles fósiles. Arrow labeled por eso to box 2: Aumentan las emisiones de CO2. Arrow labeled por lo tanto to box 3: Calentamiento global. Arrow labeled debido a esto to box 4: Más sequías e incendios forestales. Arrow labeled como consecuencia to box 5: Se pierden ecosistemas y especies.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

- *Quemamos combustibles fósiles (gasolina, carbón, gas); por eso aumentan las emisiones.* (*quemar*
  = to burn; *el carbón* = coal; *aumentar* = to increase, lesson 14)
- *Debido al calentamiento global, las sequías y los incendios forestales son más frecuentes.*
- *El hielo de los glaciares se derrite; por consiguiente, sube el nivel del mar.* (*el hielo* = ice;
  *derretirse* = to melt, an *e → i* verb like *pedir*: *se derrite, se derritió*)

## Some facts, with dates

- The warmest years. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO; in Spanish *la Organización
  Meteorológica Mundial, OMM*) said in January 2025 that 2024 was the warmest year on record, about
  1.55 °C above the pre-industrial average. In January 2026 it reported that 2025 was the second
  or third warmest, and that the years 2015 to 2025 are the eleven warmest on record.
- Drought in Mexico. Mexico's *Monitor de Sequía*, published by Conagua (the national water
  commission) and the Servicio Meteorológico Nacional, reported that on 15 May 2024 about 71 % of
  the country (70.76 %) was in moderate to exceptional drought.
- The vaquita. *La vaquita marina*, a small porpoise that lives only in the upper Gulf of
  California, is the classic Mexican example of an animal *en peligro de extinción*. The 2025
  survey, announced on 28 October 2025, saw between seven and ten.

Numbers like these change; check the current report before you quote them.

## Dialogue: a fan or an air conditioner?

Valeria and her brother Tomás share a small house in Hermosillo, Sonora, in July.

> Tomás: Vale, ya no aguanto. Aunque sea caro, voy a comprar un aire acondicionado.
>
> Valeria: ¿Otra vez con eso? Ya que vamos a gastar, compremos un buen ventilador.
>
> Tomás: Un ventilador no sirve con cuarenta y cinco grados. Por mucho que lo prendas, mueve aire caliente.
>
> Valeria: Puede ser. Pero el aire gasta muchísima luz, de modo que el recibo va a llegar altísimo.
>
> Tomás: A pesar del recibo, prefiero dormir. Y hay modelos que gastan menos.
>
> Valeria: Aun así, en México mucha luz sale de plantas que queman gas. Más aires, más emisiones.
>
> Tomás: Aunque tienes razón, no voy a salvar el planeta sudando.
>
> Valeria: Bueno, ¿y si ponemos paneles solares? Dado que aquí hay sol todo el año, sería lo más lógico.
>
> Tomás: ¡Eso me gusta! Así tenemos aire y energía renovable. Por lo tanto, los dos ganamos.
>
> Valeria: Perfecto. Aunque cueste más al principio, en unos años se paga solo.

> Tomás: Vale, I can't take it anymore. Expensive or not, I'm going to buy an air conditioner.
>
> Valeria: That again? Seeing as we're going to spend money, let's buy a good fan.
>
> Tomás: A fan is no use at forty-five degrees. However much you turn it on, it just moves hot air.
>
> Valeria: Maybe. But the AC uses a huge amount of electricity, so the bill is going to be sky-high.
>
> Tomás: Despite the bill, I'd rather sleep. And there are models that use less.
>
> Valeria: Even so, in Mexico a lot of the power comes from plants that burn gas. More ACs, more emissions.
>
> Tomás: Although you're right, I'm not going to save the planet by sweating.
>
> Valeria: OK, what if we put in solar panels? Given that there's sun here all year, it would be the most logical thing.
>
> Tomás: I like that! That way we have AC and renewable energy. So we both win.
>
> Valeria: Perfect. Even if it costs more at first, in a few years it pays for itself.

New words in passing: *el aire acondicionado* (air conditioner; *el aire* for short), *el
ventilador* (fan), *sudar* (to sweat), *salvar* (to save, rescue), *la planta* (here: power plant), *el panel solar*. *La luz*
(light) is also the everyday word for electricity in Mexico: *el recibo de la luz* is the
electricity bill. Tomás's *Aunque sea caro* waves the price away; *Aunque tienes razón* admits a
fact.

## A short opinion text

> ¿Ciudades sin carros?
>
> En mi ciudad, el transporte es la principal causa de las emisiones, ya que casi todos vamos en
> carro. Por consiguiente, el aire está contaminado muchos días del año. Aunque el metro y los
> camiones no sean perfectos, son la única solución realista. A pesar de que a muchos no les guste
> la idea, la ciudad debería cerrar el centro a los carros los domingos. Puesto que los recursos
> son limitados, el dinero tiene que ir al transporte público. Una ciudad sostenible empieza por
> el transporte.

> Cities without cars?
>
> In my city, transportation is the main cause of emissions, since almost all of us go by car.
> As a result, the air is polluted many days of the year. Although the metro and the buses may
> not be perfect, they're the only realistic solution. Even though many people may not like the
> idea, the city should close the downtown area to cars on Sundays. Since resources are limited,
> the money has to go to public transportation. A sustainable city starts with transportation.

In much of Mexico, *el camión* is the everyday word for a city bus (A1's *el autobús*). The subjunctive after
the concessions (*no sean perfectos, no les guste*) waves objections away. *Sostenible*
(sustainable; in Mexico *sustentable* is also very common) has one form for both genders.

## Pronunciation

- *Aun así*: *aun* is unstressed here and runs into *así*: *au-na-SÍ*.
- *Sequía* has three syllables, *se-QUÍ-a*: the accent keeps the *i* and *a* apart. Plural *sequías*.
- *Derretirse*: roll the *rr* and tap the *r* of *-tir-*: *de-rre-TIR-se*; *se de-RRI-te*.

## Common mistakes

- Using only the indicative after *aunque* because English "although" has one form. *Aunque llueva
  mañana, vamos* (even if) needs the subjunctive: you can't assert the future rain as a fact.
- ~~*A pesar de que la lluvia*~~ → *A pesar de la lluvia* (noun) or *A pesar de que llueve* (clause).
- ~~*Aún así*~~ → *aun así*: no accent when *aun* means "even".
- Starting an answer to *¿Por qué?* with *ya que* or *puesto que*: like *como*, they don't answer
  a question on their own. Answer with *Porque…*.
- Reading *de modo que* + subjunctive as a result. *Habla alto, de modo que te oigan* is a purpose:
  so that they hear you.

## Key points

- *Aunque* + indicative: a fact you assert. *Aunque* + subjunctive: a possibility (*even if*) or a
  known fact you wave away. Imperfect subjunctive: an unlikely case.
- *A pesar de* + noun / infinitive; *a pesar de que* and *por mucho que* + a clause (either mood);
  *aun así* = even so.
- Cause: *ya que, puesto que, dado que* + indicative; *debido a, a causa de* + noun.
- Consequence: *por lo tanto, por consiguiente* (formal); *de modo que* + indicative = so, +
  subjunctive = so that; *de ahí que* + subjunctive (recognize it).
- *Provocar* = to cause; *la consecuencia*; *el cambio climático, el calentamiento global, la
  sequía, las emisiones, la energía renovable, una especie en peligro de extinción*.

lessons.title: As long as you pay on time: conditions beyond si
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

In lesson 14 you built conditions with *si*: *Si pagas a tiempo, no hay problema; Si tuviera
dinero, compraría una casa.* Contracts, banks and careful speakers also use other **[[connectors]]**
of condition: "as long as", "provided that", "unless", "in case". Most of them take the
subjunctive, because the condition hasn't happened yet. The theme is money: budgets, debt,
credit cards and renting. (A2's lesson 19 covered banks and ATMs; this lesson goes further.)

## Four conjunctions that always take the subjunctive

| Conjunction | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *con tal de que* (also *con tal que*) | provided that, so long as |
| *a menos que* | unless |
| *en caso de que* | in case, if (it happens) |
| *salvo que* (formal) | unless |

- *Te presto el dinero con tal de que me lo devuelvas en la quincena.* — I'll lend you the money
  provided that you pay me back on payday.
- *No firmes a menos que entiendas todas las cláusulas.* — Don't sign unless you understand all
  the clauses.
- *En caso de que pierdas la tarjeta, llama al banco.* — If you lose your card, call the bank.
- *El precio no cambia, salvo que el contrato diga otra cosa.* — The price doesn't change, unless
  the contract says otherwise.

*A no ser que* means the same as *a menos que*; you'll meet it in writing. *Salvo* on its own
means "except" (*todos salvo yo*).

There is no indicative option after these four when they set a condition: ~~*a menos que
entiendes*~~ is a mistake. Like *si*, they never take the conditional or the future either.

## *Siempre que* and *mientras*: the mood changes the meaning

*Siempre que* is literally "always that". With the indicative it describes a habit: "whenever".
With the subjunctive it sets a condition: "as long as".

- *Siempre que voy al banco, hay una fila enorme.* — Whenever I go to the bank, there's a huge
  line. (habit: indicative)
- *Puedes usar mi tarjeta siempre que me avises.* — You can use my card as long as you tell me.
  (condition: subjunctive)

With the subjunctive, *siempre que* can also mean "whenever" about the future (*Siempre que
vengas, trae pan* — Whenever you come, bring bread); context tells you which. *Siempre y cuando*
(as long as) has only the condition meaning and always takes the subjunctive: *Te lo vendo a
plazos, siempre y cuando tengas un trabajo fijo* (a steady job).

*Mientras* (while, lesson 07) works the same way. With the indicative it means "while"; with the
subjunctive it can mean "as long as" (or, about the future, simply "while", as in lesson 07):

- *Mientras pagues a tiempo, no hay problema.* — As long as you pay on time, there's no problem.
- *Mientras yo pagaba, mi hermano esperaba en el carro.* — While I was paying, my brother waited
  in the car.

![A chart of conjunctions of condition. Left box, headed Siempre subjuntivo (always subjunctive): con tal de que, a menos que, a no ser que, en caso de que, salvo que, siempre y cuando. Right box, headed El modo cambia el sentido (the mood changes the meaning): siempre que plus indicative means whenever, plus subjunctive means as long as; mientras plus indicative means while, plus subjunctive means as long as. Bottom box, headed Igual que si: nunca presente de subjuntivo (like si: never the present subjunctive): si, excepto si, solo si, incluso si plus indicative, with the example Solo te cobran si pagas tarde.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Same subject: *con tal de* and *en caso de*

When there's no new subject, drop *que* and use an infinitive or a noun, as with *para / para que*
(lesson 06):

- *Haría cualquier cosa con tal de no pagar intereses.* — I'd do anything not to pay interest.
- *En caso de emergencia, rompa el vidrio.* — In case of emergency, break the glass.
- *En caso de no poder pagar, avísenos antes de la fecha límite.* — If you can't pay, let us know
  before the deadline. (*la fecha límite*, lesson 15)

## Conditions in the past

After a past or conditional main verb, these conjunctions take the imperfect subjunctive (lesson
15's sequence of tenses):

- *El banco me dio el préstamo con tal de que tuviera un aval.* — The bank gave me the loan
  provided that I had a guarantor. (*el aval* = guarantor, co-signer)
- *Mi papá me dijo que me prestaría el carro siempre que se lo devolviera limpio.* — My dad said
  he'd lend me the car as long as I gave it back clean.

## *Si* stays *si*

*Excepto si* (except if), *solo si* (only if) and *incluso si* (even if) are built on *si*, so they
follow its rules: the indicative, or the imperfect subjunctive for an unlikely case, but never the
present subjunctive.

- *Solo te cobran comisión si sacas dinero en otro banco.* — They only charge you a fee if you
  take money out at another bank.
- *No uses la tarjeta de crédito, excepto si es una emergencia.*

Compare *a menos que sea una emergencia* (subjunctive) with *excepto si es una emergencia*
(indicative): same meaning, different grammar.

## Money words

Your *ingresos* (income) come in, your *gastos* (expenses) go out, and what's left is *el ahorro*
(saving; *mis ahorros* = my savings). In Mexico many people are paid by *la quincena*, a period of
fifteen days: payday falls around the 15th and the last day of the month. The Ley Federal del
Trabajo (art. 88) allows pay periods of up to a week for manual work and up to fifteen days for
other workers, so the quincena is common, but not universal: many people are paid weekly.

- *gastar* (to spend money): *Gasté toda la quincena en el súper.* (*el súper* = supermarket)
- *la deuda* (debt) and *endeudarse* (to get into debt): *Se endeudó con tres tarjetas.*
- *la tarjeta de crédito*; *el interés* (interest, usually plural for money: *los intereses*). Many
  Mexican stores sell *a meses sin intereses*: you pay *a plazos* (in installments), one
  *mensualidad* (monthly payment) at a time, without interest, if you pay every *pago* on time.
- *el saldo* (balance): *¿Cuál es el saldo de mi cuenta?* In Mexico it's also your phone credit:
  *Se me acabó el saldo.*
- *el seguro* (insurance): *el seguro del carro, el seguro de vida.* (A2's *seguro* is the
  adjective "safe, sure".)
- *el riesgo* (risk) and *arriesgarse* (to take a risk; *me arriesgué*): *No me quiero arriesgar.*
- *la estafa* (scam): *Si te llaman para pedir tu NIP, es una estafa.* (*el NIP* = PIN, Mexico)
- *la economía* (economy; *la economía familiar* = household finances).

Who handles complaints? Most problems with stores and services go to Profeco (lesson 20). Problems
with banks and other regulated financial services usually go to Condusef, the national commission
for users of financial services.

## Reading a card statement

![A credit card statement from the invented Banco Horizonte, fecha de corte 15 de noviembre de 2026. Rows: Saldo al corte 17,450.00 MXN; Pago mínimo 845.00 MXN; Pago para no generar intereses 6,200.00 MXN; Fecha límite de pago 5 de diciembre de 2026; Intereses del periodo 312.40 MXN. Below, a box headed Compras a meses sin intereses: Laptop, comprada el 2 de agosto de 2026; Mensualidad 3 de 12, 1,250.00 MXN; Saldo pendiente después de este pago: 11,250.00 MXN.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

- *Saldo al corte* is the balance on the closing date (*la fecha de corte*).
- *Pago mínimo*: if you pay only this, you avoid a late fee but you pay interest on the rest.
- *Pago para no generar intereses*: the amount that avoids interest. On many statements it is
  smaller than the balance, because future installments of interest-free purchases aren't due yet.
- *Mensualidad 3 de 12*: the third of twelve monthly payments.

## Reading a contract

Rental contracts (*contratos de arrendamiento*) are full of conditions. Here are four invented
clauses:

> *Cláusula tercera.* El inquilino pagará la renta dentro de los primeros cinco días de cada mes. En caso de
> que se retrase, pagará un recargo del 5 %.
>
> *Cláusula cuarta.* El inquilino podrá tener mascotas siempre y cuando no causen daños.
>
> *Cláusula quinta.* El propietario devolverá el depósito al final del contrato, a menos que haya
> rentas pendientes.
>
> *Cláusula sexta.* El contrato se renovará por un año más, salvo que alguna de las partes avise
> por escrito con treinta días de anticipación.

> *Clause three.* The tenant will pay the rent within the first five days of each month. If he or
> she is late, he or she will pay a 5 % surcharge.
>
> *Clause four.* The tenant may keep pets as long as they don't cause damage.
>
> *Clause five.* The landlord will return the deposit at the end of the contract, unless rent is
> owed.
>
> *Clause six.* The contract will be renewed for one more year, unless either party gives
> written notice thirty days in advance.

*Renovar* = to renew (*renuevo*; *la renovación*); *retrasarse* = to be late; *el recargo* = surcharge; *pendiente* = outstanding; *las partes* = the
parties; *por escrito* = in writing; *con anticipación* = in advance. Contracts use the future
(*pagará, podrá*) for obligations, and every condition is in the subjunctive. Always read *las
condiciones* (the terms) before you sign.

## Dialogue: renewing the lease

Mariana rents an apartment in Guadalajara. She calls the landlord, señor Ochoa.

> Mariana: Buenas tardes, señor Ochoa. Lo llamo por la renovación del contrato.
>
> Sr. Ochoa: Ah, sí. Mire, se lo renuevo con gusto, siempre que acepte un aumento de quinientos pesos.
>
> Mariana: ¿Quinientos? Es mucho. Lo acepto con tal de que arregle la regadera, que gotea desde agosto.
>
> Sr. Ochoa: Está bien, mando al plomero esta semana, a menos que usted prefiera llamar al suyo.
>
> Mariana: No, mejor el suyo. Otra cosa: ¿puedo pagar por transferencia? Mi quincena llega el día quince.
>
> Sr. Ochoa: Mientras pague antes del día cinco, no hay problema. Si se retrasa, ya sabe que hay recargo.
>
> Mariana: Entendido. Y en caso de que me transfieran a otra ciudad, ¿puedo terminar el contrato antes?
>
> Sr. Ochoa: Sí, siempre y cuando me avise con un mes de anticipación.
>
> Mariana: Perfecto. Entonces mándeme el contrato y lo firmo.

> Mariana: Good afternoon, Mr. Ochoa. I'm calling about renewing the lease.
>
> Mr. Ochoa: Ah, yes. Look, I'm happy to renew it, as long as you accept a five-hundred-peso increase.
>
> Mariana: Five hundred? That's a lot. I'll accept it provided that you fix the shower, which has been dripping since August.
>
> Mr. Ochoa: All right, I'll send the plumber this week, unless you'd rather call your own.
>
> Mariana: No, yours is better. One more thing: can I pay by transfer? My pay comes on the fifteenth.
>
> Mr. Ochoa: As long as you pay before the fifth, there's no problem. If you're late, you know there's a surcharge.
>
> Mariana: Understood. And in case they transfer me to another city, can I end the contract early?
>
> Mr. Ochoa: Yes, as long as you give me a month's notice.
>
> Mariana: Perfect. Then send me the contract and I'll sign it.

*Gotear* = to drip.
Mariana's pay arrives on the 15th but rent is due by the 5th: she'll pay with the end-of-month
quincena.

## Pronunciation

- *Cláusula* is stressed on the first syllable: *CLÁU-su-la* (an *esdrújula*, so it needs the accent).
- *Intereses*: four syllables, *in-te-RE-ses*; the singular *interés* stresses the last.
- *Endeudarse*: *eu* is one syllable: *en-deu-DAR-se*.
- *Quincena*: *qu* is a *k* sound and *ce* is *se*: *kin-SE-na*.

## Common mistakes

- ~~*a menos que entiendes*~~ → *a menos que entiendas*. These conjunctions take the subjunctive.
- ~~*Si pagues a tiempo…*~~ → *Si pagas a tiempo* or *Siempre que pagues a tiempo*. *Si* never takes
  the present subjunctive.
- Reading every *siempre que* as "always". *Siempre que* + subjunctive is usually "as long as".
- ~~*en caso de que emergencia*~~ → *en caso de emergencia* (noun) or *en caso de que haya una
  emergencia* (clause).
- *Gastar* is for money (and for fuel or electricity: lesson 17's *gasta mucha luz*); for spending
  time somewhere, use *pasar*: *Pasé el fin de semana en casa*, not ~~*Gasté el fin de semana en casa*~~.

## Key points

- Always subjunctive: *con tal de que, a menos que, a no ser que, en caso de que, salvo que, siempre
  y cuando*.
- *Siempre que, mientras*: + indicative = whenever / while; + subjunctive = as long as.
- Same subject: *con tal de* + infinitive; *en caso de* + noun or infinitive.
- *Excepto si, solo si, incluso si* follow *si*: indicative, never present subjunctive.
- After a past verb: *con tal de que tuviera, siempre que se lo devolviera*.
- Money: *el ingreso, el gasto, el ahorro, la deuda, el interés, la mensualidad, a plazos, el saldo,
  la quincena, el seguro, el riesgo, la estafa*.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Firstly…: organizing an argument and an opinion text
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

An opinion is more convincing when the reader can follow it: first this, then that, on the
other hand, so in the end. In A2 you gave simple opinions (*creo que, en mi opinión*) and in
lesson 04 you learned that *no creo que* takes the subjunctive. Lesson 17 added the connectors of
cause, consequence and concession. Now you'll put them together into a forum post and a short
opinion composition, two kinds of text the DELE B1 writing test can ask for (lessons 23 and 24
return to the exam). The theme is life online: social media, privacy, artificial intelligence
and fake news.

## Discourse markers

**[[Discourse markers]]** are words and phrases that organize a text: they tell the reader where an
argument starts, when a new point comes, when you turn to the other side and when you conclude.
They are a kind of connector, but they usually stand at the start of a sentence or a paragraph,
followed by a comma.

| Job | Markers |
|---|---|
| Begin | *para empezar, en primer lugar* (then *en segundo lugar, en tercer lugar*) |
| Add a point | *además, asimismo* (likewise; formal), *también* |
| Two sides | *por un lado… por otro (lado)…* |
| Contrast | *sin embargo, no obstante* (nevertheless; formal), *en cambio* (whereas) |
| Conclude | *en conclusión, en resumen* (to sum up), *en definitiva* (ultimately), *para terminar* |

- *Por un lado, las redes sociales nos conectan con la familia; por otro, nos roban tiempo.* — On
  the one hand, social media connects us with family; on the other, it steals our time.
- *Mi hermano publica todo; yo, en cambio, cuido mucho mi privacidad.* — My brother posts
  everything, whereas I'm very careful about my privacy.
- *La app es gratis. No obstante, usa nuestros datos para la publicidad.* — The app is free.
  Nevertheless, it uses our data for advertising.

*Sin embargo* and *no obstante* mean the same; *no obstante* sounds more formal. *En cambio* sets two
things side by side (my brother… I…), so it often comes after the second subject, between commas.

## Stating your position

- *Desde mi punto de vista,…* — From my point of view,…
- *A mi juicio,…* — In my judgment,… (formal, written)
- *En mi opinión,… / Para mí,…* (A2)
- *Estoy a favor de… / Estoy en contra de…* — I'm in favor of… / I'm against…

*A favor de* and *en contra de* take a noun, an infinitive, or *que* + subjunctive (a different
subject):

- *Estoy a favor de la nueva ley.* (noun)
- *Estoy en contra de prohibir los videojuegos.* (infinitive: same subject or general)
- *Estoy en contra de que los niños tengan redes sociales.* (que + subjunctive)

Your opinion is *tu postura* (your position, your stance), and you *defiendes* it (*defender*: *e →
ie*, like *entender*: *defiendo, defiendes*; subjunctive *defienda*) with *argumentos* (reasons).
*El argumento* is a reason or a point, not a quarrel (*una discusión*, lesson 16). A topic that
divides people is *una polémica* (a controversy).

## Certainty or judgment: which mood?

This is where B1 opinions often go wrong. Two families of expressions look alike in English but
take different moods.

Certainty takes the indicative: you state a fact.

- *Es verdad que / Es cierto que / Es evidente que / Está claro que las redes son adictivas.*
- *Me parece que tienes razón.* — I think you're right.

Denying certainty and judging take the subjunctive:

- *No es verdad que todos los jóvenes sean adictos.* — It isn't true that all young people are
  addicts. (Denial, lesson 04.)
- *Me parece bien / mal / injusto / lógico / normal que limiten el tiempo de pantalla.* — I think
  it's good / bad / unfair / logical / normal for them to limit screen time.
- *Es importante / necesario / mejor que aprendamos a detectar noticias falsas* (lesson 02).

Watch the pair: *me parece que* + indicative gives an opinion about what is true (*Me parece que
llueve*, I think it's raining), while *me parece* + an adjective + *que* takes the subjunctive
because it judges something (*Me parece injusto que llueva hoy*).

![Two boxes. The top box, headed Indicativo: afirma un hecho (indicative: states a fact), lists es verdad que, es cierto que, es evidente que, está claro que, me parece que, with the example Es evidente que las redes distraen. The bottom box, headed Subjuntivo: niega o juzga (subjunctive: denies or judges), lists no es verdad que, no creo que, es importante que, me parece bien, mal, injusto, lógico or normal que, with the example Me parece injusto que prohíban todo.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Hedging: not too sure

A careful writer doesn't present everything as certain:

- *Parece que* + indicative: *Parece que el video se hizo viral por un error.* — It seems the
  video went viral by mistake.
- *Es posible que / Puede que* + subjunctive (lesson 04): *Es posible que la inteligencia
  artificial cambie muchos trabajos.*
- *Al parecer* (lesson 16) + indicative: *Al parecer, la noticia era falsa.*

## The shape of an opinion text

![An opinion text drawn as three blocks joined by arrows. Introducción: Presenta el tema y tu postura (desde mi punto de vista, en mi opinión). Argumentos: Primer punto, segundo punto, el otro lado (en primer lugar, además, asimismo; por un lado, por otro, no obstante). Conclusión: Resume y repite tu postura (en conclusión, en resumen, en definitiva).](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Before you write, list the pros and cons. Weighing both sides, even if you choose one, is what
makes a text an argument rather than a list of complaints.

![A balance scale with two pans. Left pan, headed Ventajas: información rápida, contacto con la familia, aprender en línea. Right pan, headed Desventajas: adicción, ciberacoso, noticias falsas, menos privacidad. Under the scale, the question ¿Celulares en la escuela?](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Model 1: a forum post (112 words)

A parents' forum asks: *¿A qué edad deben tener redes sociales los niños?*

> Hola a todos. Les cuento mi experiencia. El año pasado mi hija de doce años quería una cuenta en
> una red social, ya que todas sus amigas tenían una. Por un lado, entiendo que quiera estar con
> sus amigas; por otro, me preocupaba su privacidad y el ciberacoso. Al final, llegamos a un
> acuerdo: puede usarla, siempre que la cuenta sea privada y no acepte seguidores que no conozca.
> Revisamos juntas la configuración y le expliqué qué no debe publicar nunca. No es verdad que los
> padres siempre exageremos: hay riesgos reales. Aun así, me parece injusto que prohibamos todo.
> En resumen, mi consejo es hablar mucho con ellos. ¿Ustedes qué opinan?

> Hi, everyone. Let me tell you about my experience. Last year my twelve-year-old daughter wanted
> an account on a social network, since all her friends had one. On the one hand, I understand
> that she wants to be with her friends; on the other, I was worried about her privacy and
> cyberbullying. In the end, we reached an agreement: she can use it, as long as the account is
> private and she doesn't accept followers she doesn't know. We went through the settings together
> and I explained what she must never post. It isn't true that we parents always exaggerate: there
> are real risks. Even so, I think it's unfair for us to ban everything. To sum up, my advice is to
> talk with them a lot. What do you all think?

*Llegar a un acuerdo* = to reach an agreement; *la configuración* = settings. *Entiendo que quiera*:
after *entender que*, the subjunctive accepts the other person's point (I understand her wanting
to); with the indicative it would just report information. The writer tells a short experience,
weighs both sides, gives a condition (lesson 18) and ends with a question to the forum, as such
posts usually do.

## Model 2: an opinion composition (143 words)

> ¿Deberían las escuelas prohibir los celulares?
>
> En los últimos años, la polémica sobre los celulares en las escuelas ha crecido mucho. Desde mi
> punto de vista, lo mejor es limitarlos, pero no prohibirlos del todo.
>
> En primer lugar, es evidente que el celular distrae a los alumnos. Por ejemplo, en mi escuela
> algunos estudiantes revisan sus redes cada cinco minutos. Además, varios estudios hablan de
> adicción a las pantallas. Por lo tanto, me parece lógico que no se usen durante las clases.
>
> No obstante, el celular también tiene ventajas. Muchos alumnos lo usan para buscar información o
> para avisar a su familia. Asimismo, es necesario que aprendan a detectar noticias falsas, y para
> eso necesitan practicar.
>
> En definitiva, no creo que la solución sea prohibir. A mi juicio, las escuelas deberían enseñar
> a usar la tecnología con responsabilidad, ya que los jóvenes la van a usar toda su vida.

> Should schools ban cell phones?
>
> In recent years, the controversy over cell phones in schools has grown a lot. From my point of
> view, the best thing is to limit them, but not to ban them completely.
>
> First of all, it's obvious that cell phones distract students. For example, at my school some
> students check their social media every five minutes. Moreover, several studies talk about
> screen addiction. Therefore, I think it makes sense for them not to be used during class.
>
> Nevertheless, cell phones also have advantages. Many students use them to look up information or
> to let their family know something. Likewise, it's necessary for them to learn to spot fake news,
> and for that they need practice.
>
> Ultimately, I don't think the solution is to ban them. In my judgment, schools should teach
> students to use technology responsibly, since young people are going to use it all their lives.

(The word count leaves out the title.) Four paragraphs: position, arguments for, the other side,
conclusion. Notice the moods: *es evidente que distrae* (fact, indicative), *me parece lógico que
no se usen, es necesario que aprendan, no creo que sea* (judgment and denial, subjunctive).

## More words for life online

- *el seguidor / la seguidora* (follower): *Tiene medio millón de seguidores.*
- *viral* (same for both genders): *hacerse viral* = to go viral.
- *las noticias falsas* (fake news; usually plural; you'll also hear *las fake news*).
- *la inteligencia artificial, la IA*: *La IA puede escribir textos, pero también inventa datos.*
- *el ciberacoso* (cyberbullying) and *la libertad de expresión* (freedom of speech): *La libertad
  de expresión no protege el ciberacoso.*
- *la privacidad* (privacy; also *la intimidad*, private life); *la adicción*.
- *la ventaja / la desventaja*: advantage / disadvantage.

## Pronunciation

- *Asimismo* is one word, stressed *a-si-MIS-mo*. (*Así mismo*, two words, also exists, but in
  texts the one-word form is the usual connector.)
- *No obstante*: *no-obs-TAN-te*; in fast speech the two *o* sounds blend into one.
- *Ciberacoso*: *ci-be-ra-CO-so*; *ci* is *si*.
- *Polémica* is an *esdrújula*: *po-LÉ-mi-ca*.

## Common mistakes

- ~~*Es verdad que sean adictivas*~~ → *Es verdad que son adictivas.* Certainty takes the indicative.
- ~~*Me parece injusto que prohíben todo*~~ → *que prohíban.* A judgment takes the subjunctive.
- ~~*Estoy a favor que…*~~ → *Estoy a favor de que…*: keep the *de*.
- Using *argumento* for a quarrel: *Tuvimos una discusión*, not ~~*un argumento*~~.

## Key points

- Discourse markers organize a text: *en primer lugar, además, asimismo, por un lado / por otro, sin
  embargo, no obstante, en cambio, en conclusión, en resumen, en definitiva*.
- Position: *desde mi punto de vista, a mi juicio, estoy a favor de / en contra de* (+ noun,
  infinitive, *que* + subjunctive).
- Certainty + indicative (*es verdad / evidente que, me parece que*); denial and judgment +
  subjunctive (*no es verdad que, me parece bien / injusto / lógico que, es necesario que*).
- Hedging: *parece que, al parecer* + indicative; *es posible que, puede que* + subjunctive.
- Forum post: experience, both sides, your view, a question. Composition: introduction,
  arguments, the other side, conclusion.

lessons.title: Estimados señores: register, formal letters and complaints
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

The same request can be a text to a friend or a letter to a company. In A1 you learned *Estimado
señor* and *Atentamente*; in A2, polite requests with the conditional (*¿Podría…?*). Lesson 13 gave
you *quisiera*, and lesson 15 the imperfect subjunctive after a past or conditional verb (*Me
gustaría que me llamaras*). This lesson puts it all to work in the most practical formal text you
may ever write in Spanish: a complaint. Along the way you'll see how Mexicans choose between *tú*
and *usted*, and what Profeco is.

## Register

**[[Register]]** is the level of formality you choose for a situation: the pronoun (*tú / usted*), the
verb forms, the words (*¿Qué onda?* vs *Buenas tardes*), and in writing, the greeting and the
closing. The noun is *el registro* (it also means registration or a record). The skill is to pick
one register and keep it all the way through.

### *Tú, usted* and *ustedes* in Mexico

- *Ustedes* is the only plural "you", for friends and strangers alike (*vosotros* is Spain's).
- *Tú* is usual with friends, family, children and people your age, and increasingly among
  colleagues, especially young ones.
- *Usted* is usual with older people you don't know well, with customers and staff in shops and
  offices, with officials, and often with a boss. In some families, *usted* is used even with
  parents or grandparents.

When in doubt, start with *usted* and let the other person offer *tú*: *Háblame de tú* (A1's
*tutear*: *¿Nos tuteamos?*). Switching from *usted* to *tú* without an invitation can sound rude;
staying with *usted* after an invitation can sound cold.

### Courtesy in speech

A1 and A2 gave you some Mexican chunks; here is what they do:

- *¿Mande?* — Pardon? / Yes? Said when you didn't catch something or when someone calls your name.
  It's polite in Mexico; a bare *¿Qué?* can sound abrupt.
- *Con permiso* — said when you pass in front of someone or leave a room. The answer is often
  *Propio* (A1) or *Adelante* (go ahead).
- *¡Provecho!* — said to people who are eating, even strangers in a small restaurant.
- *Disculpe / Perdone* to get attention; *Disculpe las molestias* — sorry for the inconvenience.

![A ladder of five steps from informal at the top to formal at the bottom. Step 1: ¡Oye! ¿Me pasas la sal? (amigos). Step 2: Disculpa, ¿me pasas la sal? (tú, cortés). Step 3: Disculpe, ¿me pasa la sal? (usted). Step 4: Perdone la molestia, ¿podría decirme dónde está la caja? (usted, muy cortés). Step 5: Me dirijo a ustedes para solicitar información… (carta formal).](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

(*La caja* on step 4 is the checkout.) *La cortesía* is courtesy; its opposite, at its worst, is *una falta de respeto* (disrespect). *El
trato* is the way people treat you: *El trato fue excelente.*

## Softening a request

Each step down this list is softer:

- *Quiero hablar con el encargado.* — I want to speak to the person in charge. (direct)
- *Quisiera hablar con el encargado.* — I'd like to… (lesson 13)
- *¿Podría comunicarme con el encargado?* — Could you put me through to…? (A2)
- *Me gustaría que me comunicara con el encargado.* — I'd like you to put me through… (lesson 15)
- *Le agradecería que me comunicara con el encargado.* — I'd be grateful if you put me through…

*Le agradecería que* (I would be grateful if) is the key formula of formal Spanish. *Agradecería*
is a conditional, so the verb after *que* is traditionally in the imperfect subjunctive, just as
in lesson 15:
*Le agradecería que me enviara la factura. Les agradeceríamos que nos respondieran pronto.* The
future (*Le agradeceré que me envíe*) is also correct and sounds more insistent. Many Latin
Americans also say, and write, *Le agradecería que me envíe* with the present subjunctive; it is
not a mistake, but in a formal letter the imperfect subjunctive is the safest choice. The *-se* forms (*que me enviase*) are correct too, but rarer in
Mexico.

*¿Sería posible que…?* (Would it be possible for…?) works the same way: *¿Sería posible que me
cambiaran la cita?*

## Formal written Spanish: the formulas

| Part | Formulas |
|---|---|
| Greeting | *Estimado señor Ruiz: / Estimada licenciada Paz: / Estimados señores:* / *A quien corresponda:* (to whom it may concern) |
| Purpose | *Me dirijo a usted(es) para…* (I am writing to…) / *Por medio de la presente…* (I hereby…; *la presente* = this letter) |
| Request | *Le(s) agradecería que* + imperfect subjunctive / *Le(s) solicito que* + present subjunctive / *¿Sería posible que…?* |
| Deadline | *a la mayor brevedad* (as soon as possible) / *en un plazo de diez días hábiles* (within ten business days) |
| Attachments | *Adjunto la factura. / Le envío como archivo adjunto…* |
| Closing | *Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.* (I await your reply.) / *Sin otro particular, reciba un cordial saludo.* / *Atentamente,* |

Formal letters in Spanish put a colon, not a comma, after the greeting: *Estimados señores:*. *Sin
otro particular* means "with nothing further to add", a common closing line in Mexican formal letters.

In an e-mail, *el remitente* is the sender, *el destinatario* the recipient, *el asunto* (A1) the
subject line and *el archivo adjunto* the attachment.

![A formal e-mail with its parts labeled. De: mariana.leon@correo.example is labeled el remitente; Para: atencion@casa-aurora.example is labeled el destinatario; Asunto: Reclamación por licuadora defectuosa, pedido 58213 is labeled el asunto; a paperclip with the file factura-58213.pdf is labeled el archivo adjunto. The body begins Estimados señores: Me dirijo a ustedes para presentar una reclamación, and ends Quedo a la espera de su respuesta. Atentamente, followed by the name Mariana León Ruiz, labeled la firma.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## One problem, two messages

Mariana bought a blender online, and it doesn't work. First she writes to her friend Sofía:

> ¡Hola, Sofi! ¿Qué crees? La licuadora que compré en línea salió defectuosa: hace un ruidazo y se
> apaga. Los llamé y me dijeron que me iban a contactar, pero nada. Ya me harté, así que les voy a
> mandar un correo bien formal. Si no me hacen caso, me voy a quejar con la Profeco. ¿Me ayudas a
> revisarlo antes de mandarlo?

> Hi, Sofi! Guess what? The blender I bought online turned out to be faulty: it makes a terrible
> noise and switches off. I called them and they said they'd get in touch, but nothing. I've had
> enough, so I'm going to send them a really formal e-mail. If they don't listen to me, I'm going to
> complain to Profeco. Will you help me check it before I send it?

Then she writes to the store:

> Asunto: Reclamación por licuadora defectuosa, pedido 58213
>
> Estimados señores:
>
> Me dirijo a ustedes para presentar una reclamación por una licuadora que compré en su tienda en
> línea el 3 de octubre de 2026 (pedido núm. 58213).
>
> El aparato llegó el 6 de octubre y, desde el primer día, el motor hace un ruido muy fuerte y se
> apaga a los pocos segundos. El 9 de octubre llamé a su servicio de atención a clientes y me
> dijeron que alguien se comunicaría conmigo en 48 horas. Sin embargo, hasta la fecha nadie lo ha
> hecho.
>
> Puesto que el producto está en garantía, les agradecería que me lo cambiaran por uno nuevo o que
> me devolvieran el importe total. Adjunto la factura y un video del problema.
>
> Les pido que me respondan a la mayor brevedad, en un plazo máximo de diez días hábiles. En caso de
> no recibir respuesta, presentaré una queja ante la Profeco.
>
> Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.
>
> Atentamente,
>
> Mariana León Ruiz

> Subject: Complaint about a faulty blender, order 58213
>
> Dear Sir or Madam:
>
> I am writing to file a complaint about a blender I bought in your online store on 3 October 2026
> (order no. 58213).
>
> The appliance arrived on 6 October and, from the first day, the motor has made a very loud noise
> and switches off after a few seconds. On 9 October I called your customer service and was told
> that someone would contact me within 48 hours. However, to date nobody has done so.
>
> Since the product is under warranty, I would be grateful if you would replace it with a new one
> or refund the full amount. I attach the invoice and a video of the problem.
>
> I ask you to reply as soon as possible, within ten business days at most. If I receive no reply,
> I will file a complaint with Profeco.
>
> I await your reply.
>
> Sincerely,
>
> Mariana León Ruiz

*El ruidazo* = a huge noise (*-azo* makes it big); *ya me harté* = I've had enough (*hartarse*,
lesson 03's *harto*); *el importe* = the amount; *hasta la fecha* = to date; *los días hábiles* =
business days. Compare the moves: the message to Sofía uses *tú*, informal words (*¿Qué crees?, bien formal*) and
feelings; the e-mail gives facts with dates (preterite, present and perfect), the request (*les
agradecería que* + imperfect subjunctive), a deadline and the next step, with no feelings at all.
It never insults anyone: a calm complaint gets results more often than an angry one.

A complaint to a company is *una reclamación* (in much of Latin America also *un reclamo*); to
Profeco you *presentas una queja* (A2), which is Profeco's own word. *Presentar* here means to
submit or file (also to present, to introduce).

## Profeco and your rights (checked November 2026)

*La Procuraduría Federal del Consumidor* (Profeco) is the federal agency that protects consumers
in Mexico. The first Ley Federal de Protección al Consumidor (published 22 December 1975, in force
from 5 February 1976) created it; the law in force today dates from 1992 and has been reformed
many times since.

- Its services, including advice and conciliation (a meeting to reach an agreement with the
  business), are free. You can call the *Teléfono del Consumidor* (55 5568 8722 in Mexico City,
  800 468 8722 from the rest of the country), visit an office, or use *Concilianet* online when
  the business is registered on it.
- To file a complaint you usually need proof of the purchase (*el ticket, la factura* or the contract) and an official ID.
- By law (art. 77), a warranty (*la garantía*) may not be shorter than ninety days from delivery.
- In some cases, for example a product that doesn't match the quality or specifications offered,
  or a repair under warranty that leaves it unusable, the consumer may choose a replacement or a
  refund, and also receives a *bonificación* (compensation) of at least 20 % of the price (arts.
  92 and 92 TER).

Phone numbers and procedures change: check Profeco's current page before you rely on them. Other
words: *el consumidor / la consumidora*, *el derecho* (a legal right: *tener derecho a* = to have
the right to), *el daño* (damage), *la compensación*, *satisfecho / insatisfecho*.

### Other formal documents

A school or employer may give you *una constancia*: an official paper that proves a fact (*una
constancia de estudios*, proof of enrollment; *una constancia de trabajo*). *Un certificado*
certifies a result (*el certificado de bachillerato*). An official case has *un expediente* (a case
file), and a formal *petición* (request) usually starts with *Por medio de la presente, solicito…*.

## Pronunciation

- *Reclamación*: four syllables, *re-cla-ma-CIÓN*; the plural *reclamaciones* loses the accent.
- *Expediente*: *ex* is *eks*: *eks-pe-DIEN-te*.
- *Agradecería*: the stress is on *-rí-*: *a-gra-de-se-RÍ-a*.
- *Profeco* is said as a word, *pro-FE-co*, usually with *la*: *la Profeco*.

## Common mistakes

- Not a mistake, but a choice: *Le agradecería que me envíe* is common in Latin America; in a
  formal letter the imperfect subjunctive after the conditional is the safest choice: *que me enviara*. (*Le
  agradeceré que me envíe*, with the future, is fine.)
- Mixing registers: *Estimados señores: … ¿Qué onda con mi licuadora?* Keep one register.
- ~~*Estimados señores,*~~ with a comma is an English habit; Spanish uses a colon.
- Switching to *tú* with an official or a shop clerk without being invited.
- Writing feelings instead of facts: *¡Su servicio es horrible!* is less effective than dates,
  order numbers and a clear request.

## Key points

- Register is the level of formality; keep one through a text. In Mexico: *ustedes* for every
  plural, *tú* with friends and peers, *usted* with strangers, customers, officials and elders.
- Courtesy: *¿Mande?, con permiso, ¡Provecho!, Disculpe las molestias.*
- Softening: *quisiera, ¿podría…?, me gustaría que…, le agradecería que* + imperfect subjunctive,
  *¿sería posible que…?*
- Formal letter: *Estimados señores: / A quien corresponda:*, *Me dirijo a ustedes para… / Por
  medio de la presente…*, facts with dates, request, deadline (*a la mayor brevedad*), *Quedo a la
  espera de su respuesta. Atentamente*.
- Profeco is free and handles consumer complaints (*presentar una queja*); a warranty lasts at
  least ninety days.
