questions.stem: What does "Es difícil que gane el partido" mean?
choices: Winning the game is hard work for her.
She will definitely win the game.
She probably won't win the game.
She doesn't want to win the game.
questions.explanation: Es difícil que + subjunctive usually means "it's unlikely that". For "it's hard to do", Spanish uses the infinitive: Es difícil ganar.

questions.stem: Complete: "Dudo que los fantasmas ___." (existir)
questions.explanation: Dudar que takes the subjunctive: existan (-ir verb: e → a). Existen is indicative.

questions.stem: Which expression is followed by the indicative?
questions.explanation: Es evidente que presents something as a fact: indicative (Es evidente que hay muchas estrellas). Possibility, probability and negated opinions take the subjunctive.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, who was the first Mexican in space, and when?
questions.explanation: Rodolfo Neri Vela flew on the space shuttle Atlantis from November 26 to December 3, 1985. Katya Echazarreta became the first Mexican-born woman in space on June 4, 2022.

questions.stem: In Mexico and several other Spanish-speaking countries, which day is traditionally unlucky?
questions.explanation: The traditional unlucky day is martes 13, Tuesday the 13th: "En martes 13, ni te cases ni te embarques" (don't get married or set sail).

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Estoy seguro de que tenga razón.
questions.explanation: Es posible que takes the subjunctive; quizás takes either mood. A lo mejor takes only the indicative (a lo mejor tiene), and estoy seguro de que expresses certainty, so it takes the indicative (tiene).

questions.stem: Write the present subjunctive of llover: "Puede que ___ esta noche."
questions.explanation: Puede que always takes the subjunctive. llover → llueve → llueva (o → ue, like volver).

questions.stem: Which mood follows each expression?
questions.explanation: Certainty (es evidente que) and a lo mejor take the indicative; doubt (dudo que) and possibility (puede que) take the subjunctive; quizás and tal vez take either.

questions.stem: Put these from the most certain to the least certain.
questions.explanation: Evident (certain) → probable (likely) → improbable (unlikely) → impossible. Only the first takes the indicative.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I don't think it's true.
questions.explanation: No creo que + subjunctive: sea. Creo que es verdad (without no) takes the indicative.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: There may be life on other planets. (Use "es posible".)
questions.explanation: Es posible que + subjunctive: hay → haya. The place can come before the verb (Es posible que en otros planetas haya vida) or open the sentence (En otros planetas es posible que haya vida), and the que clause can come first (Que haya vida en otros planetas es posible).

questions.stem: Your friend is leaving for a party. What do you say?
questions.explanation: ¡Que te diviertas! = Have fun! Que en paz descanse is only for someone who has died; ¡Que aproveche! is for people eating; ¡Que te mejores! is for someone who is ill.

questions.stem: You're leaving doña Lupe's house at night. You call her usted. What do you say?
questions.explanation: For usted, use the third-person singular subjunctive: ¡Que descanse! Descanses is for tú, descansen for ustedes, and descansa is indicative.

questions.stem: In a Mexican restaurant, a stranger passing your table says "¡Provecho!" What does it mean?
questions.explanation: ¡Provecho! or ¡Buen provecho! = Enjoy your meal. In Mexico it is often said even to strangers; ¡Que aproveche! means the same and is the usual phrase in Spain (understood, but much less common, in Mexico).

questions.stem: What does "Pase lo que pase, te llamo mañana" mean?
choices: Come in, I'll call you tomorrow.
Whatever happens, I'll call you tomorrow.
If something happens, call me tomorrow.
What happened? I'll call you tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Pase lo que pase (a subjunctive repeated around lo que) = whatever happens, no matter what.

questions.stem: Complete: "Voy a terminar la carrera, ___ lo que ___."
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase repeats the same subjunctive: cueste lo que cueste (whatever it takes). Both verbs must be the same form.

questions.stem: Which phrase is used only for someone who has died?
questions.explanation: Que en paz descanse (may he / she rest in peace) follows the name of someone who has died. ¡Que descanses! is good night to a living person.

questions.stem: What does the lesson say about where "ojalá" comes from?
choices: It comes from Latin, through Old Spanish.
The RAE traces it to a Hispanic Arabic phrase meaning roughly "if God wills"; the exact source is debated.
It was borrowed from Nahuatl after the conquest.
It is a modern word from the twentieth century.
questions.explanation: The RAE's dictionary (2001 edition, as reported by the column Castellano actual) gives Hispanic Arabic law šá lláh, "if God wills"; other Arabic sources have been proposed, so the lesson labels the usual account and the debate.

questions.stem: Look at the two cards. Which form of address does the condolence card use?

image.alt: Two cards. Left, a wedding card: Queridos Ana y Rodrigo: ¡Muchas felicidades en este día tan especial! Les deseamos un matrimonio lleno de amor y armonía. Que sean muy felices y que la vida les dé muchos años juntos. Con cariño, familia Méndez. Right, a condolence card: Estimada señora Gutiérrez: Lamento profundamente el fallecimiento de su esposo, don Arturo. Fue un excelente vecino. Reciba mi más sentido pésame. Que en paz descanse. Atentamente, Julio Ramos.

questions.explanation: The condolence card says su esposo and Reciba (an usted command) to señora Gutiérrez: usted, the safe choice for an older person. The wedding card uses ustedes (Les deseamos, Que sean).

questions.stem: Which messages would suit an older neighbor whose husband has died? Select all that apply.
choices: Lamento mucho la pérdida de su esposo.
questions.explanation: Mi más sentido pésame, Lamento mucho la pérdida… and Mis condolencias are condolences (with usted where a verb is needed). ¡Que te diviertas! (have fun) and ¡Que cumplas muchos más! (a birthday wish) are for happy occasions.

questions.stem: Write the usted form of tener: "¡Que ___ buen día, señora!"
questions.explanation: Usted takes the third-person singular subjunctive: tenga (from tengo). To a friend: ¡Que tengas buen día!

questions.stem: Match each wish to the occasion.
questions.explanation: Many more birthdays; get well soon; be very happy (to a couple); my deepest condolences; have a good trip. For an interview you might say ¡Que te salga bien!

questions.stem: Put the parts of the lesson's get-well message in order.
choices: Lamento mucho lo de su operación.
Ojalá que se recupere muy pronto.
Todos en la oficina le mandamos un abrazo.
questions.explanation: Greeting, reaction, wish (ojalá + subjunctive), closing: the order of the worked example.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Whatever happens, I'll call you tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Pase lo que pase repeats the same subjunctive (not pasa). It can open or close the sentence or sit in the middle (Mañana, pase lo que pase, te llamo), and mañana can come before or after te llamo.

questions.stem: Complete: "¿Y si le ___ una carta?" (escribir, tú)
questions.explanation: ¿Y si…? (What if…?) is a si meaning "if", so it takes the present indicative: ¿Y si le escribes una carta? Si is never followed by the present subjunctive.

questions.stem: Which is the softest way to give the same advice?
choices: Te exijo que hables con él.
Te aconsejo que hables con él.
questions.explanation: A question (¿Y si hablas con él?) leaves the decision to the reader. Te aconsejo que is clear advice; tienes que and te exijo que are strong.

questions.stem: What does "Mi hermana es muy comprensiva" mean?
choices: My sister understands a lot of languages.
questions.explanation: Comprensivo is a false friend: understanding, sympathetic. "Comprehensive, thorough" is completo or integral; "sensitive" is sensible.

questions.stem: In Letter 1, why is Corazón roto unsure about getting back together with her ex?
choices: Her friends say he is a bad person.
She is afraid the same thing will happen again.
He is moving to another city.
questions.explanation: She writes: "Me da miedo que vuelva a pasar lo mismo" (I'm afraid the same thing will happen again), and also that she is afraid of being alone.

questions.stem: In the reply to Tímido en Mérida, what does the adviser suggest first?
choices: Asking his sister to speak for him in meetings.
Preparing one idea for the next meeting and saying it.
Not inviting anyone out for a while.
questions.explanation: "Te sugiero que empieces con pasos pequeños. ¿Y si en la próxima reunión preparas una sola idea y la dices?" The sister is suggested only as someone to practice with.

questions.stem: Complete: "Toma en cuenta ___ el museo cierra los lunes."
questions.explanation: Tomar en cuenta (very common in Mexico; tener en cuenta is the usual form in Spain) is followed directly by que: Toma en cuenta que… Adding de is a common error.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: No creo que sea buena idea.
Es importante que hablen con sinceridad.
Te sugiero de que empieces poco a poco.
questions.explanation: Advice, doubt and an impersonal expression all take the subjunctive (te desahogues, sea, hablen). ¿Y si…? takes the indicative (¿Y si le llamas?), and sugerir is followed directly by que (no de).

questions.stem: Write the present subjunctive of desahogarse for tú (two words): "Te aconsejo que ___ con alguien de confianza."
questions.explanation: Reflexive verbs keep their pronoun: te. The g of -gar becomes gu before e: desahogo → desahogues.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: el desamor = heartbreak; la autoestima = self-esteem; el rechazo = rejection; la timidez = shyness; desahogarse = to vent, let it all out. Success is A1's el éxito.

questions.stem: Put the parts of an advice-column reply in the order the lesson recommends.
choices: React to the feelings: Siento que…
Give your honest opinion: No creo que…
Close with a wish: Ojalá que…
questions.explanation: Greet, react, advise, give an opinion, then close with a wish and a sign-off, as in the diagram in Worked example 2.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I don't think you have to change who you are.
questions.explanation: No creo que + subjunctive: tengas que (tener que in the subjunctive). Tienes que is indicative.

questions.stem: How long is the reply in the DELE B1's first writing task?
questions.explanation: The first writing task is a letter, e-mail or post of 100–120 words answering a short text; the second is a composition of 130–150 words.

questions.stem: The columnist writes "No dudo que te extraña". What does the lesson say about the mood after "no dudo que"?
choices: The indicative is more usual, but the subjunctive is also heard.
questions.explanation: Not doubting is being sure, so no dudo que usually takes the indicative, as in the columnist's No dudo que te extraña; the subjunctive (No dudo que te extrañe) is also heard.

questions.stem: Using tú, tell your friend not to use her phone while she drives: "___ el celular mientras manejas."
questions.explanation: A negative tú command is no + the tú subjunctive: usar → que tú uses → "No uses". "No usas" is a statement (You don't use), "No usa" is "She doesn't use", and "No use" is the usted command, not tú.

questions.stem: What is the negative of "Dímelo" (tú: Tell me)?
questions.explanation: In a negative command the pronouns move in front of the verb, in the same order (me before lo), and the verb is the tú subjunctive: decir → digo → "digas". "No dímelo" keeps the affirmative form, "No me lo dices" is a statement, and "lo me" has the pronouns in the wrong order.

questions.stem: Complete with the negative tú command of cruzar (to cross): "No ___ la calle sin mirar."
questions.explanation: Negative tú command = no + the tú subjunctive. cruzar → cruzo → cruce-: the z changes to c before e, so "cruces". (Not "cruzes": Spanish writes ce, ci, not ze, zi.)

questions.stem: How do you say "Let's not park here"?
questions.explanation: A nosotros command is the nosotros subjunctive: estacionar → "estacionemos"; negative: "No estacionemos aquí." "No estacionamos aquí" is a statement (We don't park here). The subjunctive form has no written accent, and no goes before the verb.

questions.stem: You and your friends are ready to leave. Which is the correct way to say "Let's go!"?
questions.explanation: For "let's go" ir uses vamos, and with the pronoun nos the final -s drops: vamos + nos → "¡Vámonos!" (the accent keeps the stress on va-). "Vámosnos" keeps the -s; "Nos vámonos" and "Vamos nos" put the pronoun in the wrong place: in an affirmative command it is attached to the end.

questions.stem: Which of these command forms are present subjunctive forms? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Every command except the affirmative tú command is a subjunctive form: usted "frene", negative "no frenes", nosotros "frenemos". The affirmative tú command "frena" is the él form of the present.

questions.stem: Match each Mexican road sign to what it tells drivers.
questions.explanation: Signs use the usted command ("Ceda el paso", "Disminuya su velocidad": ceder = to give way, disminuir = to reduce) or an infinitive ("No estacionarse", "Prohibido rebasar"; rebasar = to pass another car).

questions.stem: This is the street from the lesson without its labels. Choose the word for each numbered part.

image.alt: A top-down drawing of a street with six numbered parts: 1 the monument island in the middle of a traffic circle; 2 one of the lanes of the road; 3 the gray strip along the top edge, next to the buildings; 4 the white stripes across the road; 5 a person walking across the stripes; 6 the green strip with a bicycle symbol between the sidewalk and the road.

questions.explanation: 1 la glorieta (traffic circle; Spain la rotonda), 2 el carril (lane), 3 la banqueta (sidewalk; elsewhere la acera), 4 el cruce (crosswalk), 5 el peatón (pedestrian), 6 la ciclovía (bike lane). La placa (license plate) and el volante (steering wheel) are parts of a car.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Don't get distracted while you drive. (tú)
questions.explanation: Negative tú command of distraerse: no + te + the subjunctive "distraigas" (distraigo → distraig- + -as). The pronoun te goes before the verb. "Mientras manejas" (indicative: a fact happening at the same time) can go first or last. "No te distraes" would be a statement.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Fasten your seat belts, please. (to a group: ustedes)
questions.explanation: Affirmative ustedes command of abrocharse (to fasten): "abrochen" + se, attached, with an accent to keep the stress: "abróchense". Spanish says "el cinturón" (each person fastens their own). "Por favor" can go first or last. "Abróchese" is for one person (usted).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Let's not park on the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: "Let's not…" = no + the nosotros subjunctive: "No estacionemos en la banqueta." "No estacionamos en la banqueta" would mean "We don't park on the sidewalk." (Banqueta is the Mexican word; elsewhere la acera.)

questions.stem: Your boss is driving you to a meeting, too fast for your liking. Which is the most polite way to ask him to slow down?
choices: ¿Podría ir un poco más despacio, por favor?
questions.explanation: A question with the conditional ("¿Podría…?") softens a request, and usted suits a boss. "¡No acelere!" is a correct usted command but sounds like an order; "¡Frena!" and "No aceleres tanto" are tú commands, too direct and too informal for a boss.

questions.stem: According to Mexico City's Reglamento de Tránsito (2019 text, as described in the lesson), what is the default speed limit in a school zone?
questions.explanation: Where no sign says otherwise, the limits are 20 km/h in school and hospital zones, 40 km/h on secondary roads, 50 km/h on main roads and 80 km/h in the central lanes of expressways.

questions.stem: Choose the right form: "Donamos cobijas para que los niños ___ calientes."
questions.explanation: "para que" always takes the subjunctive: the subject changes (we donate, the children are warm), and the purpose isn't a fact yet. estar → "estén". The indicative "están" and the future "estarán" are wrong after para que; the infinitive "estar" would need the same subject.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm studying so I can get a better job"?
choices: Estudio para conseguir un mejor trabajo.
Estudio para que consiga un mejor trabajo.
Estudio para que consigo un mejor trabajo.
Estudio por conseguir un mejor trabajo.
questions.explanation: The subject is the same (I study, I get the job), so use para + infinitive: "para conseguir". "para que consiga" would suggest someone else gets the job; "para que consigo" uses the indicative; "por" expresses a cause, not a purpose.

questions.stem: Complete with the right form of entender (tú): "Te lo explico otra vez para que lo ___."
questions.explanation: Different subjects (I explain, you understand), so para que + subjunctive. entender is a stem changer (e → ie): entiendo → "entiendas".

questions.stem: You see a box at the shelter and want to know what the money in it is for. What do you ask?
questions.explanation: "¿Para qué?" asks about purpose (what for?); the answer would be "Para reconstruir la escuela", for example. "¿Por qué?" asks for a cause. The question word "qué" needs its accent; "para que" without it is the conjunction "so that".

questions.stem: Choose the right form: "Ayudo a mi vecina sin que ella me lo ___."
questions.explanation: "sin que" always takes the subjunctive, because what doesn't happen isn't a fact: pedir → pido → "pida". The indicative "pide" and "pidió" are wrong after sin que, and the infinitive would need sin alone and the same subject.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Lo hacemos sin que nadie lo sepa.
Habla fuerte para que todos te oigan.
questions.explanation: "sin descansar": same subject, infinitive. "sin que nadie lo sepa" and "para que todos te oigan": different subjects, subjunctive. "sin que descansan" is wrong twice: sin que needs the subjunctive, and with the same subject Spanish uses sin + infinitive.

questions.stem: Put Andrés's Saturday at the collection center in order, as he describes it.
choices: They arrive at eight to receive the donations.
They sort everything so the trucks leave before twelve.
In the afternoon they go to the shelter to help the children with homework.
questions.explanation: Andrés writes: "Llegamos a las ocho para recibir las donaciones… lo separamos todo para que los camiones salgan antes de las doce… En la tarde vamos al albergue."

questions.stem: According to the poster, why does the campaign need volunteers?

image.alt: The campaign poster from the lesson: CAMPAÑA «MANOS QUE AYUDAN», Reconstruyamos juntos la escuela de San Isidro. It says the October rains damaged the school, that they need volunteers so that the children go back to school in January, that you can donate school supplies, blankets and water at the Centro Comunitario, Av. Juárez 15, on Saturdays from 9:00 to 14:00, and that no experience is needed.

choices: So the children can go back to school in January.
So the families have blankets this winter.
To build a new community center.
questions.explanation: The poster says: "Necesitamos voluntarios para que los niños vuelvan a clases en enero" (volver a clases = to go back to school). Blankets are one of the donations asked for, not the reason for volunteers.

questions.stem: According to the poster, when can you bring donations to the collection center?

image.alt: The campaign poster from the lesson, with the collection center address, Av. Juárez 15, and the hours: Sábados de 9:00 a 14:00.

questions.explanation: "Centro de acopio: Centro Comunitario, Av. Juárez 15. Sábados de 9:00 a 14:00." (el centro de acopio = collection center; sábados = on Saturdays).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: We're raising funds so that the families have blankets.
questions.explanation: Different subjects (we raise, the families have): para que + subjunctive, "tengan". The purpose clause can also come first: "Para que las familias tengan cobijas, recaudamos fondos." "Tienen" is indicative and can't follow para que.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Don't sign anything without reading it. (tú)
questions.explanation: Same subject (you sign, you read), so sin + infinitive, with the pronoun attached: "sin leerlo". "No firmes" is the negative tú command of firmar. "sin que" would need a different subject and a subjunctive verb.

questions.stem: Which sentence would you expect in a formal notice rather than in conversation?
choices: Ven, que te explique cómo funciona.
Les pedimos que lleguen temprano a fin de que podamos empezar a tiempo.
Habla más fuerte para que te oigan.
questions.explanation: "a fin de que" means the same as "para que" but belongs to formal writing such as notices and letters. "Ven, que te explique" is informal speech, and the other two are everyday Spanish.

questions.stem: At the end of his post, Andrés writes: "Ven un sábado, que te presente al equipo." What does it mean?
choices: Come one Saturday, because the team introduces you.
Come one Saturday, when the team introduces itself.
Come one Saturday, and I'll introduce you to the team.
Come one Saturday; I hope the team introduces you.
questions.explanation: After a command, informal Spanish uses que + subjunctive for a purpose: "que te presente" = so that I (can) introduce you. "presente" is the yo subjunctive of presentar (to introduce).

questions.stem: Sofía flies to Toronto tomorrow for the first time. She tells her mom: "Cuando ___ a Toronto, te llamo."
questions.explanation: The arrival is in the future, so cuando takes the subjunctive: llegar → "llegue" (g → gu before e). The future "llegaré" is never used after cuando in a time clause; "llego" would describe a habit and "llegué" the past.

questions.stem: Choose the right form: "Cuando ___ niña, vivía en Puebla."
questions.explanation: This is the past (a description, so the imperfect: "era"), and cuando + a past or habitual action takes the indicative. The subjunctive is only for a future action.

questions.stem: Complete with the right form of volver (yo): "Espera aquí hasta que yo ___."
questions.explanation: The return hasn't happened yet (the main verb is a command about the future), so hasta que + subjunctive: volver → vuelvo → "vuelva".

questions.stem: Choose the right form: "Quiero empacar antes de que ___ mis papás."
questions.explanation: "antes de que" always takes the subjunctive: llegar → "lleguen" (g → gu before e). The infinitive "llegar" only works with the same subject (antes de llegar).

questions.stem: Which is the natural way to say "I'm going to pack before I leave"?
choices: Voy a empacar antes de que salga.
Voy a empacar antes de que salgo.
Voy a empacar antes de salir.
questions.explanation: With the same subject (I pack, I leave), Spanish uses antes de + infinitive: "antes de salir". "antes de que salga" would normally be understood as someone else leaving (he, she or you, usted); "antes de que salgo" uses the indicative; and "antes" needs "de" before an infinitive.

questions.stem: Which question is correct?
questions.explanation: A question with "¿cuándo?" asks for information, so it takes the indicative (or the future: ¿Cuándo llegarás?). The subjunctive goes after cuando without an accent, joining two clauses about the future: "Cuando llegues, llámame."

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: En cuanto tenga la visa, compro el boleto.
Cuando tendré la residencia, buscaré trabajo.
Mientras estés en Canadá, llámame los domingos.
Después de que se fueron los invitados, limpiamos.
questions.explanation: "En cuanto tenga" and "Mientras estés": future, so subjunctive. "Después de que se fueron": past, so indicative. "Cuando tendré" is wrong: the future is never used after cuando in a time clause; say "Cuando tenga la residencia".

questions.stem: Match each sentence to the time it talks about.
choices: a single event in the past
questions.explanation: The mood follows the time: past (llegué) and habit (llego) take the indicative; the future takes the subjunctive (llegue). A question would use "¿Cuándo…?" with the indicative.

questions.stem: According to Kevin's letter, what does he have to do within thirty days?
choices: Apply for the visa at the consulate in Dallas.
Get a work permit from his company.
Exchange his visa for a resident card at the INM.
Leave Mexico and come back in.
questions.explanation: "Ahora tengo un plazo de treinta días para cambiar la visa por la tarjeta de residente en una oficina del Instituto Nacional de Migración." He already got the visa in Dallas, and he will apply for the work permit once he has the card.

questions.stem: Kevin writes: "En cuanto tenga la tarjeta, voy a pedir el permiso de trabajo." What does this tell you?
choices: He already has the card and the work permit.
He applied for the work permit before getting the card.
He gets a new card every time he applies for a permit.
He doesn't have the card yet; he'll apply for the work permit once he does.
questions.explanation: "En cuanto tenga" is subjunctive: the card is still in the future. With the indicative ("En cuanto tuve la tarjeta, pedí…") the events would be in the past.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: When you arrive, call me. (tú)
questions.explanation: The arrival is in the future, so "cuando llegues" (subjunctive). The cuando clause can go first or last: "Cuando llegues, llámame" or "Llámame cuando llegues." "Cuando llegas" describes a habit, which doesn't fit a command about a future arrival.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'm not leaving until you finish.
questions.explanation: "hasta que" + subjunctive for something that hasn't happened yet: "termines". The clause can also come first: "Hasta que termines, no me voy."

questions.stem: In standard Spanish, which is the usual way to write "After the guests left, we cleaned up"?
choices: Después de que se fueron los invitados, limpiamos.
Después de que se vayan los invitados, limpiamos.
Después de que se iban los invitados, limpiamos.
Después de que se irán los invitados, limpiamos.
questions.explanation: In the past, después de que takes the indicative preterite in standard usage: "se fueron". "se vayan" would make it a future plan ("After the guests leave, we'll clean up"). Newspapers sometimes write the imperfect subjunctive (se fueran) here; recognize it, but write the indicative.

questions.stem: Choose the right form: "Busco una licuadora que no ___ mucho ruido."
questions.explanation: You're looking for one and haven't found it: the antecedent (una licuadora) is wanted, not known, so the relative clause takes the subjunctive: hacer → hago → "haga".

questions.stem: Choose the right form: "Tengo una licuadora que ___ mucho ruido, y quiero cambiarla."
questions.explanation: You have this blender: the antecedent is known and real, so the relative clause takes the indicative: "hace". The subjunctive "haga" is for one you're looking for.

questions.stem: Complete with the right form of gustar: "No hay nada en esta tienda que me ___."
questions.explanation: "No hay nada que…" describes something that doesn't exist, so the relative clause takes the subjunctive: "guste".

questions.stem: What is the difference between "Compra lo que necesitas" and "Compra lo que necesites"?
choices: The first is wrong; only the subjunctive is possible after lo que.
The first is formal and the second informal.
There is no difference at all.
The first refers to things already known (the list); the second means "whatever you need".
questions.explanation: Both are correct. With the indicative, "lo que necesitas" is something definite that both speakers know about. With the subjunctive, "lo que necesites" is open: whatever you need.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly says "I don't know anyone who repairs blenders"?
choices: No conozco a nadie que repare licuadoras.
No conozco nadie que repara licuadoras.
No conozco a nadie que repara licuadoras.
No conozco nadie que repare licuadoras.
questions.explanation: "nadie" as an object keeps the personal a ("a nadie"), and a nonexistent antecedent takes the subjunctive ("repare"). Each of the other choices drops the a, uses the indicative, or both.

questions.stem: In which sentences is the subjunctive used correctly? Select all that apply.
choices: Tengo un amigo que sepa reparar aparatos.
Busco unos audífonos que sean inalámbricos.
questions.explanation: Asking whether someone exists ("¿Hay alguien que hable…?"), looking for something ("Busco unos audífonos que sean…") and "whatever" ("lo que quieras") take the subjunctive. "Tengo un amigo" is a real, known person, so it needs the indicative: "que sabe reparar aparatos".

questions.stem: This is the product page from the lesson without its headings. Choose the word for each numbered part.

image.alt: The invented online store page for the Licuadora Remolino 600 with five numbered parts and no headings: 1 next to the amount 1,299 MXN; 2 a green box listing a 1.5-liter glass jar, a 600 W motor with three speeds and stainless steel blades; 3 a box with 20 × 18 × 40 cm; 4 a box saying Llega el jueves 19; 5 a box with four stars and a customer's comment signed Lupita R.

questions.explanation: 1 el precio (1,299 MXN), 2 las características (the features), 3 el tamaño (the size: how big it is), 4 el envío (shipping: when it arrives), 5 la reseña (a customer's review). There's no refund (el reembolso) on the page, and the brand (la marca) is in the title, which has no number.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly says "This is the store where I bought my computer"?
choices: Esta es la tienda que compré mi computadora en.
Esta es la tienda en la que compré mi computadora.
Esta es la tienda la que compré mi computadora.
Esta es la tienda en que la compré mi computadora.
questions.explanation: The preposition goes before the relative word: "en la que" (also possible: "en que" or "donde"). Spanish never leaves the preposition at the end, and it can't be dropped. The last choice adds a stray "la".

questions.stem: In the reviews, why did Jorge give the headphones only two stars?
choices: The store refused to give him a refund.
The material seemed cheap and the case broke after a week.
questions.explanation: "El material es muy delgado: parece plástico barato… A la semana se rompió el estuche." He did get his refund ("me lo dieron sin problemas"), and he doesn't complain about the sound or the delivery.

questions.stem: Ana writes: "No hay ningún modelo que tenga cable de repuesto." What does she mean?
choices: None of the models comes with a spare cable.
She bought a model with a spare cable.
The store sells spare cables for every model.
She is looking for a model without a cable.
questions.explanation: "No hay ningún modelo que tenga…" says that such a model doesn't exist, which is why the verb is subjunctive (tenga). "de repuesto" = spare.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'm looking for a backpack that's waterproof. (any one, as long as it's waterproof)
questions.explanation: The backpack is wanted, not one you know, so the relative clause takes the subjunctive: "que sea impermeable". "que es impermeable" would describe a particular backpack you already have in mind.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: There's nothing I like.
questions.explanation: Spanish needs "que" here ("nothing that I like"), and the antecedent "nada" doesn't exist, so the verb is subjunctive: "No hay nada que me guste."

questions.stem: Your friend can't decide between three shirts. You say: "Llévate la que te guste." What do you mean?
choices: Take the one you like (I know which one).
You took the one you liked.
Take it if you like it.
questions.explanation: The subjunctive makes "la que te guste" open: whichever one. "Llévate la que te gusta" (indicative) would point to one you both know she likes.

questions.stem: Which word does the lesson describe as the everyday Mexican word for any earthquake, big or small?
questions.explanation: "el temblor" is the everyday word (¿Sentiste el temblor?). "el sismo" is the word of the news and official texts, "el terremoto" is usually a big, destructive one, and "las réplicas" are aftershocks.

questions.stem: A news report says: "Se esperan réplicas en las próximas horas." What is expected?
questions.explanation: "las réplicas" are the aftershocks that follow a big earthquake. A drill is "un simulacro", rescue volunteers are "brigadistas", and collapsing is "derrumbarse".

questions.stem: Which of these earthquakes did NOT happen on 19 September?
questions.explanation: The magnitude 7.3 quake in Guerrero was on 14 September 1995: it triggered the seismic alert's first public warning. The other three are the 19 September earthquakes of 1985, 2017 and 2022.

questions.stem: Why can the seismic alert warn Mexico City tens of seconds before a quake from the Pacific coast arrives?
choices: Scientists can predict earthquakes a few minutes ahead.
The sensors are under Mexico City itself.
The alert sounds every day at the same time.
Its radio signal travels much faster than seismic waves.
questions.explanation: Sensors near the coast detect the quake and send a radio signal, which reaches the city almost instantly; the seismic waves take tens of seconds to travel hundreds of kilometers. Earthquakes can't be predicted, and a quake that starts near the city may give no warning.

questions.stem: A poster says "No usar el elevador." Say it to a group of coworkers (ustedes): "___ el elevador."
questions.explanation: The ustedes command is the ustedes subjunctive: usar → "usen"; negative: "No usen el elevador."

questions.stem: A poster says "Dirigirse a la zona de seguridad" (dirigirse = to head for). Encourage your group, including yourself (nosotros): "___ a la zona de seguridad."
questions.explanation: The nosotros subjunctive of dirigirse is "nos dirijamos" (g → j before a). In an affirmative command the pronoun attaches and the final -s drops: dirijamos + nos → "dirijámonos", with an accent to keep the stress.

questions.stem: Choose the right form: "No empujes, para que nadie se ___."
questions.explanation: Different subjects (you don't push, nobody falls), so para que + subjunctive: caer → caigo → "caiga".

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: "el simulacro" = drill; "los escombros" = rubble (usually plural); "el brigadista" = rescue volunteer or member of an emergency team; "la salida de emergencia" = emergency exit. An aftershock is "una réplica".

questions.stem: This is the school's evacuation plan without its labels. Choose the word for each numbered part.

image.alt: The floor plan of an invented school with five numbered parts: 1 a yellow backpack by the door of classroom 1; 2 green arrows along the hallway; 3 the staircase; 4 a green door at the end of the hallway; 5 a round sign with four arrows pointing to a dot, in the schoolyard.

questions.explanation: 1 la mochila de emergencia (emergency backpack), 2 la ruta de evacuación (evacuation route), 3 las escaleras (stairs), 4 la salida de emergencia (emergency exit), 5 la zona de seguridad (safe area; the sign with four arrows). There is no elevator on the plan, and no rubble.

questions.stem: In the invented news report, what do the authorities ask people not to do?
choices: Go back into any damaged building until specialists inspect it.
Leave their homes during the aftershocks.
questions.explanation: "…piden que la población revise sus casas y que no regrese a ningún edificio dañado hasta que lo revisen los especialistas." Thousands of people did evacuate offices and schools when the alert sounded.

questions.stem: In the report, "La alerta sísmica sonó unos 50 segundos antes de que llegara el movimiento." Why is "llegara" in the subjunctive?
choices: Because the sentence gives an order.
antes de que always takes the subjunctive; in the past it's the imperfect subjunctive.
Because llegar is an irregular verb.
questions.explanation: "antes de que" always takes the subjunctive, because at the time of the main action the other event hadn't happened yet. After a past main verb (sonó), it is the imperfect subjunctive, "llegara" (lessons 13 and 15).

questions.stem: Which instructions keep to the tú form all the way through? Select all that apply.
choices: Mantén la calma y no uses el elevador.
Mantén la calma y no use el elevador.
Aléjate de las ventanas y no corras.
Sal por la ruta de evacuación y no empujes.
questions.explanation: "Mantén… no uses", "Aléjate… no corras" and "Sal… no empujes" are all tú. "no use" is the usted form, so the second instruction mixes tú and usted.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: When the alert sounds, stay calm. (tú)
questions.explanation: The alert is a future event, so "cuando suene" (subjunctive). "mantén" is the irregular tú command of mantener (like ten). The subject "la alerta" can come before or after "suene", and the cuando clause can go first or last.

questions.stem: Who developed Mexico City's seismic alert system after the 1985 earthquake?
choices: CIRES, working with the Mexico City government
questions.explanation: After 1985 the Mexico City government worked with the Centro de Instrumentación y Registro Sísmico (CIRES), a nonprofit, to develop the alert, which has worked for Mexico City since 1991.

questions.stem: A guest asks what to bring to your party. Which answer is the most hospitable?
choices: Trae lo que sea que quieres.
questions.explanation: "lo que quieras" (subjunctive) hands the choice to your guest: whatever you want. "lo que quieres" refers to something definite; "cualquiera cosa" should be "cualquier cosa", and that would sound less warm anyway.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tengo tanta hambre que me como ___." (I'm so hungry I'll eat anything.)
questions.explanation: "lo que sea" = anything at all. "lo que es" isn't an open phrase, "cualquiera cosa" should be "cualquier cosa", and "lo que quieras" means "whatever you want".

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "Llámame cuando ___, de día o de noche." (Call me any time, day or night.)
questions.explanation: "cuando sea" = any time at all. "cuando quieras" (whenever you want) and "cuando puedas" (whenever you can) also fit. The verb is subjunctive in all three because the time is open.

questions.stem: Complete the formal sentence with one word: "___ que vivas, recuerda de dónde vienes." (Wherever you live, remember where you come from.)
questions.explanation: "dondequiera que" + subjunctive = wherever. It is written as one word; "donde quiera" in two words means "where he / she / you (usted) wants".

questions.stem: Which sentence spells the formal "whoever" correctly?
choices: Quien quiera que llame, que deje un mensaje.
Quienquiera llame, que deje un mensaje.
Quienesquiera que llame, que deje un mensaje.
Quienquiera que llame, que deje un mensaje.
questions.explanation: "quienquiera" is one word and is followed by que + subjunctive. "Quienesquiera" is the plural, which doesn't fit the singular verb "llame".

questions.stem: "—Te dejé el informe en tu escritorio. —Ajá, como sea." How does the reply sound?
questions.explanation: Said like this, "como sea" means "whatever": the speaker doesn't care. "Ajá" is "uh-huh". A friendly reply would be "Gracias, ahorita lo veo."

questions.stem: At the end of a conversation a friend says: "Cualquier cosa, me avisas." What does she mean?
choices: If anything comes up, let me know.
questions.explanation: It is a fixed, friendly offer of help: if you need anything, tell me. The full idea would be "Si necesitas cualquier cosa, avísame".

questions.stem: Match each phrase to its meaning.
questions.explanation: + sea = any option at all: lo que sea, quien sea, donde sea. "a cualquier hora" = at any time of day. "however you want" would be "como quieras".

questions.stem: Which sentences use the subjunctive correctly for an open choice? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "lo que quieras, a quien quieras, cuando puedas" leave the choice open. "Ayer hice lo que quiera" is about a past fact, so it needs the indicative: "hice lo que quise".

questions.stem: Complete: "Vivo donde ___." (I live where I was born.)
questions.explanation: This is a real, known place, so the indicative: "donde nací" (preterite). The subjunctive would make the place open: "Puedes vivir donde quieras."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Order whatever you want, it's on me.
questions.explanation: "lo que quieras" = whatever you want (subjunctive: the choice is open). "Yo invito" or "invito yo" (it's my treat) can come first or last.

questions.stem: Which everyday sentence means the same as the notice "Quienquiera que use la cocina debe dejarla limpia"?
choices: El que use la cocina, que la deje limpia.
El que usa la cocina siempre la deja limpia.
questions.explanation: "quienquiera que" → "el que" (or "quien"), still with the subjunctive "use"; "debe dejarla" → "que la deje". The second choice is a statement about a habit, not a rule.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ puede aprender a cocinar." (Anyone can learn to cook.)
questions.explanation: As a pronoun, "cualquiera" = anyone. "cualquier" only goes before a noun; "cualquier cosa" means "anything"; and "quienquiera que" needs a verb after it (quienquiera que quiera…).

questions.stem: In the dialogue, what does Beto want to do on Saturday?
choices: Go to the movies in the evening.
Invite a lot of people to his house.
Anything, as long as he doesn't have to get up early.
questions.explanation: "Lo que sea, mientras no tenga que madrugar" (madrugar = to get up very early; mientras + subjunctive = as long as).

questions.stem: Cuando llegamos al cine, la película ya ___. (empezar)
questions.explanation: The film started before the moment you arrived, so the pluperfect fits: haber in the imperfect + participle. "La película" is singular, so "había", and the participle never changes: "había empezado". "Habían" is plural, "empezada" wrongly makes the participle agree, and the present perfect "ha empezado" doesn't fit a story told in the past ("llegamos").

questions.stem: Nadie había ___ el caso. (resolver)
questions.explanation: "Resolver" has an irregular participle, like "volver" (vuelto) and "devolver" (devuelto): "resuelto". "Resolvido" is the regular pattern the verb doesn't follow; "resolto" and "resuelvido" are mixtures.

questions.stem: How do you say "I had already seen it" (el video)?
questions.explanation: Object pronouns go in front of "había", and nothing goes between "había" and the participle: "Ya lo había visto". The participle stays "visto" even though it refers to something: it never agrees after haber.

questions.stem: What does this sentence mean? "Cuando llegó la policía, el ladrón huyó."
choices: The thief ran away when the police arrived.
The thief had already run away before the police arrived.
The police ran away when the thief arrived.
The police arrested the thief when they arrived.
questions.explanation: Two preterites tell two events in sequence: the police arrived, and then (at that moment) the thief fled. To say he was already gone, Spanish uses the pluperfect: "Cuando llegó la policía, el ladrón ya había huido."

questions.stem: Which of these participles are spelled correctly? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Huido" (huir) has no accent, because the i comes after u; "leído" takes one because it comes after e; "descrito" is the irregular participle of "describir". The correct forms of the others are "resuelto", "roto" and "construido" (no accent after u, by the same rule as "huido").

questions.stem: Write the pluperfect of "huir": Para entonces, los sospechosos ya ___.
questions.explanation: "Los sospechosos" is plural, so haber in the imperfect is "habían", and the participle of "huir" is "huido" (no accent): "habían huido". By then, the suspects had already fled.

questions.stem: Match each verb with its participle.
questions.explanation: All five participles are irregular: hecho, dicho, vuelto, escrito, abierto. "Hacido" and "abrido" follow the regular -ido pattern, which these verbs don't use.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things and the person in this detective's evidence board.

image.alt: An evidence board titled Caso 214, Robo en la joyería. Numbered: a photo of a man with a mustache, a card with a large fingerprint, a plastic evidence bag with a pistol inside, a movie ticket for Cine Luna at 21:30 next to a sticky note reading ¿Estuvo en el cine?, and a woman standing beside the board, pointing at it.

questions.explanation: The photo is the suspect (el sospechoso), the fingerprint card la huella (digital), the bag holds the weapon (el arma), the ticket is a possible alibi (la coartada: was he at the movies?), and the woman investigating is la detective. Nothing on the board shows a victim or a judge.

questions.stem: In the story El collar de jade, what first made the detective suspicious?
choices: Julián had no alibi for that night.
Don Ernesto's fingerprints were all over the safe.
A neighbor had seen don Ernesto at a jewelry store.
The broken glass was outside, so the window had been broken from inside.
questions.explanation: "El vidrio estaba afuera... alguien la había roto desde adentro." The glass in the garden showed the window was broken from inside the house. Julián had an alibi (the movie ticket), the safe had no fingerprints at all, and the jewelry store visit came the next day.

questions.stem: Which noun is always feminine, even when it refers to a man?
questions.explanation: "La víctima" keeps its feminine article for anyone: "La víctima, un hombre de 60 años…". The others change for a woman: la detective, la jueza, la sospechosa.

questions.stem: Fui a la policía a ___ el robo de mi bicicleta.
questions.explanation: To report a crime to the police is "denunciar" (or "poner una denuncia"). "Detener" is what the police do to a suspect (arrest), "huir" is to flee, and "confesar" is what a guilty person does.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: When the police arrived, the thief had already fled.
questions.explanation: The arrival is the moment being told (preterite "llegó"); the escape happened before it, so it's pluperfect: "ya había huido", singular because there is one thief. The "cuando" clause can come first or last, and the subject can go before or after the verb: "Cuando llegó la policía, el ladrón ya había huido", "El ladrón ya había huido cuando llegó la policía", "Ya había huido el ladrón cuando llegó la policía".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: They had already closed the store.
questions.explanation: "Habían cerrado": haber agrees with "they", and the participle never changes, so not "cerrada" even though "la tienda" is feminine. "Ya" usually goes first ("Ya habían cerrado la tienda"), and can also come after the verb or at the end.

questions.stem: Put the events of El collar de jade in the order they happened (not the order the story tells them).
choices: Don Ernesto vendió el collar en una joyería.
Don Ernesto llamó a la policía.
questions.explanation: The sale happened in March, seven months earlier: the story only reveals it near the end, in the pluperfect ("había vendido"). Julián's evening at the movies was on Tuesday night, before don Ernesto came home at ten thirty and called the police. The detective visited the jewelry stores the next day, and the confession came last.

questions.stem: ___ abrir la puerta, Marta vio una carta en el suelo.
questions.explanation: "Al" + infinitive means "when, on (doing)": "Al abrir la puerta" = When she opened the door. "Cuando" needs a conjugated verb (cuando abrió), "después" needs "de" (después de abrir), and "en abrir" isn't used this way.

questions.stem: Era de noche y ___. De pronto, alguien tocó la puerta.
questions.explanation: The first sentence sets the scene, so it takes the imperfect: "Era de noche y llovía." The preterite "llovió" would make the rain an event in the chain of events, the future doesn't fit a past story, and "llueva" is a subjunctive with nothing to trigger it.

questions.stem: What does this sentence mean? "Apenas llegó a casa, se durmió."
choices: He fell asleep before he got home.
He got home when he woke up.
As soon as he got home, he fell asleep.
questions.explanation: Before a clause about an event, "apenas" means "as soon as", like "en cuanto": as soon as he got home, he fell asleep. With a verb on its own or an amount, it means "barely": "Apenas dormí" = I barely slept.

questions.stem: Marta buscaba las llaves. ___, su hermano llamaba a un cerrajero (locksmith).
questions.explanation: Two things were going on at the same time in different places, so "mientras tanto" (meanwhile) fits. "Por último" introduces the last step of a series, "hasta entonces" looks back from a turning point, and "al cabo de" needs a period of time after it (al cabo de una hora).

questions.stem: How do you say "The thief was about to leave when the alarm went off"?
choices: El ladrón acababa de salir cuando sonó la alarma.
El ladrón estaba a punto de salir cuando sonó la alarma.
El ladrón estaba a punto de salió cuando sonó la alarma.
El ladrón estuvo a punto de salir cuando sonaba la alarma.
questions.explanation: "Estar a punto de" + infinitive = to be about to; in a story it's usually in the imperfect, interrupted by a preterite event: "estaba a punto de salir cuando sonó la alarma". "Acababa de salir" means he had just left (the opposite moment), "a punto de salió" puts a conjugated verb after "de", and the last option turns the alarm into background.

questions.stem: In which part of a story is the conflict resolved?
questions.explanation: "El desenlace" is the ending, where the conflict is resolved. "El planteamiento" sets up the story, "el nudo" is where the conflict starts and grows, and "la moraleja" is the lesson a fable states at the end, not the resolution itself.

questions.stem: Editorial Colibrí publicó la novela en 2024. Here, "la editorial" means:
questions.explanation: "La editorial" (feminine) is a publisher, a publishing house. "El editorial" (masculine) is a newspaper's editorial. An editor is "el editor" or "la editora", and a bookstore is "la librería".

questions.stem: Which of these connectors take the indicative when they describe a real event in the past? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: For a past fact, "en cuanto", "tan pronto como" and "apenas" take the indicative: "En cuanto llegó, me llamó." "Antes de que" always takes the subjunctive (lesson 07), and "para que" (purpose, lesson 06) does too.

questions.stem: Complete with a connector meaning "after": ___ una hora, llegó la policía. (An hour later, the police arrived.)
questions.explanation: "Al cabo de" + a period of time = after, … later: "Al cabo de una hora, llegó la policía." "Después de una hora", "luego de una hora" (common in Latin America), "tras una hora" and "pasada una hora" are also correct. In everyday Mexican speech you'll also hear "a la hora, llegó la policía".

questions.stem: Match each connector with its meaning.
questions.explanation: "Desde entonces" reaches from a past moment toward now; "hasta entonces" looks back to what was true until a turning point; "a partir de entonces" starts something new from that point; "mientras tanto" is what happened at the same time; "de pronto" = "de repente". "As soon as" would be "en cuanto", "tan pronto como" or "apenas".

questions.stem: Name the numbered things and the person in this bookstore.

image.alt: A small bookstore. A book stands on a table; its front shows a moon over a house, the words La noche de los relojes and Ana Robles, and at the bottom a hummingbird logo with Editorial Colibrí. On a stand, an open book shows short lines in two groups. A young man sits in an armchair reading an open book whose page is headed Capítulo 3. Six numbers: on the picture on the front of the standing book, beside its large title words, beside the logo, above the stand, above the heading on the young man's page, and beside the young man.

questions.explanation: The front of the book is la portada; "La noche de los relojes" is el título; the hummingbird logo and "Editorial Colibrí" are the publisher, la editorial. The short lines in groups (stanzas) on the stand are a poem, el poema. "Capítulo 3" heads a chapter, el capítulo, and the young man reading is el lector. A narrator is inside a story, not something you can point to.

questions.stem: Put the events of the fable El tlacuache y el agua in order.
choices: Hace mucho tiempo, vivía en el bosque un tlacuache muy tímido.
Un año no llovió y el río se secó.
Una noche, el tlacuache salió del bosque sin decir nada.
La tercera noche, encontró el manantial.
A partir de ese día, nadie se rio de él.
questions.explanation: The fable moves from the planteamiento (the shy opossum, in the imperfect), through the nudo (the drought, his secret departure) and the clímax (finding the spring), to the desenlace ("A partir de ese día…").

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: As soon as she opened the door, she saw the letter.
questions.explanation: For a real past event, "en cuanto" takes the indicative: "en cuanto abrió la puerta". The subjunctive "abriera" is for a past sentence that looks ahead to something that hadn't happened yet (lesson 15). The "en cuanto" clause can go first or last: "Vio la carta en cuanto abrió la puerta."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I haven't seen him since then.
questions.explanation: "Desde entonces" (since then) reaches from a past moment to now, so it goes well with the present perfect: "Desde entonces no lo he visto" or "No lo he visto desde entonces". "No" and "lo" go in front of "he visto". "Hasta entonces" means "until then", which doesn't fit.

questions.stem: Para el viernes, nosotros ya ___ el proyecto. (terminar)
questions.explanation: A point in the future ("para el viernes", by Friday) and something finished before it: future perfect, "habremos terminado" for nosotros. "Habrán" is the ellos form, "habemos" isn't the standard nosotros form of haber in compound tenses (that's "hemos" in the present perfect), and the participle never takes a plural ending.

questions.stem: —¿Dónde está Luis? No vino a la reunión. —No sé. Se habrá quedado dormido. What does the second speaker mean?
choices: He had fallen asleep before the meeting started.
questions.explanation: Here the future perfect is a guess about something that has probably happened: "He must have overslept / fallen asleep." The simple future "estará" makes the same kind of guess about the present.

questions.stem: How do you say "In your place, I would have accepted the promotion"?
choices: En tu lugar, habré aceptado el ascenso.
En tu lugar, había aceptado el ascenso.
En tu lugar, habría aceptado el ascenso.
En tu lugar, habría aceptar el ascenso.
questions.explanation: "Would have" + participle is the conditional perfect: "habría aceptado". "Habré aceptado" is "I will have accepted", "había aceptado" is "I had accepted", and "habría aceptar" uses the infinitive instead of the participle. (In speech you'll also hear "hubiera aceptado" in this meaning.)

questions.stem: Ana no contesta el teléfono. ___ en una reunión. (a guess about right now: She's probably in a meeting.)
questions.explanation: A guess about the present takes the simple future: "Estará en una reunión" (A2 honors 16h2). The future perfect "habrá estado" would guess about the past (she has probably been in a meeting), and the conditional forms describe hypotheticals or guesses about a past moment.

questions.stem: Me ___ estudiar música, pero mis padres no me dejaron.
questions.explanation: A past wish that didn't come true: "Me habría gustado" (I would have liked). "Habrá gustado" is a future perfect, "había gustado" means "I had liked", and the participle doesn't change to "gustada". (Many speakers say "Me hubiera gustado", which is also correct.)

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Para junio habré terminado el curso.
Si habría tenido tiempo, habría ido.
questions.explanation: "Para junio habré terminado" (future perfect before a future point), "Yo no lo habría hecho" (conditional perfect) and "¿Qué habrá pasado?" (a guess about the past) are correct. A "si" meaning "if" never takes the conditional ("Si hubiera tenido tiempo, habría ido" is honors 16h1), and the participle after haber never agrees: "habrán cerrado".

questions.stem: Write the conditional perfect of "decir" (yo): En tu lugar, yo no le ___ nada.
questions.explanation: Haber in the conditional (habría) + the irregular participle "dicho": "habría dicho". "Hubiera dicho" is also heard and accepted in this meaning (honors 16h1 explains that form).

questions.stem: Match each Spanish sentence with its meaning.
questions.explanation: All four are haber + "terminado"; only the tense of haber changes: future (habré), conditional (habría), imperfect (había), present (he). "I will finish" is the simple future, "terminaré".

questions.stem: Put the events of Lucía's career (from the podcast Trayectorias) in time order, from earliest to latest.
choices: Trabajaba en un banco en Guadalajara.
Dejó el banco y abrió una panadería.
Para 2031 habrá abierto tres panaderías más.
questions.explanation: She worked at the bank, was offered a promotion there ("me habían ofrecido un ascenso", before her decision), left to open a bakery, saw it fail after eight months, and hopes to have opened three more bakeries by 2031: the future perfect looks back from that future point.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: By 2035 I will have finished my degree.
questions.explanation: "Will have finished" by a future point is the future perfect, "habré terminado". "Para 2035" (by 2035) can start or end the sentence. "Habría terminado" would mean "I would have finished".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I wouldn't have done it.
questions.explanation: "Would have done" = "habría hecho" ("hecho" is the irregular participle of "hacer"). "No" and "lo" go before "habría". "Yo" is optional; it adds emphasis at the start or the end: "Yo no lo habría hecho", "No lo habría hecho yo". "Había hecho" means "had done".

questions.stem: Después de su fracaso, decidió ___: dejó la ingeniería y estudió cocina.
questions.explanation: Leaving engineering for cooking is a change of direction: "cambiar de rumbo". "Valer la pena" (to be worth it) doesn't take a person as subject this way, "envejecer" is to grow old, and "esforzarse" (to make an effort) doesn't describe the change the sentence explains.

questions.stem: Which word is closest in meaning to "el reto"?
questions.explanation: "El reto" and "el desafío" both mean "challenge"; "reto" is the more everyday word in Mexico. "El ascenso" is a promotion, "el fracaso" a failure and "el porvenir" the future.

questions.stem: La ciudad ___ por los mexicas en 1325.
questions.explanation: With "por" + agent, Spanish uses the ser passive, and the participle agrees with the subject, "la ciudad": "fue fundada". "Fundado" is masculine; the se passive doesn't normally take "por" + agent; "estaba fundada" describes a state, not the event of founding.

questions.stem: Las ruinas ___ patrimonio mundial.
questions.explanation: The subject "las ruinas" is feminine plural, so both ser and the participle agree: "fueron declaradas". In the ser passive the participle behaves like an adjective.

questions.stem: Hoy no podemos entrar: el museo ___ cerrado.
questions.explanation: The museum's state right now (not open) is estar + participle: "está cerrado". "Es cerrado" would be a passive event ("is closed by someone"), which doesn't fit "today we can't go in"; "sea" has no trigger for the subjunctive, and "son" is plural.

questions.stem: Turn into the passive: "Adamo Boari diseñó el Palacio de Bellas Artes."
choices: El Palacio de Bellas Artes fue diseñada por Adamo Boari.
El Palacio de Bellas Artes ha diseñado por Adamo Boari.
El Palacio de Bellas Artes fue diseñado de Adamo Boari.
El Palacio de Bellas Artes fue diseñado por Adamo Boari.
questions.explanation: The object (el Palacio, masculine) becomes the subject; "diseñó" (preterite) becomes "fue" + participle agreeing with it, "diseñado"; the old subject becomes the agent with "por". "Ha diseñado" is an active perfect with no ser, and "de" is not the agent preposition.

questions.stem: En la tumba ___ dos máscaras de jade.
questions.explanation: In the se passive the verb agrees with the thing: two masks, so plural "se encontraron". The RAE's Diccionario panhispánico de dudas asks for this agreement. "Fueron encontrado" leaves the participle without agreement (it should be "encontradas").

questions.stem: What does "Me robaron la cartera en el metro" mean?
choices: My wallet was stolen on the metro.
I stole a wallet on the metro.
They found my wallet on the metro.
I lost my wallet on the metro.
questions.explanation: The ellos form with no subject means someone unknown did it: literally "they stole my wallet", in English usually "my wallet was stolen". "Me" marks who it happened to.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT correct Spanish?
choices: Las tumbas se fueron descubiertas en 1952.
questions.explanation: "Se fueron descubiertas" mixes the se passive and the ser passive. Choose one: "Se descubrieron dos tumbas" or "Las tumbas fueron descubiertas". The ellos form "Descubrieron dos tumbas" (someone discovered them) is also correct.

questions.stem: In which sentences is the participle correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Los templos fueron construido por los mayas.
Las piezas están conservadas en el museo.
questions.explanation: With ser and estar the participle agrees: "fue restaurada" (la escultura), "están conservadas" (las piezas), "fue inaugurado" (el museo). "Los templos fueron construidos" needs the plural; with haber, the participle never changes: "Han restaurado la iglesia".

questions.stem: Write the ser passive in the preterite: La Piedra del Sol ___ en el Zócalo en 1790. (descubrir)
questions.explanation: Ser in the preterite (fue) + the irregular participle of "descubrir", agreeing with "la Piedra del Sol": "fue descubierta". The stone was found on 17 December 1790 during work in the Zócalo.

questions.stem: Match each active sentence with its passive version.
choices: La ciudad fue fundada por los mexicas.
Las casas fueron diseñadas por una arquitecta.
El puente fue construido por los ingenieros.
Las pinturas fueron restauradas por el INAH.
Las casas fue diseñado por una arquitecta.
questions.explanation: Each object becomes the subject, ser takes the preterite of the active verb (fue, fueron), the participle agrees with the new subject, and the old subject follows "por". The distractor fails on agreement: "las casas" needs "fueron diseñadas".

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this archaeological site.

image.alt: An archaeological site with green hills behind. Numbered: a small building on top of a stepped pyramid, the stepped pyramid itself, a carved stone serpent's head at the foot of the stairs, low broken stone walls in the foreground, and a woman in a hat kneeling with a brush next to a half-buried carved stone. A sign reads ZONA ARQUEOLÓGICA.

questions.explanation: The small building on top is el templo, standing on la pirámide; the carved serpent's head is una escultura; the broken walls are las ruinas, and the woman excavating with a brush is la arqueóloga.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The museum was opened in 1987.
questions.explanation: "El museo" is masculine, so "fue inaugurado". The date can start or end the sentence, and the subject can come before or after the verb: "En 1987 fue inaugurado el museo" and "Fue inaugurado el museo en 1987" are natural in a written text. (The Museo del Templo Mayor opened on 12 October 1987.)

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish, using the passive se.
questions.prompt: Two tombs were discovered.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the plural thing: "se descubrieron dos tumbas" (the usual order) or "Dos tumbas se descubrieron". The singular "descubrió" would not agree with "dos tumbas".

questions.stem: According to the guide in the lesson's dialogue, how was the Coyolxauhqui sculpture found?
choices: Archaeologists were looking for it in 1790.
Electric company workers found it while digging in 1978.
It was found in the Zócalo during paving work.
It was found when the museum was being built in 1987.
questions.explanation: "El 21 de febrero de 1978, unos trabajadores de la compañía de luz estaban excavando… cuando encontraron una enorme piedra redonda." The Zócalo and 1790 belong to the Sun Stone, and the museum opened in 1987, after the excavations.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, what makes a story magical realism?
choices: Something supernatural happens in a realistic world and is told as if it were normal.
The story takes place in an invented world of dragons and wizards.
The narrator explains every strange event scientifically.
The story is always set in a real Colombian town.
questions.explanation: The key is the combination: a recognizable, realistic world plus something impossible, told calmly, without surprise. A world of dragons is fantasy; a narrator who explains everything removes the magic; and the label isn't tied to one country.

questions.stem: Who first used the term (Magischer Realismus), and for what?
choices: Alejo Carpentier, for his novel, in 1949
Franz Roh, for a kind of painting, in 1925
Juan Rulfo, in Pedro Páramo, in 1955
questions.explanation: The German art critic Franz Roh used the term in 1925 for post-Expressionist painting. Carpentier wrote of "lo real maravilloso" in his 1949 prologue, a related but different idea.

questions.stem: Match each writer with a book the lesson mentions.
questions.explanation: Rulfo (Mexico) wrote Pedro Páramo; García Márquez (Colombia) Cien años de soledad; Allende (Chile, born in Lima) La casa de los espíritus; Carpentier (Cuba) El reino de este mundo. "La noche de los relojes" is the invented book in lesson 10's picture.

questions.stem: "Las gallinas ponían huevos azules cuando iba a llover." Why is this in the imperfect?
choices: It describes one event at one moment.
It describes something that happened regularly, as part of the village's normal life.
It describes something that had happened before the story began.
It describes something that will happen later.
questions.explanation: The imperfect makes the blue eggs a habit, part of the scene, like the weather. That is how the story makes the impossible seem normal. One event would be "una gallina puso un huevo azul".

questions.stem: In part 1, why is "Se había ido a Chicago doce años antes" in the pluperfect?
choices: It is a guess about the past.
Lucía left before the moment being told, so the story steps back.
questions.explanation: Lucía's departure is the earliest event of all, but it is told after the prophecy. The pluperfect, with "antes" (earlier), marks that jump back in time.

questions.stem: Put these events of La niebla de San Isidro in the order they happened.
choices: Doña Celia anunció la fecha de su muerte.
Doña Celia murió y llegaron las mariposas.
Lucía recibió la carta de su abuela.
questions.explanation: Lucía left twelve years earlier; then the prophecy, the death on 31 October with the butterflies, the fog after the burial, the letter dated 3 November (found one night in November), and the fog lifting when Lucía arrived on 9 December.

questions.stem: Why does the fog lift at the end? Choose the best inference.
choices: Because the teacher found a scientific explanation.
Because Lucía has come back, as doña Celia had predicted.
Because the butterflies left for the forest.
questions.explanation: The prophecy said the fog wouldn't leave "hasta que regrese Lucía", the letter said "la niebla te está esperando", and the butterfly leads Lucía to the house just before the fog rises. The last line, "siempre cumplía su palabra", confirms it.

questions.stem: What is impossible about the letter Lucía receives?
choices: It is dated after her grandmother's death.
questions.explanation: The letter is dated 3 November, three days after doña Celia died. The missing stamp is odd, but not impossible; the date is what a realistic world can't explain, and Lucía accepts it calmly.

questions.stem: Which sentences from the story present the impossible as normal? Select all that apply.
choices: En San Isidro nadie se sorprendía de nada.
Solo comentaron, con toda tranquilidad, que doña Celia siempre cumplía su palabra.
Por eso, cuando doña Celia anunció la fecha de su muerte, nadie se asustó.
Lucía trabajaba de enfermera en un hospital.
Compró un boleto de avión esa misma noche.
questions.explanation: The first three frame strange events as ordinary: nobody is surprised, nobody gets scared, and the villagers comment calmly. The last two are plain realistic facts with nothing impossible in them.

questions.stem: Match each word with its meaning.
questions.explanation: A presagio is a sign or omen; a profecía, a prediction someone says aloud; a hechizo, a spell; el alma (feminine, with el), the soul; la niebla, fog. "Butterfly" is la mariposa.

questions.stem: Complete with a word from the lesson: Durante semanas, la gente se perdía en la ___ blanca y espesa.
questions.explanation: "La niebla" (fog) covered San Isidro after the burial; it was "blanca y espesa" (white and thick).

questions.stem: Which phrase is correct?
questions.explanation: "Alma" is feminine: its adjectives are feminine ("buena") and its plural is "las almas". It takes "el" in the singular only because it starts with a stressed a, like "el agua" and "el arma".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: In the end, the prophecy came true.
questions.explanation: One event at the end of the story takes the preterite: "se cumplió" (cumplirse = to come true, lesson 01). "Se cumplía" would describe something that kept happening. "Al final" can start or end the sentence or sit in the middle, and the subject can follow the verb: "Al final se cumplió la profecía", "Se cumplió la profecía al final".

questions.stem: According to the lesson, how is Juan Rulfo often described?
choices: As a forerunner of magical realism
As the writer who invented Macondo
As a Chilean novelist born in Lima
As the critic who named the style in 1925
questions.explanation: Rulfo (Mexico, 1917–1986) is often called a forerunner of magical realism; García Márquez said reading Pedro Páramo helped him find his way. Macondo is García Márquez's town, Allende was born in Lima, and Franz Roh named the style.

questions.stem: Según la tradición, la ciudad de Tenochtitlan ___ en 1325.
questions.explanation: The subject is "la ciudad" (de Tenochtitlan), so the participle is feminine singular: "fue fundada". "Se fundaron" is plural and "fueron fundada" mixes plural and singular.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, how did the Maya count?
choices: In base 20, with a sign for zero
questions.explanation: "Contaban en base 20 y usaban un signo para el cero." Quipus were the Inca's records.

questions.stem: What were quipus?
choices: Maya books made of bark paper
Knotted, colored cords the Inca used to keep records
Stone courts for the ball game
questions.explanation: "Sus datos se guardaban en quipus, cuerdas con nudos de colores." Whether they recorded words as well as numbers is still debated. The Maya's bark-paper books are codices.

questions.stem: "Se cree que El Caracol era usado como observatorio." What does "se cree que" tell the reader?
choices: The building is certainly an observatory.
The writer visited the building personally.
The claim is a belief, not a settled fact.
questions.explanation: "Se cree que" (it is believed that) reports an opinion or hypothesis. History texts use it, with "se discute" and "según", to show that a claim isn't settled.

questions.stem: Name each numbered place on the map.

image.alt: A map in two panels. Left, Mesoamérica: southern Mexico with a shaded area labeled mexicas and a shaded area labeled zona maya over the Yucatán Peninsula and the land south of it; three numbered dots: one inside the mexicas area, one near the northern tip of the Yucatán Peninsula, and one at the southwestern edge of the Maya area. Right, Los Andes: a shaded band along the west coast of South America labeled incas, a numbered dot in southern Peru (with a smaller dot beside it), and a number beside a dashed brown line running the length of the band.

questions.explanation: Tenochtitlan (today Mexico City) is the mexica capital in central Mexico; Chichén Itzá is near the northern tip of the Yucatán Peninsula; Palenque is in Chiapas, at the edge of the Maya area; Cusco was the Inca capital in southern Peru (Machu Picchu is the small dot beside it); the dashed line is the Inca road network, the Qhapaq Ñan.

questions.stem: Match each civilization with a fact from the lesson.
choices: escritura jeroglífica y un signo para el cero
una ciudad en una isla unida a tierra firme por calzadas
una red de caminos de unos 30 000 kilómetros
questions.explanation: Maya glyphs and the zero, the mexica island city of Tenochtitlan with its three causeways, and the Inca Qhapaq Ñan. The pyramids of Egypt belong to another continent.

questions.stem: Put these events in time order, from earliest to latest.
choices: Muchas ciudades mayas del sur fueron abandonadas.
questions.explanation: The end of the Maya Classic period (about 900), the founding of Tenochtitlan (1325, by tradition), its conquest (13 August 1521), Atahualpa's capture (16 November 1532) and the fall of Nojpetén (13 March 1697).

questions.stem: Rewrite with the ser passive: "Alberto Ruz Lhuillier descubrió la tumba de Pakal en 1952." → La tumba de Pakal ___ por Alberto Ruz Lhuillier en 1952.
questions.explanation: "Descubrió" is preterite, so "fue"; the participle of "descubrir" is irregular ("descubierto") and agrees with "la tumba": "fue descubierta".

questions.stem: Which sentences use the passive correctly? Select all that apply.
choices: Se cultivaban maíz, frijol y calabaza.
La escritura maya fue descifrada en el siglo XX.
Los textos se tallaba en piedra.
Las calzadas fueron construidas sobre el lago.
questions.explanation: "Se cultivaban" agrees with three crops; "fue descifrada" agrees with "la escritura"; "fueron construidas" agrees with "las calzadas". "Los textos se tallaba" needs the plural "se tallaban", and "se fue capturado" mixes two passives: "Atahualpa fue capturado".

questions.stem: El apogeo de una civilización es…
questions.explanation: "El apogeo" is the peak, the time of greatest power or splendor; "la decadencia" is the opposite, the decline.

questions.stem: Which statement about Hiram Bingham and Machu Picchu is accurate?
choices: He was the first person ever to see it.
He built it in the 15th century.
He reached it in 1911 and made it known abroad, but other people had been there before.
He found it buried under Cusco.
questions.explanation: Bingham reached Machu Picchu on 24 July 1911 and made it famous abroad, but local farmers knew it and other visitors had been there in 1902. It was built in the 15th century, near Cusco, not under it.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish, using the passive se.
questions.prompt: Corn was grown in Mesoamerica.
questions.explanation: A long-lasting practice takes the imperfect, and the verb agrees with one thing, "maíz": "En Mesoamérica se cultivaba maíz" or "Se cultivaba maíz en Mesoamérica". "Se cultivaban" would need a plural noun.

questions.stem: Complete with the imperfect subjunctive of tener: "Ojalá ___ más tiempo." (I wish I had more time.)
questions.explanation: The imperfect subjunctive comes from the ellos preterite: tuvieron → tuvie- → tuviera. Ojalá never takes the indicative (tenía) or the conditional (tendría), and tenera is built from the infinitive, which never works. (Tuviese, the -se form, is also correct.)

questions.stem: Which is the nosotros imperfect subjunctive of decir?
questions.explanation: Ellos preterite dijeron → dije- + -ramos, with an accent on the vowel before the ending: dijéramos. After j there is no i (not dijiéramos), the stem is the preterite's dij- (not dec-), and nosotros always takes the written accent.

questions.stem: Sofía might come to the party. Compare "Ojalá venga Sofía" and "Ojalá viniera Sofía". What is the difference?
choices: The first is about the future and the second about the past.
The first is informal and the second is formal.
The second is a mistake: ojalá takes only the present subjunctive.
Both are about the party; the first sounds likely, the second sounds unlikely.
questions.explanation: With ojalá, the present subjunctive (venga) expresses a hope that may well come true; the imperfect subjunctive (viniera) expresses a wish the speaker doesn't really expect. Both refer to now or the future: the tense shows likelihood, not time. Neither is more formal, and both are correct.

questions.stem: Complete: "Mi primo gasta dinero como si ___ millonario."
questions.explanation: Como si (as if) takes the imperfect subjunctive: como si fuera millonario. The present indicative (es), the present subjunctive (sea) and the conditional (sería) are never used after como si.

questions.stem: Read: "Desde que heredó la casa de su abuela, Martín vive como si fuera rico. Pero la casa necesita muchas reparaciones (repairs) y él no tiene trabajo. Su esposa dice: Ojalá vendiera la casa y buscara un departamento." What does Martín's wife wish?
choices: That he would sell the house, although she doesn't really expect it.
That he will inherit more money soon.
That he had sold the house years ago.
That he will buy an apartment next week.
questions.explanation: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive (vendiera, buscara) is a wish about now or the future that the speaker thinks is unlikely: she wishes he'd sell the house and look for an apartment. Nothing is said about more money, and a wish about the past would need hubiera vendido (honors 16h1).

questions.stem: In a restaurant you say: "Quisiera la sopa del día." What is quisiera?
choices: The present subjunctive of querer: "that I want".
The conditional of querer: "I would want".
The imperfect subjunctive of querer, used as a polite "I'd like".
questions.explanation: Quisiera comes from quisieron (ellos preterite) → quisie- + -ra. Its unreal, softened meaning makes it a polite "I'd like". The preterite is quise, the present subjunctive quiera, and the conditional querría.
