questions.stem: Complete: "Nos conocimos por ___ en un crucero por el Caribe."
questions.explanation: Por casualidad = by chance: they met by chance on a cruise. Un capricho is a whim, el lujo is luxury and la fantasía is fantasy; none of them makes a phrase with por here.

questions.stem: Type the imperfect subjunctive of poder (yo): "Ojalá ___ volar."
questions.explanation: Ellos preterite pudieron → pudie- + -ra: Ojalá pudiera volar (I wish I could fly). The -se form pudiese is also correct. Podiera doesn't exist: the stem comes from the preterite (pud-).

questions.stem: Complete with the imperfect subjunctive of ser: "Me habla como si yo ___ un niño."
questions.explanation: Ser and ir share their preterite (fueron), so the imperfect subjunctive is fuera (or fuese) for both: como si yo fuera un niño (as if I were a child).

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Sueño con viajar a una isla desierta.
Sueño de viajar a una isla desierta.
questions.explanation: Ojalá takes the subjunctive (tuviera), never the conditional (tendría). Como si takes the imperfect subjunctive (fuera), not the indicative (sabe → supiera). Soñar takes con, not de: Sueño con viajar.

questions.stem: Match each infinitive to its imperfect subjunctive (yo).
questions.explanation: Each comes from the ellos preterite: fueron, durmieron, leyeron, trajeron, pidieron. The -ir stem changers keep their preterite vowel (durmiera, pidiera, not pediera), -er verbs with a vowel before the ending have y (leyera), and after j there is no i (trajera, not trajiera).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I wish I had a time machine.
questions.explanation: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive for a wish that can't come true: Ojalá tuviera una máquina del tiempo. The conditional tendría is never used after ojalá.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: She lives as if money didn't matter.
questions.explanation: Como si + imperfect subjunctive: Vive como si el dinero no importara. The subject can also follow the verb: …como si no importara el dinero. The present importa is never used after como si.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si ___ más dinero, compraría una casa."
questions.explanation: A hypothetical condition: si + imperfect subjunctive, with the conditional in the main clause (compraría). The conditional (tendría) and the present subjunctive (tenga) never go after si; tengo would need a present or future in the main clause (Si tengo dinero, compro / compraré una casa).

questions.stem: Complete: "Si fuera alcaldesa, ___ los baches de la colonia."
questions.explanation: With si + imperfect subjunctive (fuera), the main clause takes the conditional: arreglaría (I would fix). The present and future (arreglo, arreglaré) go with a real condition (si + present); arregle is a present subjunctive, which has no place here.

questions.stem: Which sentence shows that the speaker doesn't really expect to win?
choices: Si ganara, te invitaría a cenar.
Si gano, te invito a cenar.
Si ganas, me invitas a cenar.
Cuando gane, te invito a cenar.
questions.explanation: Si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional presents the win as unlikely or imaginary. Si gano / si ganas present it as a real possibility, and cuando gane takes it for granted.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT correct?
questions.explanation: The conditional never goes after si: Si tuviera tiempo, te ayudaría. The other three are correct: a hypothetical with the si clause second, a real condition, and a hypothetical with the si clause first.

questions.stem: A friend asks: "¿Qué harías si te sacaras la lotería?" Which answer fits?
choices: Compré una casa para mis papás.
Compraré una casa para mis papás.
Compre una casa para mis papás.
Compraría una casa para mis papás.
questions.explanation: A question with the conditional (harías) asks you to imagine, so you answer with the conditional: compraría. Compré is the preterite (I bought), compraré the future (I will buy) and compre a subjunctive or usted command.

questions.stem: Your friend can't decide between two jobs. How do you say "If I were you, I'd take the job in Puebla"?
choices: Si yo sería tú, aceptaría el trabajo en Puebla.
Si yo fuera tú, aceptaría el trabajo en Puebla.
Si yo estuviera tú, aceptaría el trabajo en Puebla.
Si yo era tú, aceptaría el trabajo en Puebla.
questions.explanation: If I were you = Si yo fuera tú, with ser in the imperfect subjunctive and the conditional after it. Sería can't follow si, estar doesn't fit, and the indicative era makes no hypothetical. Yo que tú, aceptaría… says the same more briefly.

questions.stem: Complete: "El ___ de la ciudad no alcanza para arreglar todas las calles."
questions.explanation: El presupuesto is the budget: the city's budget isn't enough (no alcanza) to fix every street. Un impuesto is a tax, un bache a pothole and el drenaje the drainage system.

questions.stem: Read: "Si yo fuera presidenta municipal, mi prioridad sería el agua potable. Invertiría en el drenaje y no subiría los impuestos, porque la gente ya paga mucho." What does the speaker say about taxes?
choices: She would raise them to pay for the drainage.
questions.explanation: No subiría los impuestos = she wouldn't raise taxes, because people already pay a lot. Everything is hypothetical (si fuera…, sería, invertiría), so she hasn't done anything yet.

questions.stem: Complete with vivir (nosotros): "Si ___ cerca del trabajo, no tendríamos que manejar tanto."
questions.explanation: A hypothetical about now: si + imperfect subjunctive. Ellos preterite vivieron → vivié- + -ramos, with the accent: viviéramos (or viviésemos).

questions.stem: Complete with the conditional of hacer: "¿Qué ___ (tú) si fueras invisible?"
questions.explanation: Hacer has the irregular stem har- in the conditional: harías. The si clause takes the imperfect subjunctive (fueras); the main verb takes the conditional.

questions.stem: Label the numbered parts of the neighborhood.

image.alt: A neighborhood crossroads with five numbered spots: a town hall with a flag and clock, a dark hole in the road, a drain grate in a puddle, a street lamp marked with an X, and a water tank with a tap and a jug.

questions.explanation: 1 la alcaldía (the town hall with the flag), 2 el bache (the hole in the road), 3 el drenaje (the drain grate with water pooling), 4 el alumbrado público (the street lamp that is out), 5 el agua potable (the tap for drinking water). El presupuesto (budget) and el impuesto (tax) are money, not things you can see on the street.

questions.stem: Match each si clause to the main clause that goes with it.
questions.explanation: Real: si + present → present (or future). Hypothetical now: si + imperfect subjunctive → conditional. Past: si + pluperfect subjunctive → conditional perfect (honors 16h1). Nos quedáramos is an imperfect subjunctive, which doesn't go in the main clause.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I would invest in housing if I were mayor.
questions.explanation: Main clause in the conditional, si clause in the imperfect subjunctive: Invertiría en vivienda si fuera alcalde. The si clause can also come first (in writing, with a comma after it: Si fuera alcalde, invertiría en vivienda). Sería can't follow si.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: If they improved the drainage system, the street wouldn't flood.
questions.explanation: Si + imperfect subjunctive (mejoraran), conditional in the main clause (no se inundaría; inundarse = to flood). Either clause can come first (with a comma after a si clause that comes first, in writing), and la calle can go before or after the verb. Mejorarían, a conditional, can't follow si.

questions.stem: Put it in the past: "Quiero que vengas." → "Quería que ___."
questions.explanation: A past main verb (quería) takes the imperfect subjunctive: vinieron → viniera(s). The indicative venías and the conditional vendrías don't fit after querer que, which always takes a subjunctive.

questions.stem: Complete: "Mi jefa me pidió que la ___ antes de las cinco."
questions.explanation: Pedir que reports a request, so it takes the subjunctive, and after the preterite pidió it's the imperfect subjunctive: llamara. The indicative (llamaba, llamó) would report information, and the conditional doesn't follow pedir que.

questions.stem: Complete the polite wish: "Me gustaría que ___ (tú) a mi presentación."
questions.explanation: A conditional main verb (me gustaría) works like a past one: it takes the imperfect subjunctive, vinieras. Gustar que always needs a subjunctive, so the indicative (venías, vienes) and the conditional (vendrías) are wrong.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "He told me to call him"?
choices: Me dijo que lo había llamado.
questions.explanation: Decir que + subjunctive reports an instruction: Me dijo que lo llamara. With the indicative it reports information: lo llamaba (he was calling him), lo había llamado (he had called him), lo llamaría (he would call him).

questions.stem: Complete: "Era imposible que ___ el informe en un día."
questions.explanation: Es imposible que always takes the subjunctive; with the main verb in the past (era), it's the imperfect subjunctive: termináramos (terminaron → terminá- + -ramos).

questions.stem: Complete: "El gerente salió de la oficina sin que nadie lo ___."
questions.explanation: Sin que always takes the subjunctive; after a past main verb (salió) it's the imperfect subjunctive: viera (from vieron). He left without anyone seeing him.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si no entrego el informe antes de la ___, mi supervisora se va a enojar."
questions.explanation: La fecha límite is the deadline. La renuncia is a resignation, la puntualidad punctuality and la productividad productivity; none of them is a point in time you hand something in before.

questions.stem: Read the message: "Equipo: la gerente pidió que mañana todos llegáramos a las 8. Quiere que preparemos juntos la presentación para el cliente. — Toño" What does the manager want?
choices: Everyone to arrive at 8 tomorrow and prepare the presentation together.
Toño to give the presentation alone.
The team to stay late tonight.
Everyone to arrive at 8 every day from now on.
questions.explanation: Pidió que mañana todos llegáramos a las 8 (a past request, imperfect subjunctive) and quiere que preparemos juntos la presentación (a current wish, present subjunctive). It's about tomorrow only, and the whole team prepares the presentation.

questions.stem: Last week the manager said: "Revisa las gráficas." You did it right away. Report it: "La gerente me pidió que ___ las gráficas."
questions.explanation: A command reported after a past verb becomes an imperfect subjunctive: revisaron → revisara (or revisase). Las gráficas = the charts.

questions.stem: Complete with the imperfect subjunctive of llegar: "Me gustaría que ustedes ___ puntuales a la junta."
questions.explanation: Me gustaría (conditional) + que + imperfect subjunctive: llegaron → llegaran (or llegasen). The spelling change of llegué affects only the yo preterite, not the imperfect subjunctive. (After me gustaría you will also hear the present, lleguen, especially in Latin America; the RAE doesn't call it wrong, but the imperfect subjunctive is the usual choice.)

questions.stem: Label the numbered parts of the office.

image.alt: An office with five numbered parts: a calendar on a whiteboard with the 20th circled in red, a woman pointing at it, a bound report with a bar chart, a sticky note on a monitor that says ¡No olvides!, and a desk.

questions.explanation: 1 la fecha límite (the date circled on the calendar), 2 la gerente (the manager presenting at the board), 3 el informe (the bound report with a chart), 4 el recordatorio (the sticky note: ¡No olvides! = Don't forget!), 5 el escritorio (the desk). La renuncia (resignation) and las horas extra (overtime) aren't objects in the picture.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: My boss wanted me to finish the report.
questions.explanation: A past main verb (quería) + que + imperfect subjunctive: Mi jefa quería que terminara el informe. The present subjunctive termine follows a present main verb (quiere que termine).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'd like you to help me with the presentation.
questions.explanation: Me gustaría (conditional) + que + imperfect subjunctive: Me gustaría que me ayudaras con la presentación. The conditional ayudarías can't follow que here.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Le molestó que no lo invitan.
questions.explanation: After a past main verb, the subjunctive is imperfect: vinieras, ayudaras, llegáramos. Le molestó que needs a subjunctive (invitaran), and querer que never takes the indicative (vienes → vinieras).

questions.stem: Last week Ana said: "Llegaré tarde a la boda." The wedding was on Saturday. Report it today: "Ana dijo que ___ tarde a la boda."
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb, a future becomes a conditional: llegaré → llegaría. Llegará would only fit if the wedding were still ahead; llegara and llegue are subjunctives, used for reported commands, not statements.

questions.stem: Beto told you: "Perdí las llaves." Report it: "Beto me dijo que ___ las llaves."
questions.explanation: A preterite usually becomes a pluperfect in reported speech: había perdido. (Me dijo que perdió las llaves is also common, but it's not among the choices.) Perdería would report a future, and the subjunctives would report a command.

questions.stem: On Monday Carla said to you: "Te veo mañana." On Friday you report it: "Carla me dijo que me veía ___."
questions.explanation: In a report made days later, mañana becomes al día siguiente (the next day). El día anterior replaces ayer, and ese día replaces hoy.

questions.stem: "¿Dónde trabajas?", me preguntó. → "Me preguntó ___."
questions.explanation: A reported question keeps the question word with its accent (dónde) and shifts the present to the imperfect: trabajaba. Si is only for yes/no questions, and trabajé changes the person and the meaning.

questions.stem: "¿Vas a la cena?", me preguntó mi hermana. → "Mi hermana me preguntó ___ a la cena."
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with si (whether), without an accent: me preguntó si iba. Sí (yes) has an accent; que iba turns it into a statement; cuándo asks a different question.

questions.stem: "No le digas a nadie", me pidió Beto. → "Beto me pidió que no le ___ a nadie."
questions.explanation: A reported command or request after a past verb takes the imperfect subjunctive: dijeron → dijera. The indicative and the conditional would report information, not a request.

questions.stem: Last year Ana told you: "Vivo en Puebla." She still lives there. Which report is NOT correct?
choices: Ana me dijo que vive en Puebla.
Ana me dijo que vivía en Puebla.
Ana me contó que vivía en Puebla.
Ana me dijo que viviera en Puebla.
questions.explanation: Both vive (still true now) and vivía (the usual shift) are correct reports of a statement. Viviera, a subjunctive, would turn it into an instruction: she told me to live in Puebla.

questions.stem: What do you call someone who loves telling everyone other people's private news?
questions.explanation: Un chismoso / una chismosa is a gossip (person). Un malentendido is a misunderstanding, un rumor a rumor, and una indirecta a dig or hint.

questions.stem: Read: "Por lo visto, Rubén renunció. Al parecer, el gerente le había prometido un aumento y nunca se lo dio. Pero eso es solo un rumor; Rubén no ha dicho nada." How sure is the speaker?
choices: Not sure: it's what people are saying.
Completely sure: Rubén told her himself.
Sure about the raise, but not about the resignation.
She says she made it up.
questions.explanation: Por lo visto and al parecer (apparently) report what you've heard without vouching for it, and she adds that it's only a rumor and that Rubén hasn't said anything.

questions.stem: Report it: "Voy a llegar tarde." → "Me dijo que ___ a llegar tarde."
questions.explanation: Ir a + infinitive shifts to the imperfect of ir: voy a llegar → iba a llegar.

questions.stem: "¿Por qué no me invitaste?" → "Me preguntó ___ no lo había invitado." (two words)
questions.explanation: A reported question keeps its question word, written as in the question: por qué, two words with an accent. Porque (one word, no accent) means because.

questions.stem: Match each original sentence to its report after dijo que.
questions.explanation: Present → imperfect (estaba), future → conditional (estaría), present perfect → pluperfect (había estado), command → imperfect subjunctive (descansara). Esté is a present subjunctive and reports nothing here.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: She told me she had bought the ring.
questions.explanation: "Compré el anillo" reported after a past verb: Me dijo que había comprado el anillo (pluperfect). Compraría would report a future ("I'll buy the ring").

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: He asked me where I lived.
questions.explanation: A question word stays in the report, with its accent, and the present shifts to the imperfect: Me preguntó dónde vivía. Si is only for yes/no questions.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si ___ que estabas enfermo, habría ido a verte."
questions.explanation: A condition that didn't happen in the past: si + pluperfect subjunctive (hubiera sabido; hubiese sabido is also correct). The conditional (habría sabido, sabría) never goes after si, and the indicative había sabido doesn't make it hypothetical.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si hubiéramos salido antes, no ___ el vuelo."
questions.explanation: The main clause of a past hypothetical takes the conditional perfect: habríamos perdido (we wouldn't have missed). In speech, hubiéramos perdido is also common. Habíamos perdido and perdimos are indicatives (they report what really happened), and hayamos perdido is a perfect subjunctive.

questions.stem: How do you say "If I had studied medicine, I'd be a doctor now"?
choices: Si estudiara medicina, ahora habría sido doctora.
Si había estudiado medicina, ahora sería doctora.
Si hubiera estudiado medicina, ahora habría sido doctora.
Si hubiera estudiado medicina, ahora sería doctora.
questions.explanation: A mixed condition: past cause (si + hubiera estudiado) and present result (ahora + conditional sería). Si estudiara is about now, si había estudiado uses the indicative, and ahora habría sido puts the result in the past while ahora says now.

questions.stem: How do you say "I wish I had studied more" (for last week's exam)?
questions.explanation: A regret about the past: ojalá + pluperfect subjunctive. Ojalá estudiara más is a wish about now (I wish I studied more), ojalá estudie más a hope (I hope I study more), and ojalá never takes the indicative (había).

questions.stem: What is true of "Si hubiera sabido, hubiera venido"?
choices: It's a mistake: the main clause must use habría.
It's very common in speech and accepted as an alternative to habría venido.
It means "If I knew, I would come".
questions.explanation: The -ra form hubiera is accepted in the main clause of a past hypothetical (= habría venido) and is everyday speech across the Spanish-speaking world, Mexico included. Habría is the safer choice in formal writing. The sentence is about the past: If I had known, I would have come.

questions.stem: What does "Por poco me caigo en la escalera" mean?
choices: I fell a little on the stairs.
I'm about to fall on the stairs.
I nearly fell on the stairs.
I almost always fall on the stairs.
questions.explanation: Por poco (almost, nearly) usually takes the present for a near miss in the past: Por poco me caigo = I nearly fell. It doesn't describe a habit or something about to happen.

questions.stem: What does "De haberlo sabido, no habría venido" mean?
choices: Since I knew it, I didn't come.
Having known it, I came anyway.
If I find out, I won't come.
Had I known, I wouldn't have come.
questions.explanation: De + haber + participle replaces a si clause about the past: de haberlo sabido = si lo hubiera sabido (had I known). The main clause is a conditional perfect: no habría venido.

questions.stem: Read: "Por poco perdemos el tren. Si no hubiera llovido, habríamos llegado temprano a la estación." What happened?
choices: It rained, and they nearly missed the train but caught it.
They missed the train because of the rain.
It didn't rain, so they arrived early.
They arrived early and waited for the train.
questions.explanation: Por poco perdemos = we nearly missed (so they caught it). Si no hubiera llovido… is contrary to fact: it did rain, and they didn't arrive early.

questions.stem: How do you say "I dialed the wrong number"?
questions.explanation: Equivocarse de + noun = to get the wrong one: Me equivoqué de número, de camión, de casa. The verb is pronominal (me equivoqué) and takes de, not a direct object or con.

questions.stem: Complete with haber: "Si me lo ___ dicho, te habría ayudado."
questions.explanation: Si + pluperfect subjunctive: hubieras (or hubieses) + dicho, with the pronouns me lo before hubieras. If you had told me, I would have helped you.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to its meaning.
left: Si hubiera tenido tiempo, te habría ayudado.
Si hubiera tenido tiempo, ahora estaría descansando.
choices: If I had time (now), I'd help you.
If I'd had time (then), I would have helped you.
If I'd had time (then), I'd be resting now.
If I have time, I'll help you.
If I have had time, I help you.
questions.explanation: Si + present: a real condition. Si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional: unreal now. Si + pluperfect subjunctive + conditional perfect: unreal in the past. Si + pluperfect subjunctive + conditional: a mixed condition, past cause with a present result.

questions.stem: Which sentences mean "If I had known, I would have come"? Select all that apply.
choices: Si lo hubiera sabido, habría venido.
Si lo hubiera sabido, hubiera venido.
Si lo habría sabido, habría venido.
questions.explanation: Hubiera… habría is the standard pattern, hubiera… hubiera is the common spoken one, and de haberlo sabido replaces the si clause. Si never takes the conditional (habría sabido), and vendría makes a mixed sentence about now (I'd come).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: If you had told me, I would have helped you.
questions.explanation: Si + pluperfect subjunctive (me lo hubieras dicho) and the conditional perfect in the main clause (te habría ayudado). Either clause can come first (in writing, put a comma after a si clause that comes first). Habrías dicho, a conditional, can't follow si.

questions.stem: When was Thomas More's Utopia first published?
questions.explanation: More published Utopia, in Latin, in 1516; it was first printed in Leuven. 1932 is Huxley's Brave New World (Un mundo feliz) and 1949 is Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four.

questions.stem: How is the name Utopia usually explained?
choices: From the name of a real island near England.
From Greek: "no place", which also sounds like "good place".
questions.explanation: The usual explanation is Greek "no place" (ou-topia), which sounds like eu-topia, "good place". That double meaning is why a utopia is both ideal and impossible.

questions.stem: Which novel from 1932 is a famous dystopia, known in Spanish as Un mundo feliz?
questions.explanation: Un mundo feliz is the Spanish title of Huxley's Brave New World (1932). Orwell's dystopia is from 1949 (1984 in Spanish), and More's Utopia (1516) describes an ideal society, not a dystopia.

questions.stem: Complete: "Para el año 2200 ___ tres planetas más." (we will have colonized)
questions.explanation: Something finished before a future date takes the future perfect: habremos colonizado (lesson 11). Habríamos colonizado means we would have colonized; the subjunctives don't fit a statement.

questions.stem: In the lesson's story, the grandmother says: "Si la gente supiera la verdad, Esperanza no duraría ni un año." What does she mean?
choices: She is sure the colony will end within a year.
She wants Ixchel to tell everyone the truth.
People don't know the truth; if they did, the colony would fall apart.
People found out the truth a year ago.
questions.explanation: Si + imperfect subjunctive (supiera) + conditional (no duraría) is contrary to fact now: people don't know. It's a warning about what would happen, not a prediction or a request.

questions.stem: Complete: "El androide hablaba como si ___ humano."
questions.explanation: Como si always takes the imperfect subjunctive for the same time as the main verb: como si fuera humano (as if it were human), even after a past main verb.

questions.stem: Which question is correct?
choices: ¿Qué pasaría si los robots tendrían sentimientos?
¿Qué pasaría si los robots tuvieran sentimientos?
¿Qué pasa si los robots tuvieran sentimientos?
¿Qué pasaría si los robots tengan sentimientos?
questions.explanation: Si + imperfect subjunctive (tuvieran) with the conditional in the main clause (pasaría). The conditional and the present subjunctive never follow si, and a present (pasa) in the main clause doesn't match an imperfect subjunctive after si.

questions.stem: What is a robot shaped like a person called?
questions.explanation: Un androide is a humanlike robot. Un clon is a genetic copy of a living being, un genio a genie or genius, and un ciudadano a citizen.

questions.stem: What are the plurals of el robot and el clon?
questions.explanation: Robot is a loanword ending in t and takes -s: los robots. Clon ends in n like most Spanish nouns and takes -es: los clones.

questions.stem: Complete with the conditional of ser: "¿Cómo ___ el mundo si nadie tuviera que trabajar?"
questions.explanation: The main clause of a hypothetical takes the conditional: sería (what would the world be like). The si clause has the imperfect subjunctive tuviera.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: La supervivencia is the noun of sobrevivir. Humanity is la humanidad, which isn't on the left.

questions.stem: Put the events of the lesson's story in order.
choices: Ixchel finds a hidden staircase while looking for her cat.
She tells her grandmother what she saw.
She decides to go back and open the door for the clones.
questions.explanation: The grandparents left in 2089; Ixchel was born in the colony; looking for her cat she found the factory of clones; that night she told her grandmother; at the end she decides to go back the next day.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: If robots did all the work, we would have more free time.
questions.explanation: Si + imperfect subjunctive (hicieran) and the conditional in the main clause (tendríamos). Either clause can come first (in writing, with a comma after a si clause that comes first). Harían, a conditional, can't follow si.

questions.stem: Even if it rains tomorrow (nobody knows yet), we're going to the beach. "Aunque ___ mañana, vamos a la playa."
questions.explanation: Nobody knows whether it will rain, and it makes no difference: that is aunque + subjunctive, "even if". "Llueve" or "lloverá" would present the rain as a fact you are announcing (a forecast you trust), which is not what the English says. "Llovería" is a conditional and never follows aunque in this kind of sentence.

questions.stem: What does "Aunque sea caro, lo voy a comprar" mean?
choices: I'm buying it only if it turns out to be cheap.
I'm buying it because it's expensive.
It may well be expensive, but that doesn't matter: I'm buying it.
It was expensive, so I didn't buy it.
questions.explanation: Aunque + subjunctive concedes a point and waves it away: expensive or not, I'm buying it. It is not a condition ("only if it's cheap"), not a cause (that would be porque or como) and not past.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: A pesar de la sequía, hubo agua en la ciudad.
A pesar de que la sequía, hubo agua en la ciudad.
A pesar la sequía, hubo agua en la ciudad.
Aunque la sequía, hubo agua en la ciudad.
questions.explanation: A pesar de takes a noun directly: a pesar de la sequía. "A pesar de que" and "aunque" need a whole clause with a verb (a pesar de que hubo sequía), and "a pesar" without de is incomplete.

questions.stem: Emissions went up; as a result, the temperature rose. "Las emisiones aumentaron; ___, la temperatura subió."
questions.explanation: Por consiguiente (formal) introduces a consequence, after a semicolon and followed by a comma. "Ya que" gives a cause, so it would make the rising temperature the reason for the emissions. "Aunque" and "a pesar de" concede; they don't give a result.

questions.stem: What does "Explícalo despacio, de modo que todos lo entiendan" mean?
choices: Explain it slowly, because everyone understands it.
Explain it slowly, so that everyone understands it.
Explain it slowly, although everyone understands it.
You explained it slowly, so everyone understood it.
questions.explanation: De modo que + subjunctive (entiendan) gives a purpose: "so that". With the indicative it would give a result: Lo explicó despacio, de modo que todos lo entendieron (so everyone understood). It never means "because" or "although".

questions.stem: Read: "Dado que en mi colonia solo hay agua tres días a la semana, compramos un tinaco. Aun así, a veces no alcanza, de modo que también guardamos agua de lluvia." (el tinaco = rooftop water tank) Why did the family buy a tinaco?
choices: Because the tinaco was on sale.
Because their neighborhood only has water three days a week.
Because they use very little water.
questions.explanation: Dado que (given that) gives the reason: the water only comes three days a week. "Aun así" (even so) adds that the tank sometimes isn't enough, and "de modo que" + indicative gives the result: they also save rainwater.

questions.stem: Which of these can be followed directly by a noun, with no que (for example, "___ la lluvia")? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Debido a, a causa de and a pesar de are followed by a noun: debido a la lluvia, a causa de la lluvia, a pesar de la lluvia. Ya que and puesto que are conjunctions: they need a clause with a verb (ya que llueve, puesto que llueve).

questions.stem: Complete with the yo preterite of provocar: "Sin querer, ___ un accidente en la cocina."
questions.explanation: Provocar changes c to qu before e: provoqué (like busqué, toqué). Provocó is the él/ella form.

questions.stem: Complete so that it means "Despite the rain, we went out": "___ la lluvia, salimos."
questions.explanation: A pesar de + a noun: A pesar de la lluvia, salimos. (A causa de or debido a would mean "because of", which changes the meaning.) Pese a (formal) means the same and is accepted.

questions.stem: Match each connector to the relation it shows.
questions.explanation: Ya que gives a known reason (cause); por lo tanto introduces a result (consequence); aunque admits a point that doesn't change the main idea (concession); de modo que with the subjunctive means "so that" (purpose). Condition would be si, siempre que or a menos que (lesson 18).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Expensive or not, it's worth it.
questions.explanation: "Aunque sea caro, vale la pena": aunque + subjunctive waves the price away (expensive or not). The aunque clause can also come second: "Vale la pena aunque sea caro." "Por eso" (that's why) would make the price the reason, and "ser" is not a conjugated form.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Seeing as we have time, let's walk.
questions.explanation: "Ya que tenemos tiempo, vamos caminando": ya que gives a reason both speakers accept and takes the indicative (tenemos, not tengamos). It can come first, like como, or after the main clause: "Vamos caminando, ya que tenemos tiempo."

questions.stem: Put the chain of causes from the lesson in order, from the first cause to the last consequence.
choices: Hay más sequías e incendios forestales.
questions.explanation: Burning fossil fuels raises emissions; more emissions warm the planet; warming brings more droughts and forest fires; and these destroy ecosystems and species.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses aunque to tell the listener a fact as news?
choices: Aunque está lloviendo, el partido sigue.
questions.explanation: The indicative (está lloviendo) presents a fact the speaker asserts: it is raining, and the game goes on. "Aunque llueva" is a possibility (even if), "aunque tuviera" an unlikely case, and "aunque sea difícil" waves a fact away; all three use the subjunctive.

questions.stem: Don't sign the contract unless you understand all the clauses. "No firmes el contrato a menos que ___ todas las cláusulas."
questions.explanation: A menos que (unless) always takes the subjunctive: entiendas. The indicative, the future and the conditional are never used after it.

questions.stem: What does "Siempre que voy al banco, hay una fila enorme" mean?
choices: As long as I go to the bank, there's a huge line.
Whenever I go to the bank, there's a huge line.
Unless I go to the bank, there's a huge line.
I always went to the bank when there was a huge line.
questions.explanation: Siempre que + indicative (voy) describes a habit: "whenever". With the subjunctive it would set a condition: siempre que vayas = as long as you go. "Unless" is a menos que, and the sentence is in the present.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT correct?
choices: Si pagas a tiempo, no hay recargo.
Siempre que pagues a tiempo, no hay recargo.
Si pagues a tiempo, no hay recargo.
Mientras pagues a tiempo, no hay recargo.
questions.explanation: Si never takes the present subjunctive: Si pagas a tiempo. Siempre que and mientras, on the other hand, take the subjunctive when they mean "as long as", so the other three sentences are all correct.

questions.stem: Choose the correct sign: "En caso de ___, llame al 911."
questions.explanation: En caso de + a noun: en caso de emergencia. With a clause you need que + subjunctive: en caso de que haya una emergencia. "Que hay" is indicative, and "que emergencia" has no verb.

questions.stem: The bank gave me the loan provided that I had a guarantor. "El banco me dio el préstamo con tal de que ___ un aval."
questions.explanation: After a past main verb (me dio), the subjunctive moves into the imperfect subjunctive: con tal de que tuviera (or tuviese). "Tenga" would follow a present verb (El banco me da el préstamo con tal de que tenga…); the indicative and the conditional never follow con tal de que.

questions.stem: A rental contract says: "El inquilino podrá tener mascotas siempre y cuando no causen daños." What does it mean?
choices: The tenant may never keep pets.
The tenant must pay for any damage in advance.
The tenant may keep pets as long as they don't cause damage.
The tenant may keep pets whenever the landlord is away.
questions.explanation: Siempre y cuando + subjunctive = as long as: pets are allowed on condition that they cause no damage (daños). Podrá is the future of poder, used in contracts for what is allowed.

questions.stem: Which of these always take the subjunctive when they set a condition? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Con tal de que, a menos que and en caso de que always take the subjunctive. Solo si and excepto si are built on si, so they follow its rules: the indicative (or the imperfect subjunctive for an unlikely case), never the present subjunctive.

questions.stem: Complete with the right form of devolver (tú): "Te presto mi carro con tal de que me lo ___ el lunes."
questions.explanation: Con tal de que + present subjunctive. Devolver is an o → ue verb: devuelvo → devuelva, devuelvas.

questions.stem: Write a Spanish conjunction meaning "unless" that takes the subjunctive.
questions.explanation: A menos que is the most common; a no ser que and salvo que (more formal) mean the same, and all take the subjunctive: No voy a menos que me inviten.

questions.stem: Name the hidden rows of this credit card statement.

image.alt: The credit card statement from the lesson with five row names hidden and numbered. 1: 17,450.00 MXN. 2: 845.00 MXN. A visible row reads Pago para no generar intereses 6,200.00 MXN. 3: 5 de diciembre de 2026. 4: 312.40 MXN. In the box Compras a meses sin intereses, Laptop: 5, followed by 3 de 12, 1,250.00 MXN.

questions.explanation: 1 is the balance at the closing date (saldo al corte), the largest amount. 2 is the minimum payment (pago mínimo). 3 is a date: the payment deadline (fecha límite de pago). 4 is the interest charged for the period (intereses del periodo). 5 is "mensualidad 3 de 12": the third of twelve monthly payments.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'll lend you the money provided that you pay me back on payday.
questions.explanation: "Te presto el dinero con tal de que me lo devuelvas en la quincena": con tal de que always takes the subjunctive (devuelvas, not devuelves). The condition can also come first, and "en la quincena" can go before the verb.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: You can use my card as long as you let me know.
questions.explanation: "Puedes usar mi tarjeta siempre que me avises": siempre que + subjunctive sets a condition (as long as). It can also open the sentence: "Siempre que me avises, puedes usar mi tarjeta." The conditional never follows siempre que.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: El saldo is the balance (in Mexico also phone credit); la mensualidad is one monthly payment; la quincena is a fifteen-day period and, in Mexico, the payday that comes with it; la estafa is a scam; el seguro (noun) is insurance. Savings are los ahorros.

questions.stem: "Es evidente que las redes ___ a los jóvenes."
questions.explanation: Es evidente que states a certainty, so it takes the indicative: distraen. The subjunctive (distraigan) follows denial or judgment (no es verdad que, me parece mal que), and the infinitive can't follow que here.

questions.stem: "Me parece injusto que ___ los celulares en las escuelas."
questions.explanation: Me parece + an adjective (injusto) + que judges something, so it takes the subjunctive: prohíban. Compare me parece que + indicative, which only gives an opinion about what is true. Prohibir keeps its written accent on the í: prohíban.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Me parece bien que tienes razón.
Me parece bien que tener razón.
questions.explanation: Me parece que (I think that) gives an opinion about what is true and takes the indicative: tienes razón. Me parece bien que judges something and takes the subjunctive (Me parece bien que vengas); it can't be followed by the indicative or by que + infinitive.

questions.stem: "Mi hermano publica todo en redes; yo, ___, cuido mucho mi privacidad."
questions.explanation: En cambio sets two things side by side in contrast: my brother posts everything, whereas I… Además and asimismo add a similar point, and en primer lugar opens a list.

questions.stem: "Muchos padres están en contra ___ los niños tengan redes sociales."
questions.explanation: Estar en contra de + que + subjunctive: en contra de que los niños tengan… The de stays; "en contra de" alone would need a noun or an infinitive (en contra de las redes).

questions.stem: In the lesson's forum post, what condition does the mother set for her daughter?
choices: The account must be private, and she must not accept followers she doesn't know.
She may use it only on weekends.
She must share her password with her mother.
She must not post any photos.
questions.explanation: The post says: "puede usarla, siempre que la cuenta sea privada y no acepte seguidores que no conozca." Siempre que + subjunctive sets the condition (lesson 18).

questions.stem: Put the sentences of this opinion composition in order.
choices: Desde mi punto de vista, lo mejor es limitar los celulares, pero no prohibirlos.
En primer lugar, es evidente que el celular distrae a los alumnos.
No obstante, el celular también tiene ventajas.
En definitiva, no creo que la solución sea prohibir.
questions.explanation: The introduction states the position (desde mi punto de vista); the first argument opens with en primer lugar; no obstante turns to the other side; en definitiva concludes.

questions.stem: Match each discourse marker to its job in a text.
questions.explanation: En primer lugar opens the list; asimismo (likewise) adds a point; no obstante (nevertheless) contrasts; en resumen sums up. Causes are given with porque, ya que or puesto que (lesson 17).

questions.stem: Which of these are followed by the subjunctive? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Judgments (me parece lógico que, es necesario que) and denials (no es verdad que) take the subjunctive. Es evidente que and está claro que state a certainty and take the indicative.

questions.stem: Complete with the right form of defender: "Es normal que cada persona ___ su postura."
questions.explanation: Es normal que + subjunctive. Defender changes e → ie in the stressed syllable: defiendo → defienda (but defendamos).

questions.stem: Write the Spanish for "on the one hand", the phrase that pairs with "por otro".
questions.explanation: Por un lado… por otro (lado). Por una parte… por otra (parte) means the same.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'm in favor of limiting screen time.
questions.explanation: "Estoy a favor de limitar el tiempo de pantalla": a favor de + infinitive. "Que" would need a new subject and the subjunctive (a favor de que limiten…).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: From my point of view, the problem isn't technology.
questions.explanation: "Desde mi punto de vista, el problema no es la tecnología." The opinion phrase can open or close the sentence or sit after the subject, and with ser the two noun phrases can swap (la tecnología no es el problema). "Sea" is a subjunctive with nothing to trigger it.

questions.stem: "Le agradecería que me ___ la factura a la mayor brevedad."
questions.explanation: Agradecería is a conditional, so in a formal letter the verb after que goes into the imperfect subjunctive: enviara (or enviase). (The present subjunctive, envíe, is also common in Latin America, but it is not offered here.) The indicative (envía) and the conditional (enviaría) can't follow it, and que needs a conjugated verb, not an infinitive.

questions.stem: Which is the standard way to open a formal letter in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Spanish letters put a colon after the greeting: Estimados señores: A comma there is an English habit. Querido is for people you know (and would have to agree: queridos), and ¿Qué onda? is informal.

questions.stem: Your boss, whom you have always addressed as usted, says: "Háblame de tú, por favor." What is the most natural reply?
choices: Claro, con mucho gusto. ¿Cómo está usted?
questions.explanation: Your boss has invited you to use tú, so you switch at once: ¿Cómo estás? Staying with usted after the invitation can sound cold. ¿Mande? asks someone to repeat, and Disculpe las molestias apologizes for trouble.

questions.stem: In a Mexican office, a colleague calls your name from the next desk. A polite answer is:
questions.explanation: ¿Mande? is the polite Mexican answer when someone calls you or when you didn't catch something. ¿Qué quieres? sounds abrupt; ¡Provecho! is for people eating; con permiso is for passing or leaving.

questions.stem: Which line does NOT belong in a formal complaint?
choices: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.
Por medio de la presente, presento una reclamación.
Le agradecería que me respondiera a la mayor brevedad.
questions.explanation: ¿Qué onda? is informal Mexican Spanish ("what's up?"): it breaks the register of a formal letter. The other three are standard formal formulas.

questions.stem: In the lesson, what does Mariana ask the store to do?
choices: Send a technician to her house.
Give her a discount on her next order.
Replace the blender with a new one or refund the full amount.
questions.explanation: She writes: "les agradecería que me lo cambiaran por uno nuevo o que me devolvieran el importe total." The 48 hours was the store's own promise on the phone, which they didn't keep.

questions.stem: Put the parts of this formal complaint in order.
choices: Me dirijo a ustedes para presentar una reclamación por una licuadora defectuosa.
El aparato llegó el 6 de octubre y desde el primer día se apaga solo.
Les agradecería que me lo cambiaran por uno nuevo.
Quedo a la espera de su respuesta. Atentamente,
questions.explanation: Greeting, purpose (me dirijo a ustedes para…), the facts with dates, the request (les agradecería que…), and the closing.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this e-mail.

image.alt: The formal e-mail from the lesson with five numbered markers. 1 is on the line De: mariana.leon@correo.example. 2 is on the line Para: atencion@casa-aurora.example. 3 is on the line Asunto: Reclamación por licuadora defectuosa, pedido 58213. 4 is beside the paperclip and the file factura-58213.pdf. 5 is beside the name Mariana León Ruiz at the end of the message.

questions.explanation: De: (from) is the sender, el remitente; Para: (to) is the recipient, el destinatario; the subject line is el asunto; the attached PDF is el archivo adjunto; the name at the end is la firma.

questions.stem: Complete with the imperfect subjunctive of cambiar (ustedes): "Les agradecería que me lo ___ por uno nuevo."
questions.explanation: After the conditional agradecería, the imperfect subjunctive: cambiaron → cambiaran (or the -se form, cambiasen).

questions.stem: Write the formal opening that means "To whom it may concern".
questions.explanation: A quien corresponda: is used when you don't know the recipient's name, followed by a colon.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Una constancia proves a fact (una constancia de estudios); el expediente is the file of a case; el remitente sends the letter; las molestias is the trouble caused (Disculpe las molestias). A warranty is la garantía (A2).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I am writing to you to file a complaint.
questions.explanation: "Me dirijo a ustedes para presentar una reclamación": dirigirse a = to address, write to; para + infinitive gives the purpose; presentar here means to file or submit. The purpose can also come first: "Para presentar una reclamación, me dirijo a ustedes."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I would be grateful if you sent me the invoice. (usted)
questions.explanation: "Le agradecería que me enviara la factura": the conditional agradecería is followed by the imperfect subjunctive in formal writing. "Me envía" is the present indicative, which can't follow it.

questions.stem: "Perdone que lo ___, pero no estoy de acuerdo."
questions.explanation: Perdonar que reacts to something, like the emotion verbs, and takes the subjunctive: perdone que lo interrumpa. The indicative (interrumpo) is the classic mistake.

questions.stem: In a formal discussion, which is the most polite way to disagree?
choices: Yo lo veo de otra manera.
Usted no sabe de lo que habla.
questions.explanation: Yo lo veo de otra manera (I see it differently) disagrees with the idea, not the person. The other three attack the speaker.

questions.stem: "Tiene razón ___ el agua es cara, pero hay que cuidarla."
questions.explanation: Tener razón en que + indicative: you accept a fact before you answer it. The preposition en is needed.

questions.stem: "Ayer, en la reunión, yo ___ dos veces." (intervenir)
questions.explanation: Intervenir is conjugated like venir: vine → intervine. "Intervení" follows the regular pattern by mistake, intervino is the él/ella form, and intervengo is the present.

questions.stem: "No es que el plan ___ malo, sino que es caro."
questions.explanation: No es que + subjunctive rejects a reading that you don't accept; sino que + indicative gives the real point: No es que sea malo, sino que es caro.

questions.stem: In the radio roundtable, why does Paola Méndez interrupt the engineer?
choices: She owns a laundromat that uses a lot of water.
She thinks water should be free for everyone.
Her neighborhood gets water only three days a week: the problem is supply, not how much people use.
She wants the program to end early.
questions.explanation: She says: "en mi colonia hay agua solo tres días a la semana. No es que gastemos mucho, sino que no llega." The laundromat belongs to Javier Cruz.

questions.stem: What consensus does the roundtable reach?
choices: A higher rate for high household use, together with a plan to fix leaks.
questions.explanation: The engineer sums up: "tarifa más alta para el consumo alto de los hogares, y al mismo tiempo, un plan para las fugas", and Paola accepts it con tal de que the leak plan starts this year.

questions.stem: What does the moderator mean by "por cuestión de tiempo"?
questions.explanation: Por cuestión de tiempo = for reasons of time: the moderator needs to move on. El tiempo can also mean the weather, but not in this phrase.

questions.stem: Put the moves of a polite disagreement in order.
choices: …y tiene razón en que el plan es ambicioso…
…pero yo lo veo de otra manera, ya que es muy caro.
questions.explanation: Show you listened, concede part of the point, counter with pero and a reason, and give the turn back.

questions.stem: Match each phrase to what it does in a discussion.
questions.explanation: Quisiera intervenir asks for the floor; permítame terminar holds it; volviendo al tema brings the talk back; habría que matizar accepts a point with a limit.

questions.stem: Complete with the yo preterite of matizar: "Ayer ___ lo que había dicho en la reunión."
questions.explanation: Matizar changes z to c before e: maticé (like empecé). Matizó is the él/ella form.

questions.stem: Which of these concede part of the other person's point? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Es cierto que, le concedo que and reconozco que all admit something before the answer. Discrepo de usted disagrees outright, and permítame terminar keeps your turn.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: If you'll allow me, I'd like to say something. (usted; use intervenir)
questions.explanation: "Si me permite, quisiera intervenir": quisiera (lesson 13) softens the request, and intervenir means to speak in a discussion. The si clause can also come last.

questions.stem: "Mi pasaporte ya no sirve: está ___."
questions.explanation: Vencido = expired. Vigente is the opposite (valid), renovado means it has just been renewed, and certificado describes a certified copy.

questions.stem: "Para el trámite necesito el acta de nacimiento ___."
questions.explanation: Acta is feminine: it takes el only because it begins with a stressed a (like el agua). Adjectives agree in the feminine: el acta certificada, las actas certificadas.

questions.stem: A list says: "Comprobante de domicilio con antigüedad no mayor a tres meses." It is 10 November. Which document works?
choices: An electricity bill issued in June
A phone bill from last year
A water bill issued in September
questions.explanation: Antigüedad no mayor a tres meses = no more than three months old: a September bill is fine in November, a June bill is too old, and a card is not a bill with your address.

questions.stem: The official asks: "¿Me permite su folio?" What does she want?
questions.explanation: El folio is the reference number of your procedure. ¿Me permite…? is a very polite way to ask for something.

questions.stem: In the lesson, why does Diego need his documents by 15 December?
choices: To enroll in a new degree
questions.explanation: He writes: "Necesito estos documentos para un proceso de contratación en el extranjero, cuya fecha límite es el 15 de diciembre."

questions.stem: What does "No se aceptan documentos con tachaduras" mean?
choices: Documents with crossings-out are not accepted.
Crossed-out documents are returned by mail.
questions.explanation: No se aceptan = are not accepted (se with a plural verb); la tachadura = a crossing-out.

questions.stem: In the lesson, why did the official refuse Diego's passport?
choices: He had forgotten his reference number.
questions.explanation: She says: "este pasaporte está vencido desde agosto", so he shows his INE card instead, which is valid (vigente).

questions.stem: Name the numbered documents.

image.alt: The five documents from the lesson without labels, numbered. 1: a green ID card with a photo and the line Vigencia 2034. 2: an electricity bill with a name, an address, a meter reading and a total of 412 MXN. 3: a page headed Estados Unidos Mexicanos with a name, date and place of birth and the parents. 4: a gray photocopy with a round stamp and the words Certifico que es copia fiel de su original. 5: a small slip headed Su número with 2026-118-04573 and Conserve este papel.

questions.explanation: 1 is an ID card with a validity date (la credencial). 2 is a utility bill with an address, the usual proof of address. 3 records a birth (el acta de nacimiento). 4 is a copy certified as faithful to the original. 5 is the reference number to keep.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: A document is vigente during its vigencia; then it is vencido, and you have to renovar it. To sign is firmar (A1).

questions.stem: Complete with the present subjunctive of renovar (tú): "Es importante que ___ tu pasaporte antes del viaje."
questions.explanation: Renovar changes o → ue in the stressed syllable: renuevo → renueve, renueves (but renovemos).

questions.stem: Write the Spanish for "proof of address" (with its article).
questions.explanation: El comprobante de domicilio: usually a recent water, electricity, gas or phone bill.

questions.stem: Which of these are official photo IDs in Mexico? Select all that apply.
choices: la credencial para votar del INE
questions.explanation: The INE voter card and a valid passport are official IDs with a photo. An electricity bill is proof of address, and a birth certificate proves your birth and nationality but has no photo.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Expired documents are not accepted.
questions.explanation: "No se aceptan documentos vencidos": se + a plural verb agreeing with documentos. "Vigentes" would mean valid documents, the opposite.

questions.stem: "Un seguro de vida para que tu familia ___ tranquila."
questions.explanation: Para que always takes the subjunctive (lesson 06): para que tu familia esté tranquila. The infinitive would need the same subject (para estar tranquilo).

questions.stem: What is the plural of el eslogan?
questions.explanation: Eslogan adds -es in the plural, and the stress stays on the same syllable, so it needs a written accent: eslóganes (like examen → exámenes).

questions.stem: An ad says "Hasta 50 % de descuento". What does it promise?
choices: Up to 50 % off: many items may have less.
50 % off only if you pay in cash.
questions.explanation: Hasta = up to: 50 % is the maximum, not the minimum. Read the small print to see which items have it.

questions.stem: In the NubeLink ad, how much do you pay per month from the fourth month on?
questions.explanation: The small print says: "a partir del cuarto mes, 549 pesos al mes". 299 is only the promotional price for the first three months; 500 is the speed in megas.

questions.stem: At NubeLink's prices, how much do you pay in the first twelve months?
questions.explanation: Three months at 299 (897 pesos) plus nine months at 549 (4,941 pesos) = 5,838 pesos. 3,588 would be twelve months at 299, the price in big letters.

questions.stem: Which is the ellos preterite of atraer?
questions.explanation: Atraer follows traer: trajeron → atrajeron. After j, the ending is -eron, not -ieron; "atrayeron" mixes it up with verbs like leer (leyeron).

questions.stem: Which invented slogan plays on a double meaning?
choices: Gimnasio Fuerza: no es magia, es constancia.
Lavandería Burbuja: tu ropa, como nueva; tu tiempo, para ti.
Tortillería La Esquina: siempre calientitas, siempre a tiempo.
questions.explanation: La constancia means perseverance here, and it is also the word for an official certificate (lesson 20). The other slogans use parallel structure, repetition and a question.

questions.stem: "El anuncio era engañoso y muchos clientes fueron ___."
questions.explanation: Engañoso (misleading) describes the ad; engañado (deceived) is the participle that describes the customers: fueron engañados (they were deceived), agreeing in the plural.

questions.stem: Match each line of small print to its meaning.
left: Precios sujetos a cambio sin previo aviso.
questions.explanation: Agotar = to run out (existencias = stock); aplicar here = to apply; con fines ilustrativos = for illustrative purposes; sujeto a cambio = subject to change. Free shipping would be envío gratis.

questions.stem: In the Café Nube ad, which phrases contain a subjunctive? Select all that apply.
choices: para que cada taza sepa a recién hecho
siempre que traigas tu propio vaso
questions.explanation: Despierte (relative clause about a coffee you're looking for), sepa (after para que) and traigas (after siempre que, as long as) are subjunctives. Ven is a tú command, and tostamos is the present indicative.

questions.stem: Complete with the right form of comprar (tú): "Siempre que ___ dos, el tercero es gratis."
questions.explanation: Siempre que + subjunctive sets the condition of the offer: compres (comprar → compre, compres).

questions.stem: Write the Spanish for "the small print".
questions.explanation: La letra chica is the usual phrase in Mexico; Spain says la letra pequeña. Both are accepted.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Call us today so that an adviser can help you. (usted, to a man; el asesor = adviser)
questions.explanation: "Llámenos hoy para que un asesor lo atienda": a usted command with the pronoun attached (llámenos), and para que + subjunctive (atienda) because the subject changes. The subject can also follow the verb: "para que lo atienda un asesor".

questions.stem: Read the exchange. What does Beto ask? — Lupe: "¡Me gané un viaje a Cancún!" — Beto: "¿En serio? ¿No me estás tomando el pelo?"
questions.explanation: "Tomar el pelo" (literally "to take the hair") is an idiom: to pull someone's leg, to tease. Beto can't believe Lupe's news, so he asks if she's joking. Nothing to do with real hair: that's the trap of translating word for word.

questions.stem: Match each idiom to its meaning.
left: costar un ojo de la cara
choices: to put your foot in it
to be a piece of cake
questions.explanation: Literally: to put in the paw, to be eaten bread, to give the tin can, to be in the clouds, to cost an eye from the face. "To lend a hand" is "echar la mano" (Mexico) or "echar una mano", which isn't in the list.

questions.stem: Choose the right verb: "Llevo dos horas en el aeropuerto y no hay nada que hacer. ___ muy aburrido." (I've been at the airport for two hours with nothing to do.)
questions.explanation: The speaker feels bored right now, a state: "Estoy aburrido." "Soy aburrido" means "I'm a boring person", which isn't what the situation says. "Tengo" and "hay" don't go with "aburrido".

questions.stem: What does "Mi vecino es muy rico" mean?
questions.explanation: With "ser", "rico" said of a person means rich. "Estar rico" is tasty, and it's used for food ("¡Qué rico está el pozole!"), not to describe a neighbor's wealth.

questions.stem: Type the Mexican interjection that warns someone: "¡___, que viene un carro!" (Watch out, there's a car coming!)
questions.explanation: "¡Aguas!" is Mexico's informal "Watch out!": ¡Aguas con el escalón! (watch the step). You don't need to type the ¡ !.

questions.stem: Your friend in Mexico City tells you she has just won a scholarship. Which reactions fit? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "¡No manches!" (no way!) and "¡Órale, qué padre!" (wow, great!) react to surprising good news among friends. "¡Aguas!" is a warning (watch out) and "¡Qué oso!" means "how embarrassing", which don't fit.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Don't pull my leg. (to a friend)
questions.explanation: "No me tomes el pelo." Only the verb of an idiom changes: a negative tú command is the subjunctive (tomes, lesson 05), and the pronoun "me" goes before it. "Tomas" is the present indicative, which can't make a negative command.

questions.stem: Build the question in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Are you ready yet? (to a woman, tú)
questions.explanation: "¿Ya estás lista?" (also "¿Estás lista ya?" or "¿Estás ya lista?"). "Estar listo" = to be ready; "ser listo" = to be clever, so "¿Ya eres lista?" would ask something else entirely.

questions.stem: Each picture shows the literal meaning of an idiom. Choose the idiom for each numbered picture.

image.alt: Four numbered pictures: 1, a hand pulling a strand of a man's hair; 2, a woman whose head is hidden in clouds; 3, a price tag with an eye on it; 4, a dog's paw stepping into a cake.

choices: costar un ojo de la cara
questions.explanation: 1: taking the hair (tomar el pelo, to tease); 2: in the clouds (estar en las nubes, to daydream); 3: an eye on a price tag (costar un ojo de la cara, to cost a fortune); 4: a paw in the cake (meter la pata, to mess up).

questions.stem: In a job interview in Monterrey, the interviewer asks: "¿Podría empezar el lunes?" Which answer fits the situation best?
questions.explanation: A job interview calls for neutral, polite Spanish. "Güey", "¡No manches!" and "la neta" are informal Mexican words for friends; "güey" can even offend a stranger.

questions.stem: Complete: "Mi abuelo siempre cuenta el mismo ___, y todos nos reímos por cortesía."
questions.explanation: You tell ("contar") a chiste, a joke with a punch line. "Broma" is feminine (la broma: a prank or a joking remark), so it can't follow "el mismo"; "refranes" is plural; "pelo" makes no sense.

questions.stem: Complete: "Los plátanos todavía ___ verdes; mejor los comemos el fin de semana."
questions.explanation: "Estar verde" = to be unripe, a state that will change ("todavía", "el fin de semana"). Bananas aren't green by nature, so "son verdes" doesn't fit; "tienen" and "hay" don't work with an adjective here.

questions.stem: Choose the best translation: "When the teacher called on him, he went red."
choices: Cuando la maestra lo llamó, se puso rojo.
Cuando la maestra lo llamó, se hizo rojo.
Cuando la maestra lo llamó, se quedó rojo.
Cuando la maestra lo llamó, fue rojo.
questions.explanation: Blushing is sudden and temporary: "ponerse" + adjective. "Hacerse" is for changes reached by effort or time (se hizo médico), "quedarse" for the state left after an event, and "fue rojo" means "he was red" (or "it was red"), not a change.

questions.stem: Complete: "Mi prima estudió muchos años y ___ abogada."
questions.explanation: A profession reached by effort: "hacerse" (se hizo abogada; "llegó a ser abogada" would also work). "Ponerse" never takes a job; "volverse" is for a change in character; "quedarse" for the result of an event.

questions.stem: Complete: "Después del accidente, mi abuelo ___ ciego."
questions.explanation: The state someone is left in after an event, often a loss: "quedarse" + adjective (se quedó ciego = he went blind). "Convertirse" needs "en" + a noun; "ponerse" is for quick, temporary changes; "hacerse" for effort or time.

questions.stem: Complete: "La vieja fábrica de textiles ___ un museo."
questions.explanation: One thing turning into a different kind of thing: "convertirse en" + noun (lesson 22, and A2 honors). "Hacerse" takes no "en"; "ponerse" and "quedarse" take adjectives, not a noun like "un museo".

questions.stem: Complete the question: "¿___ quién cuentas para la mudanza?" (Who can you count on for the move?)
questions.explanation: "Contar con" = to count on. In a Spanish question the preposition goes first: ¿Con quién cuentas? English leaves it at the end ("who … on?"), Spanish can't.

questions.stem: Build the question in Spanish.
questions.prompt: What do you do for a living? (tú)
questions.explanation: "Dedicarse a" keeps its preposition at the front of the question: ¿A qué te dedicas? "¿De qué te dedicas?" is a common mistake: the verb takes "a".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Over the years, she became more patient.
questions.explanation: A lasting change in character: "volverse" + adjective. "Con los años" can go first or last. "Convertirse" needs "en" + a noun, so "se convirtió más paciente" isn't Spanish.

questions.stem: Choose the preposition each sentence needs.
left: Se trata ___ una historia de amor.
questions.explanation: atreverse a, fijarse en, contar con, burlarse de, tratarse de. "Por" goes with "interesarse por" (and "preocuparse por"), not with these.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Se puso nervioso antes del examen.
Se hizo vegetariano el año pasado.
Se puso médico después de seis años.
questions.explanation: A sudden mood takes "ponerse"; a change of belief or habit by choice takes "hacerse"; running out of something is "quedarse sin". A profession is never "ponerse": say "Se hizo médico" (or "Llegó a ser médico").

questions.stem: These pictures show events in Ernesto's life (from the interview in this lesson). Choose the phrase for each numbered picture.

image.alt: A timeline titled La vida de Ernesto with four numbered pictures above the years 1980, 2019, 2020 and 2022: a graduation cap, an empty cardboard box, a notebook and pencil, and a small flag in front of a cathedral.

questions.explanation: The cap is his graduation (se graduó, 1980); the empty box, the plant closing (se quedó sin trabajo, 2019, at sixty); the notebook, studying again (empezó de cero, 2020); the flag in the historic center, his new job (se hizo guía, 2022).

questions.stem: In a careful written review, which is the recommended way to say "The novel is about a family"?
choices: La novela se trata de una familia.
La novela trata de una familia.
La novela trata a una familia.
La novela se trata en una familia.
questions.explanation: The RAE's Diccionario panhispánico de dudas recommends "tratar de" without "se" when the book or film is the subject; "se trata de" has no subject (Se trata de una familia…). "La novela se trata de…" is very common in Latin American speech, but avoid it in careful writing. "Trata a una familia" means it treats a family (like a doctor).

questions.stem: Complete: "En las vacaciones comí muchísimo y ___ cuatro kilos."
questions.explanation: Eating a lot makes you gain weight: "engordar". "Adelgazar" is the opposite (to lose weight); "madurar" is to mature or ripen; "envejecer" to grow old. (In Mexico you'll also hear "subí cuatro kilos" or "subí de peso".)

questions.stem: According to the official DELE B1 guide, how long is the text in the first writing task (a reply to a short text)?
questions.explanation: Task 1 is a reply (an e-mail, letter, forum post or blog entry) of 100–120 words; task 2 is 130–150 words. 60–80 words is the DELE A2's range.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ayer fui al concierto. Me encantó que la cantante ___ una canción de su abuela."
questions.explanation: An emotion ("me encantó que") takes the subjunctive, and after a past main verb it's the imperfect subjunctive (lesson 15): "cantara" (also "cantase"). "Cantó" and "cantaba" are indicative; "cantará" is the future.

questions.stem: Complete: "Te recomiendo que la ___ en el cine; en la tele pierde mucho."
questions.explanation: A recommendation in the present ("te recomiendo que") takes the present subjunctive: "veas". "Ves" and "verás" are indicative; "vieras" would follow a past or conditional main verb (Te recomendé que la vieras).

questions.stem: Type the missing word: "El ___ de la película lo escribió la misma directora." (the script)
questions.explanation: "El guion" is the script. Since the RAE's 2010 spelling rules it's written without an accent: the RAE counts it as one syllable for spelling.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: "The script" is "el guion". Note "el escenario" is the stage in a theater, and "el reparto" also means delivery in other contexts.

questions.stem: This streaming page has lost its labels. Choose the word for each numbered part.

image.alt: A streaming page for the series Las hermanas del puerto. Numbered parts: 1, a date, viernes 13 de noviembre; 2, three actresses' names with small faces; 3, a CC symbol with español and inglés; 4, a play button and a musical note with 14 canciones; 5, a box with four stars and 120 opiniones de espectadores.

questions.explanation: The date is the release (el estreno); the names are the cast (el reparto); CC with two languages, the subtitles; the songs, the soundtrack (la banda sonora); the stars and viewers' opinions, the reviews (las reseñas, lesson 08).

questions.stem: Put the steps of this lesson's writing method in order.
choices: Read the task and underline every point
Choose tú or usted and the opening and closing
Plan one paragraph per idea, with a connector
Write, using your full range of tenses
Count the words and check agreement, accents and mood
questions.explanation: Read and underline, choose the register, plan, write, then count and check. Checking comes last, and planning before writing is what makes sure every point of the task is covered.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I recommend that you watch it. (the series, tú)
questions.explanation: "Te recomiendo que la veas." Recommending is influence: "que" + present subjunctive (veas). "La" (la serie) goes before the conjugated verb. "Ves" is indicative.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The ending was very predictable.
questions.explanation: "Previsible" = predictable. "Previsto" is the participle of "prever" (foreseen, planned): "el final fue muy previsto" isn't Spanish.

questions.stem: Complete: "No es una gran serie, pero es muy ___."
questions.explanation: The adjective agrees with "la serie" (feminine singular): entretenida. Checking agreement is the first of the three rereadings in "Editing your draft".

questions.stem: In Marina's e-mail (model text 2), why does she tell Andrés to buy tickets soon?
choices: Because they are cheaper this week.
questions.explanation: "Te recomiendo que compres los boletos pronto, porque se agotan rápido": they sell out quickly. The play will be repeated next weekend, so it isn't ending tomorrow, and the e-mail says nothing about prices or Lucía's request.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
questions.explanation: "Guion" has no accent (RAE 2010); the plural of "actriz" is "actrices" (z → c before e); "el público" is singular, so "aplaudió".

questions.stem: A candidate scores: reading 22, writing 20, listening 15, speaking 14 (25 points each). What is the result?
choices: Apto: every test has at least 10.
No apto: the total is under 75.
questions.explanation: Group 1 (reading + writing) = 42; group 2 (listening + speaking) = 29. Each group needs at least 30 of its 50 points, so 29 means "No apto", however high the total. There is no rule about 75 or about 10 per test.

questions.stem: Ana said: "Vivo en Puebla." She still lives there. Which report is NOT correct?
choices: Ana dijo que vive en Puebla.
Ana dijo que vivía en Puebla.
Ana dijo que viviera en Puebla.
Ana me contó que vive en Puebla.
questions.explanation: After "dijo que", a statement shifts to the imperfect (vivía), or keeps the present when it's still true (vive), lesson 16. "Viviera" is the subjunctive, used to report a command or request ("Vive en Puebla" → Me dijo que viviera en Puebla), not a statement of fact.

questions.stem: Which statements about the DELE B1 match the official guide? Select all that apply.
choices: Each recording in the listening test is played twice.
Wrong answers in the reading test lose points.
Any educated variety of Spanish is accepted in answers if it is used consistently.
The writing test has two tasks.
questions.explanation: Recordings are played twice; the writing test has two tasks (100–120 and 130–150 words); any educated norm used consistently is accepted. Wrong answers in reading and listening cost nothing, so answer every question.

questions.stem: Complete: "No creo que ___ tiempo para ir al cine hoy."
questions.explanation: A negated opinion (no creo que) takes the subjunctive: "tenga" (lesson 04). "Creo que tengo tiempo" would be the indicative for a belief.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si ___ más dinero, viajaría por toda Sudamérica."
questions.explanation: An unlikely or unreal condition now: si + imperfect subjunctive (tuviera, also tuviese) + conditional (viajaría), lesson 14. Never si + conditional (tendría) or si + present subjunctive (tenga); "Si tengo" would need "viajaré" or a present.

questions.stem: "Vendré mañana", dijo Ana. Complete the report: "Ana dijo que ___ al día siguiente."
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb, the future usually becomes the conditional: vendría (lesson 16). "Venía al día siguiente" is also correct: the imperfect of a present with future meaning ("Vengo mañana" → Dijo que venía al día siguiente).

questions.stem: Pablo told me: "Llámame." Report his request: "Pablo me pidió que lo ___."
questions.explanation: A reported command or request after a past verb takes the imperfect subjunctive: llamara (also llamase), lesson 15. "Que lo llamaba" would report a statement ("I was calling him"), not a request.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: If only I had more time!
questions.explanation: "¡Ojalá tuviera más tiempo!" An unlikely wish about now takes ojalá + imperfect subjunctive (lesson 13). The conditional (tendría) never follows ojalá.

questions.stem: Complete the passive sentence: "La catedral ___ construida en el siglo XVI."
questions.explanation: The passive voice is "ser" + participle, here in the preterite for a completed event: fue construida (lesson 12). "Estar" + participle describes the resulting state, not the action; "se construida" mixes two structures (the se passive is "Se construyó").

questions.stem: Complete: "No conozco a nadie que ___ tocar la guitarra."
questions.explanation: A relative clause about someone who doesn't exist (no conozco a nadie que…) takes the subjunctive: sepa (lesson 08).

questions.stem: Complete: "Cuando le dieron la noticia, ___ muy nerviosa."
questions.explanation: A sudden, temporary reaction: ponerse + adjective (lesson 22). "Volverse" would be a lasting change of character; "hacerse" a change by effort or time; "convertirse en" needs a noun.

questions.stem: Put the four tasks of the DELE B1 speaking test in order.
choices: A short talk on a topic you have prepared
A conversation with the examiner about your talk
Describing a photo and talking about it
A role play of an everyday situation
questions.explanation: The guide's order: the prepared talk (2–3 min), the conversation about it (3–4 min), the photo (2–3 min, not prepared) and the role play (2–3 min). Notes from the preparation time can be used in the first two.

questions.stem: Match each exam instruction to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Exam instructions use usted commands. "Argue for or against" would be "Argumente a favor o en contra", which isn't among the instructions here.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I hope you pass the exam. (tú)
questions.explanation: "Espero que apruebes el examen." A wish about someone else: esperar que + present subjunctive (lesson 01). "Aprobar" changes o → ue: apruebes. "Apruebas" is the indicative.

questions.stem: An Argentine friend says: "Mañana no puedo, tengo que laburar." What does she mean?
choices: I have to go dancing tomorrow.
I have to go to the pool tomorrow.
I have to take the bus tomorrow.
questions.explanation: "Laburar" is Argentina's informal "to work" (from Italian lavorare); "el laburo" is a job. Dancing would be "ir al boliche", the pool "la pileta", the bus "el colectivo".

questions.stem: In Buenos Aires, someone says: "¿Vamos al boliche esta noche?" Where do they want to go?
questions.explanation: In Argentina "el boliche" is a nightclub. In Mexico "el boliche" is bowling, and a nightclub is "el antro": the misunderstanding in this lesson's dialogue.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning and where it is used.
questions.explanation: "Job (Argentina)" is "el laburo". Remember that "la guagua" is a baby in the Andes.

questions.stem: Which Mexican informal word means the same as the Argentine "el laburo"?
questions.explanation: Both mean a job: "la chamba" (Mexico, informal) and "el laburo" (Argentina, informal). "El cuate" is a buddy, "la alberca" a pool, "el antro" a nightclub.

questions.stem: A friend from Chile says: "Mi hermana acaba de tener una guagua." What happened?
choices: Her sister got a new job.
questions.explanation: In the Andes (including Chile), "la guagua" is a baby, from a Quechua word. In the Caribbean the same word is a bus, which is why context matters.

questions.stem: Rewrite in Mexican Spanish (one word): "Vamos a la pileta" → "Vamos a la ___."
questions.explanation: A swimming pool is "la pileta" in Argentina, "la alberca" in Mexico and "la piscina" in Spain and many other countries.

questions.stem: Which words are typical of Spain? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "¡Vale!" (OK!) and "guay" (cool) are from Spain. "Bacano" is Colombian; "el pibe" is Argentine.

questions.stem: In the dialogue, why does Mariana think Facundo is inviting her to play something?
choices: Because Facundo says he loves bowling.
Because Argentine clubs have bowling lanes.
Because in Mexico el boliche is bowling.
questions.explanation: She hears "boliche" with its Mexican meaning (bowling), while Facundo means a nightclub, which a Mexican calls "un antro".

questions.stem: Build the sentence the way an Argentine would say it.
questions.prompt: I'm looking for work.
questions.explanation: "Estoy buscando laburo." "Laburo" is the noun (a job, work); "laburar" is the verb (to work), which can't be the object of "buscando" here. A Mexican would say "Estoy buscando chamba".

questions.stem: Some everyday words in one country are vulgar in another. What does this lesson recommend?
choices: Use the local slang as soon as you arrive.
Keep to neutral Spanish with strangers until you have heard locals use a word.
Avoid talking to people from other countries.
Always use Spain's words, because they are the standard.
questions.explanation: Neutral Spanish is safe everywhere; local informal words come later, once you've heard how people use them. No country's Spanish is "the standard": each educated norm is correct.

questions.stem: A Colombian friend writes: "No me alcanzó la plata para la camiseta." What does she mean?
choices: She didn't have enough money for the T-shirt.
The silver T-shirt didn't fit her.
The T-shirt wasn't made of silver.
