questions.explanation: In much of Latin America, including Colombia, "la plata" is money as well as silver; "alcanzar" here means "to be enough". In Mexico: "No me alcanzó el dinero para la playera."

questions.stem: Which Mexican phrase means the same as the Colombian "¡Qué bacano!"?
questions.explanation: "¡Qué bacano!" (Colombia) = "¡Qué padre!" or "¡Qué chido!" (Mexico) = How cool! "¡Qué oso!" is "How embarrassing!", "¡Aguas!" "Watch out!", "¡Qué lástima!" "What a pity!".

questions.stem: Kate's first draft said "Te propongo que nos vemos los martes." Why did she change "vemos" to "veamos"?
choices: "Proponer que" expresses influence, so it takes the subjunctive.
The two verbs have the same subject.
questions.explanation: Proposing is a form of influence (lesson 02): proponer que + present subjunctive (veamos). "Veamos" isn't a future, the subjects are different (yo / nosotros), and "vemos" is the normal indicative everywhere.

questions.stem: Lucía's first draft had 118 words for a task that asks for 130–150. What was the best fix?
choices: Repeat her first sentence at the end.
Add the point the task asked for that she had left out.
Nothing: the word count doesn't matter.
questions.explanation: She had left out how her life is now, one of the task's points (pautas). Adding it covered the task and brought the count into range. Padding with repetition or lists adds words but no content.

questions.stem: Correct the draft: "Si podría volver atrás, tomaría la misma decisión." Type the correct form of "poder": "Si ___ volver atrás, tomaría la misma decisión."
questions.explanation: An unreal condition takes si + imperfect subjunctive (pudiera, or pudiese) and the conditional in the main clause (tomaría). Never si + conditional (lesson 14).

questions.stem: Put the steps of the 15 minutes of preparation in the order this lesson suggests.
choices: Read both options and choose one
Write a key-word plan, with a connector for each point
Note useful words and questions you might be asked
Rehearse your first and last sentence
questions.explanation: Choose (0–2 min), plan in key words (2–10), add words and likely questions (10–13), rehearse the opening and closing (13–15). You can't plan before choosing, and rehearsing comes last.

questions.stem: Match each criterion to the question it asks about your work.
choices: Are agreement, tenses and mood right?
Do I use varied words and structures?
Do my ideas connect and hang together?
Do I keep talking without long stops?
questions.explanation: These are the criteria the guide names for the detailed mark (writing: fit to the task, coherence, correctness, range; speaking: coherence, fluency, correctness, range). Handwriting isn't one of them.

questions.stem: You are describing this photo. Choose the word for each numbered thing.

image.alt: A park on a sunny day: a fountain in the center, an older couple on a bench next to a tree, a girl on a bicycle and a boy with a red balloon on the right, a family having a picnic and a swing in the background. Five things are numbered.

questions.explanation: 1 is the fountain (la fuente) in the center; 2 the bench (la banca) where the couple sit; 3 the swing (el columpio) in the background; 4 the boy's red balloon (el globo); 5 the girl's bicycle. There is no market stall (el puesto) or ball (la pelota) in the photo.

questions.stem: In a photo description, which sentence is a guess rather than a description of what you can see?
choices: En el centro hay una fuente.
A la derecha, una niña anda en bicicleta.
questions.explanation: "Seguramente" (most likely) introduces a guess, like "Parece que…" and "Creo que…". Ending a description with a reasoned guess shows range; the other three describe what's in the picture.

questions.stem: In the role play, you want the store to give you your money back. Which request is the most appropriate?
choices: Quiero que me devuelven el dinero.
¿Sería posible que me devolvieran el dinero?
questions.explanation: With a stranger in a store, use usted and a polite form: ¿Sería posible que…? + imperfect subjunctive (lessons 15 and 20). The first two are rude or too informal; the third needs the subjunctive (devuelvan).

questions.stem: Build Kate's polite request in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I'd like you to exchange it for me. (the jacket, ustedes)
questions.explanation: "Me gustaría que me la cambiaran." After a conditional main verb (me gustaría), the subjunctive is the imperfect (cambiaran, also cambiasen). "Me la" (to me, la chamarra) goes before the verb. "Cambiaban" is the indicative imperfect.

questions.stem: Which of these was one of the pautas (points to cover) in the forum task of Example 1?
choices: Suggest when and where to meet.
questions.explanation: The task asked her to introduce herself, explain her interest, suggest when and where to meet, and ask a question. The length was 100–120 words, and this course always uses ustedes, not vosotros.

questions.stem: What does "cronometrar tu presentación" mean?
questions.explanation: "Cronometrar" is to time something (el cronómetro = a stopwatch). To record is "grabar"; to correct, "corregir"; to summarize, "resumir".

questions.stem: Kate's model talk is 158 words, about a minute and a half at a calm pace. The exam's talk lasts 2–3 minutes. What should she do?
choices: Read the talk aloud from a full script.
Add an example or develop one of her points.
Stop after a minute and a half and wait.
questions.explanation: Develop the content: an example, a short anecdote or a comparison. Speaking faster hurts clarity, reading a script aloud isn't the point (notes are key words), and stopping early leaves time unused.

questions.stem: Where is the history of the bolero usually traced to?
questions.explanation: The bolero is usually traced to Santiago de Cuba, where Pepe Sánchez wrote "Tristezas" in 1883. Mexico became one of its great centers, and in 2023 UNESCO listed it for Cuba and Mexico.

questions.stem: Which genre is a narrative ballad that tells a story, verse after verse?
questions.explanation: The corrido tells stories (battles, heroes, love affairs); its best-known period is the Mexican Revolution. The bolero is a slow love song; cumbia and reguetón are dance music.

questions.stem: Match each genre to where it comes from.
questions.explanation: None of these genres comes from Spain: they grew in the Americas from Spanish, African and Indigenous roots.

questions.stem: The genre names are missing from this timeline. Choose the genre for each numbered box.

image.alt: A timeline with five empty numbered boxes: 1, 1883, Santiago de Cuba, Tristezas, often called the first…; 2, 1910–1920, Mexico, the Revolution, songs that tell the news; 3, 1930s–1950s, Mexico, the golden age of cinema, stars sing; 4, late 1960s–1970s, Cuba, singer-songwriters with guitars, the nueva…; 5, 1990s, Panama and Puerto Rico, dancehall in Spanish becomes…

questions.explanation: Tristezas (1883) is often called the first bolero; the Revolution is the corrido's best-known era; film stars sang rancheras; the nueva trova came from Cuba; reguetón grew out of Panama and Puerto Rico. Cumbia and son jarocho appear in the side box, without dates.

questions.stem: Complete the passive with the participle of "componer": "La canción fue ___ en 1950."
questions.explanation: "Componer" has the irregular participle "compuesto", like "puesto"; in the passive it agrees with the subject: la canción → compuesta.

questions.stem: Choose the correct preterite: "Agustín Lara ___ muchos boleros famosos."
questions.explanation: "Componer" is conjugated like "poner": puso → compuso, with no accent (irregular preterites have none). "Componió" treats it as regular; "compondió" mixes in the future stem.

questions.stem: What is "el estribillo" of a song?
questions.explanation: El estribillo is the chorus or refrain, the part that repeats. The melody is la melodía, the rhythm el ritmo, the lyrics la letra.

questions.stem: In what year did UNESCO add the bolero (nominated by Cuba and Mexico) to its intangible cultural heritage list?
questions.explanation: 2023. In 2011 UNESCO listed mariachi; 1883 is the year of "Tristezas"; 1958 is when Ritchie Valens's rock version of "La Bamba" came out in the United States.

questions.stem: Complete: "La cumbia es un ritmo con ___ todo el mundo baila."
questions.explanation: After a preposition, a relative referring to a thing usually takes the article: con el que (or con el cual), lesson 08. "Cual" can't stand without its article; "quien" is for people; "lo que" refers to an idea, not back to "un ritmo". (Formal writing also allows "con que" without the article, so it isn't offered here.)

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The song was composed by a singer-songwriter (a woman).
questions.explanation: The ser passive: fue + participle agreeing with the subject (la canción → compuesta) + por + the agent (lesson 12).

questions.stem: Complete: "El bolero es lento y romántico; el reguetón, ___, es muy bailable."
questions.explanation: "En cambio" (on the other hand) marks a contrast. "Por eso" and "así que" give a consequence; "además" adds a similar idea.

questions.stem: Why does this lesson give song titles and facts but quote no lyrics?
choices: Lyrics are too hard at B1.
Song lyrics are protected by copyright.
questions.explanation: Song lyrics are protected by copyright, so the lesson describes the songs and invites you to listen. In a review you publish, describe the lyrics (La letra habla de…) rather than copying them.

cards.front: el verso / la estrofa / el poema
cards.back: one line / a stanza / the whole poem

cards.front: How do you count syllables in Spanish verse?
cards.back: As spoken; join vowels between words (sinalefa); +1 after a palabra aguda, −1 after an esdrújula.
Vowels across words join into one syllable: se apaga → sea-pa-ga (3).

cards.front: Llega temprano la luz: how many syllables?
cards.back: 7 written + 1 (luz is aguda) = 8: an octosyllable.
An 8-syllable line: romances, corridos, songs, Martí's Versos sencillos.
An 11-syllable line, stressed on the 10th (and the 6th, or the 4th and 8th): the line of the sonnet.
Only the vowels match from the stressed one: plaza / naranjas (á-a).
Vowels and consonants match from the stressed vowel: libreta / secreta.
Octosyllables with assonant rhyme in the even lines; the odd lines don't rhyme.
14 hendecasyllables: 2 cuartetos (ABBA ABBA) + 2 tercetos (e.g. CDC DCD), consonant rhyme.
Metaphor: Tu risa es una ventana. Simile (with como): blanco como la leche.
el mercado se despide / Te lo he dicho mil veces.
recitar: to say from memory; declamar: to perform it dramatically before an audience.
a book of poems: Versos sencillos es un poemario de Martí.

cards.front: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
cards.back: New Spain, 1648 or 1651 – 1695. Nun, poet, playwright; Primero sueño (1692), Respuesta a sor Filotea (1691); la décima musa; 100-peso note.
Cuba, 1853–1895. Ismaelillo (1882), La Edad de Oro (1889), Versos sencillos (1891, octosyllables).
Spain, 1836–1870. Rimas and Leyendas, published by friends after his death (1871).
Nicaragua, 1867–1916. Leader of modernismo: Azul… (1888), Prosas profanas (1896), Cantos de vida y esperanza (1905).
Mexico, 1870–1919 (died in Montevideo). Perlas negras, Místicas (1898); La amada inmóvil (posthumous).

cards.front: Where to read these poets free
cards.back: Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes (cervantesvirtual.com) or Spanish Wikisource: they are in the public domain.

cards.front: la noticia / la crónica / la columna
cards.back: reports facts / tells a true story with scenes and voices / argues a signed opinion
writer of crónicas / writer of a column (la cronista, la columnista)
the source of information: según una fuente oficial…
to check it against other sources
creo que, me parece que; es una lástima que + subjunctive; evaluative adjectives; deberían…
dates, figures, quotations, named sources (según…, de acuerdo con…)
The mayor will reportedly resign (condicional de rumor: unconfirmed). Write: Según fuentes no oficiales…
objective, impartial / subjective; el objetivo = goal
bias: hidden in loaded words, chosen sources and what is left out
the front page: salir en primera plana
Questions first; skim; scan; expect paraphrase; don't stop at every unknown word.

cards.front: How is a stage direction written?
cards.back: In parentheses, present tense, often verb first: (Entra TOÑO corriendo.) (Se sienta.)

cards.front: Se abre el telón… Cae el telón.
cards.back: The curtain opens… The curtain falls (the end).
the cast; the rehearsal (also essay); to rehearse
the costumes; the props (Spain: el atrezo)
stage curtain / window curtain
theater seat / any seat
playwright (la dramaturga)
Le dijo a Toño que lavara las ollas.
It's about time that… + subjunctive: Ya es hora de que alguien aprenda.
1: dozens (safety); 2: hundreds (response); 3: thousands, vaccine vs placebo at random (protection); then the regulator; 4: monitoring.
dummy treatment / neither volunteers nor doctors know who got what
demuestra que + ind. → sugiere que + ind. → es probable / posible que + subj., podría → no está claro si
to suggest something is true (Los datos sugieren que…) / to recommend (Sugieren que nos vacunemos)
+ indicative: El estudio concluyó que la vacuna funciona. (concluyo, concluyó, concluyendo)
86 000 millones (un billón = a million million)

cards.front: el virus, la bacteria, el gen
cards.back: plurals: los virus, las bacterias, los genes
1st time: gist and attitude. 2nd: numbers, names, certainty words.
Jenner: cowpox, 14 May 1796 (vacuna < vacca). Broca: speech area, left frontal lobe, 1861.
Indicative: facts (Sé que vienes). Subjunctive: wishes, influence, feelings, doubt (Quiero que vengas, Te pido que vengas, Me alegra que vengas, Dudo que vengas).
Main clause + que + a NEW subject + subjunctive: Quiero que (tú) vengas. Same subject → infinitive: Quiero venir.

cards.front: Present subjunctive: how to form it
cards.back: yo present − o + the "other" vowel: -ar → e (hable), -er/-ir → a (coma, viva). Irregular yo carries through: tenga, haga, diga, conozca.
-ar: -e, -es, -e, -emos, -en. -er/-ir: -a, -as, -a, -amos, -an.
-car → que (busque), -gar → gue (llegue), -zar → ce (alcance), -ger/-gir → ja (escoja, exija), -guir → ga (siga).
-ar/-er: no change in nosotros (pensemos, podamos). -ir: e → i, o → u in nosotros (pidamos, sintamos, durmamos).

cards.front: The six to learn by heart
cards.back: ser sea, ir vaya, estar esté, dar dé, saber sepa, haber haya (hay → haya).
querer, desear, esperar (to hope), preferir + que + subjunctive: Espero que te guste. Espero que sí / que no = I hope so / not.
I hope / let's hope, + subjunctive, with or without que: Ojalá (que) no llueva. Alone: ¡Ojalá! = I hope so! Never changes form.
All the best! (a goodbye). A wish with que alone: (Espero) que te vaya bien. usted: le; ustedes: les.
soplar las velas (blow out the candles), pedir un deseo (make a wish), que se cumpla (may it come true).
Twelve grapes at midnight, a wish with each; walking around the block with a suitcase for travel; los propósitos de Año Nuevo (resolutions). ¡Próspero Año Nuevo!
pedir, aconsejar, recomendar, sugerir, exigir, insistir en, rogar, ordenar, permitir, dejar, prohibir + que + subjunctive.

cards.front: Te pido que me llames: who is who?
cards.back: te = the person asked; llames = the same person calls; me = the person to be called.
Very common: No me dejan salir. Te prohíbo hablar así. Also correct: No me dejan que salga.

cards.front: insistir en que / decir que: two moods
cards.back: Subjunctive to push someone to act (Dice que llegues temprano); indicative to state a fact (Dice que llegas temprano).
es importante / necesario / mejor / urgente / fundamental + infinitive (general) or + que + subjunctive (someone): Es importante que duermas.
prohíbo, prohíbes, prohíbe, prohíben; prohíba (but prohibimos). crío, crías, cría, crían; críe. RAE 2010: crie, crio take no accent.
exijo, exija; ruego, rogué, ruegue, roguemos; sugiero, sugirió, sugiriendo, sugiramos.
Allowance, pocket money; also el domingo. Spain: la paga.
Chores (hacer los quehaceres); to scold (Mexico; Spain also reñir).
la regla: an everyday rule (also a ruler); la norma: a formal rule, a norm (normas de convivencia).
Feelings take the subjunctive even about true things: Me alegra que estés aquí.
The clause is one singular subject: Me molesta que lleguen tarde (not me molestan).
me da miedo / pena / rabia / vergüenza / tristeza que + subjunctive. In Mexico pena often means embarrassment.
Me alegro de que vengas (keep de). Me alegra que vengas (no de). Same meaning.
+ subjunctive = to be sorry (Siento que estés enfermo); + indicative = to feel, sense (Siento que algo no está bien).
Temo que no haya boletos (fear, subjunctive). Me temo que no hay boletos (polite bad news, indicative).
Me alegra verte. Siento llegar tarde. Estoy harto de esperar.
haya, hayas, haya, hayamos, hayan + participle, for what has happened: Me alegra que hayas venido. No drill form.
¡Qué bueno que…!, ¡Qué lástima que…!, ¡Qué raro que…!, Es una lástima que… + subjunctive.
decepcionado = disappointed; sensible = sensitive; la ilusión = excitement, hope; emocionado = excited, moved.
el estado de ánimo; estar de buen humor / de mal humor.
creo que, pienso que, me parece que, estoy seguro de que, es verdad / cierto / evidente / obvio que, está claro que.
no creo que, no pienso que, no me parece que, no estoy seguro de que, no es verdad que, dudo que, niego que.
es posible / probable / improbable / imposible / difícil que, puede (ser) que: Puede que llueva.
Usually "it's unlikely that": Es difícil que gane. "Hard to do" = es difícil + infinitive.

cards.front: quizás / tal vez vs a lo mejor
cards.back: quizás, tal vez (before the verb): either mood. a lo mejor: indicative only (A lo mejor viene).
A question can take either mood: ¿Crees que es verdad? (neutral) / ¿Crees que sea verdad? (more doubtful).
Usually + indicative (not doubting = being sure): No dudo que te extraña. The subjunctive is also heard.
es cierto = it's true; before a noun, "a certain": cierta persona, un cierto miedo.
Rodolfo Neri Vela, first Mexican in space: Atlantis, STS-61-B, Nov 26–Dec 3, 1985. Katya Echazarreta, first Mexican-born woman: Blue Origin, June 4, 2022.
The traditional unlucky day in Mexico and several other Spanish-speaking countries: En martes 13, ni te cases ni te embarques.
¡Que descanses! ¡Que te diviertas! ¡Que tengas buen día! ¡Que te mejores! ¡Que cumplas muchos más! ¡Que sean muy felices!

cards.front: Changing the person in a que wish
cards.back: tú: ¡Que descanses! usted: ¡Que descanse! ustedes: ¡Que descansen! (reflexive: te diviertas → se divierta → se diviertan)
A warm version of ¡Que te vaya bien!, heard especially in Mexico; also the title of a ranchera by José Alfredo Jiménez.
Enjoy your meal. ¡Que aproveche! is the usual phrase in Spain; Mexico much more often says ¡Provecho! or ¡Buen provecho!, often even to strangers.
God willing / I hope so: Dios quiera que no llueva. Related: si Dios quiere (added to plans).
Usually traced (RAE dictionary, 2001 edition) to Hispanic Arabic law šá lláh, "if God wills"; the exact source is debated. Today it has no religious meaning for most speakers.
pase lo que pase (whatever happens), cueste lo que cueste (whatever it takes), digan lo que digan (whatever people say), sea como sea (one way or another).
Mi más sentido pésame. Mis condolencias. Lamento mucho la pérdida de… Que en paz descanse (Q. E. P. D.). Un abrazo fuerte.
Customary in Mexico (Que Dios te bendiga, Dios quiera), never required: a warm message without them is just as correct.

cards.front: tú or usted in a message?
cards.back: tú: friends and family of your generation. usted: older people, your boss, people you don't know well; the safe choice for condolences.
1 greeting, 2 react (Siento que…), 3 advise (Te aconsejo que…), 4 opinion (No creo que…), 5 wish (Ojalá que…) and sign-off.
Te aconsejo que… → Deberías… → Quizás deberías… / Yo en tu lugar + conditional → ¿Y si + present indicative? / ¿Has pensado en…?
What if…? Takes the present indicative: ¿Y si le llamas? Never si + present subjunctive.
To take into account (very common in Mexico; Spain usually tener en cuenta). Toma en cuenta que… (no de).
Understanding, sympathetic (false friend). Comprehensive = completo, integral.
el desamor (heartbreak), desahogarse (to vent), reconciliarse (to make up), la autoestima, la timidez, el rechazo, sincero, la sinceridad.
A letter, e-mail or post of 100–120 words answering a short text. Plan every point, then count.
me desahogué (g → gu before e), que te desahogues; desahógate, desahóguese.
no + the tú form of the present subjunctive: no aceleres, no corras, no escribas; no tengas, no hagas, no digas, no vayas, no seas.

All of them except the affirmative tú command: usted (frene), ustedes (frenen), nosotros (frenemos) and every negative (no frenes, no frene, no frenen, no frenemos). Affirmative tú = él present: frena.
Attached to affirmative commands, with an accent if needed: estaciónalo, dígaselo. Before negative ones: no lo estaciones, no se lo diga.
The sound of the stem stays: buscar → no busques, llegar → no llegues, cruzar → no cruces, escoger → no escojas.
The nosotros subjunctive: crucemos (let's cross), no estacionemos (let's not park). ir: vamos / no vayamos. Everyday alternative: vamos a + infinitive.
Nosotros commands drop the final -s before nos: vamos + nos → vámonos; sentemos + nos → sentémonos. Negative: no nos vayamos, no nos sentemos.
¿Podrías frenar un poco? · Mejor no tomes esa calle. · Te recomiendo que no uses el celular. · Hay que respetar el límite de velocidad.
Infinitive: NO ESTACIONARSE, PROHIBIDO REBASAR. usted command: CEDA EL PASO (yield), DISMINUYA SU VELOCIDAD, MANEJE CON PRECAUCIÓN.
la banqueta / la acera; la glorieta / la rotonda; la placa / la matrícula; estacionar(se) / aparcar; la señal de tránsito / la señal de tráfico; la ciclovía / el carril bici.

cards.front: Mexico City speed limits (Reglamento de Tránsito, 2019 text)
cards.back: Unless a sign says otherwise: 50 km/h on main roads, 40 on secondary roads, 20 in school and hospital zones, 80 in the central lanes of expressways.

cards.front: para + infinitive or para que + subjunctive?
cards.back: Same subject: para + infinitive (Ahorro para comprar útiles). Different subject: para que + subjunctive (Dono para que los niños tengan útiles).
Always the subjunctive: a purpose isn't a fact yet. Te lo explico para que lo entiendas.

cards.front: sin + infinitive or sin que + subjunctive?
cards.back: Same subject: sin + infinitive (Trabajan sin descansar). Different subject: sin que + subjunctive (Ayudo sin que me lo pidan).
¿Para qué? = what for? (purpose): Para reconstruir la escuela. ¿Por qué? = why? (cause): Porque me importa.
Formal para que, + subjunctive, in notices and letters: a fin de que podamos empezar a tiempo. a fin de + infinitive = formal para + infinitive.
Informal: command + que + subjunctive = so that. Acércate, que te vean (Come closer, so they can see you).
Use a clause, not an infinitive: I brought chairs for the volunteers to sit on → Traje sillas para que los voluntarios se sienten.

cards.front: Helping words: la ONG, el albergue, el damnificado
cards.back: NGO (las ONG, plural unchanged); shelter (temporary housing); person affected by a disaster. el centro de acopio = collection center for donations.
Future: subjunctive (Cuando llegue, te escribo). Habit: indicative (Cuando llego, siempre te escribo). Past: indicative (Cuando llegué, te escribí).
Not "cuando llegaré": Cuando llegue, te llamo / te llamaré / voy a llamarte / llámame.

cards.front: en cuanto, tan pronto como, hasta que, después de que, mientras
cards.back: Like cuando: subjunctive for the future (en cuanto tengas la visa), indicative for habits and the past (en cuanto tuvo la visa).
Always + subjunctive: Despídete antes de que nos vayamos. Same subject: antes de + infinitive (Empaco antes de salir).
Indicative or future, never the subjunctive: ¿Cuándo llegas? ¿Cuándo llegarás? No sé cuándo me dan la residencia.

cards.front: después de que in the past
cards.back: Standard: indicative (Después de que se fueron, limpiamos). Newspapers sometimes use the imperfect subjunctive (se fueran): recognize it, write the indicative.
You emigrate from your country (emigrar, el emigrante) and immigrate to a new one (inmigrar, el inmigrante). la migración covers both; in Mexico also the immigration desk.

cards.front: Temporary residence in Mexico (as of November 2026)
cards.back: Visa from a Mexican consulate; within 30 calendar days of entering, apply to the INM for the resident card. Stays of more than 180 days, up to four years. Check current rules.
Known, real antecedent: indicative (Tengo un celular que tiene buena cámara). Wanted, unknown or nonexistent: subjunctive (Busco un celular que tenga buena cámara).

cards.front: No hay nada / nadie / ningún… que
cards.back: A nonexistent antecedent takes the subjunctive: No hay nada que me guste. No conozco a nadie que repare aparatos.

cards.front: The personal a with an unknown person
cards.back: Usually dropped: Busco un técnico que sepa… (any technician). Kept with a known person (Busco al técnico que…) and always with alguien, nadie.
Indicative = what (definite): Hago lo que me dices. Subjunctive = whatever: Haz lo que quieras. Compra lo que necesites.
Whoever, whichever one: El que llegue primero escoge. Llévate la que te guste. (Indicative: la que te gusta = the one I know you like.)
The preposition goes first: la tienda en la que compré, el amigo con el que hablé. Formal: la empresa, la cual…
de madera (wooden), de metal, de vidrio (glass; Spain cristal), de cuero (leather), de tela (fabric), de plástico.
la talla (A2): size of clothes and shoes. el tamaño: how big a thing is (El tamaño es perfecto para mi cocina).

cards.front: el temblor, el sismo, el terremoto
cards.back: el temblor: the everyday word (¿Sentiste el temblor?). el sismo: news and official texts. el terremoto: usually a big, destructive one.
Major earthquakes in 1985 (M8.1), 2017 (M7.1) and 2022 (M7.7). The SSN calls the date a coincidence.
Mexico's seismic alert system, developed by CIRES after 1985; alerting Mexico City since 1991. Coastal sensors give tens of seconds of warning; a quake near the city may give none.
A drill. The Simulacro Nacional practices evacuations across the country (2026: 6 May and 19 September).

cards.front: No corras, no grites, no empujes
cards.back: The three rules for leaving a building, as Mexico City's civil protection guide writes them (tú). Posters: No correr, no gritar, no empujar.
Both are accepted by the RAE: evacúo, evacúas, evacúa… (like actuar) or evacuo, evacuas… (like averiguar). Subjunctive evacúe / evacue.
Emergency backpack (Mexico City's guide: la maleta de vida): water, food that won't spoil, flashlight, batteries, radio, medicine, copies of documents.

cards.front: Poster to speech: Dirigirse a la zona de seguridad
cards.back: tú: Dirígete. usted: Diríjase. ustedes: Diríjanse. nosotros: Dirijámonos (g → j before a; -s drops before nos).
lo que sea (anything), quien sea (anyone), donde sea (anywhere), cuando sea (any time), como sea (one way or another; informal: anyway).
lo que quieras, quien quieras, donde quieras, cuando quieras, como quieras. usted: lo que quiera; ustedes: lo que quieran.
cualquier cosa = anything; cualquiera (pronoun) = anyone, any one; cualquier + noun = any (never "cualquiera cosa").
Everyday closing offer of help: If anything comes up, let me know.
Formal, written "whoever / wherever", one word + que + subjunctive: Dondequiera que vivas… In speech: quien sea, donde sea.
dondequiera (one word) = wherever. donde quiera (two words) = where he / she / you (usted) wants: Siéntese donde quiera.

cards.front: Lo que sea, como sea: tone
cards.back: Said flatly, they can sound dismissive ("whatever"). Friendlier: Lo que sea está bien, gracias · Lo que tú quieras.

cards.front: Hago lo que quiero vs Haz lo que quieras
cards.back: Indicative: a fact (I do what I want). Subjunctive: an open choice (Do whatever you want).
había, habías, había, habíamos, habían + participle: había llegado, habían visto. The participle never changes.
The past before the past: Cuando llegó la policía, el ladrón ya había huido (When the police arrived, the thief had already fled).

cards.front: Pronouns and no with the pluperfect
cards.back: Before había, never between: Ya lo había visto. No se habían ido. Ya me lo había dicho.

cards.front: Llegó la policía y el ladrón huyó / ya había huido
cards.back: huyó = he fled then (two events in order); ya había huido = he was already gone when they arrived

cards.front: Words that go with the pluperfect
cards.back: ya (already), todavía no (not yet), nunca antes (never before), para entonces (by then), la noche anterior (the night before)
Estaba cansada porque no había dormido. Como nadie había cerrado la ventana, el ladrón entró.
hacer hecho, decir dicho, ver visto, poner puesto, volver vuelto, devolver devuelto, resolver resuelto
abrir abierto, cubrir cubierto, descubrir descubierto, escribir escrito, describir descrito, romper roto, morir muerto

cards.front: Participles with and without an accent
cards.back: After a, e, o: leído, caído, creído, traído, oído. After u: huido, construido, destruido (no accent).
Había dos testigos (there were: always singular in standard Spanish). Los testigos habían visto al ladrón (had seen: agrees with the subject).

cards.front: huir in the present and preterite
cards.back: huyo, huyes, huye, huimos, huyen; hui, huiste, huyó, huimos, huyeron (hui and huis have no accent)

cards.front: el delito / el crimen / el asesinato
cards.back: el delito = any legal offense; el crimen = a serious crime, especially a killing; el asesinato = murder
Always feminine, even for a man: La víctima, un hombre de 60 años…
denunciar el robo; poner / presentar una denuncia (Mexico also: levantar una denuncia)
alibi / fingerprint
imperfect = the scene (llovía); preterite = the events (abrió la puerta); pluperfect = what had happened before (alguien había dejado una carta)
when, on (doing): Al abrir la puerta, vio la carta. The infinitive never changes.

cards.front: en cuanto / tan pronto como for a past fact
cards.back: Indicative: En cuanto llegó, me llamó. (Subjunctive for the future: En cuanto llegues, llámame.)
as soon as (Apenas salió el sol, empezamos a caminar); barely (Apenas dormí; Tenía apenas quince años)
after (a period), … later: Al cabo de una hora, volvió. Everyday Mexican Spanish also says a la hora, a los dos días.
from … on: A partir de ese día, todo cambió. Also future: a partir del lunes.
since then (Desde entonces no lo he visto) / until then (Hasta entonces nunca había leído poesía)
mientras tanto (meanwhile) starts a sentence; mientras (while) joins two clauses: Mientras ella buscaba la llave, él llamaba.
de pronto = suddenly (= de repente); por último = lastly, the last step of a series

cards.front: estaba a punto de / acababa de
cards.back: was about to / had just: Estaba a punto de salir cuando sonó el teléfono. Acababa de llegar cuando empezó a llover.
el planteamiento (setup), el nudo (conflict), el clímax, el desenlace (ending); a fable adds la moraleja (the moral)
the publisher / a newspaper editorial

cards.front: el protagonista, el narrador, el lector
cards.back: main character, narrator (the voice telling the story), reader; feminine la protagonista, la narradora, la lectora
Masculine, like el problema: el poema, los poemas.
habré, habrás, habrá, habremos, habrán + participle: habré terminado (I will have finished)

cards.front: Future perfect: done before a future point
cards.back: Para 2035 habré terminado la carrera. Cuando llegues, ya habremos cenado.

cards.front: Future perfect: a guess about the recent past
cards.back: Se habrá quedado dormida (She must have fallen asleep). ¿Qué habrá pasado? (I wonder what happened.)
Estará en la oficina = he's probably at the office (now). Habrá salido = he's probably left (the recent past).
habría, habrías, habría, habríamos, habrían + participle: habría terminado (I would have finished)
A past that didn't happen: Yo no lo habría hecho; En tu lugar, habría aceptado. Regrets: Me habría gustado estudiar música.
Common in speech, especially in the Americas: Yo no lo hubiera hecho = Yo no lo habría hecho. The RAE accepts both. Never habría after si meaning "if".
I have finished / I had finished / I will have finished / I would have finished
Both mean challenge; el reto is the everyday word in Mexico, el desafío a little more formal.
to be worth it: Valió la pena. ¿Vale la pena?
to regret: No me arrepiento de nada. Se arrepintió (e → i), nos arrepintamos.
mature (people) or ripe (fruit): una persona madura, un mango maduro
ser (any tense) + participle agreeing with the subject (+ por + agent): La ciudad fue fundada por los mexicas en 1325.

cards.front: Active to passive in three steps
cards.back: object → subject; ser in the active verb's tense + agreeing participle; old subject → por + agent (optional)

cards.front: Agreement: haber vs ser and estar
cards.back: With haber the participle never changes (Han restaurado la iglesia); with ser and estar it agrees (La iglesia ha sido restaurada; está restaurada).
an event (someone closed it) / a state (it isn't open)
The everyday passive; the verb agrees with the thing: Se construyó en 1950. Se descubrieron dos tumbas. No por + agent.

cards.front: Someone did it: the ellos form
cards.back: Me robaron la cartera (My wallet was stolen). Restauraron la iglesia (The church was restored).

cards.front: Where the ser passive is used
cards.back: Mostly in writing: history, the news, museum labels. In speech, prefer the active, the passive se or the ellos form.
Nací (nacer is an ordinary active verb), never fui nacido.
the usual Mexican term for an archaeological site open to the public; the INAH (Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia) looks after them
Both are heard in Mexico: pueblos indígenas in federal law (INPI); pueblos originarios used by many communities and by Mexico City.
Coyolxauhqui stone found by electric company workers, 21 February 1978; Museo del Templo Mayor opened 12 October 1987
Found in the Zócalo on 17 December 1790; in the Museo Nacional de Antropología since 1964
Something supernatural, told calmly as normal, in a realistic world: the reader is surprised, the characters aren't.
The German critic Franz Roh (Magischer Realismus, 1925), for painting. Alejo Carpentier wrote of lo real maravilloso in 1949.
Mexico, 1917–1986. El llano en llamas (1953), Pedro Páramo (1955). Often called a forerunner of magical realism.
Colombia, 1927–2014. Cien años de soledad (1967), set in Macondo. Nobel Prize in Literature 1982. Died in Mexico City.
Chilean, born in Lima in 1942. La casa de los espíritus (1982).
imperfect = the impossible as habit or scene (ponían huevos azules); preterite = as an event; pluperfect = the prophecy or past behind it
an omen, a sign / a prediction someone says aloud
feminine, with el in the singular: el alma buena, las almas

cards.front: Monarch butterflies and the Day of the Dead
cards.back: They arrive in Michoacán and the State of Mexico in late October and early November; a tradition associated especially with the Purépecha links them with the souls of the dead.
Glyphs for words and syllables, about 800 signs in all; mostly deciphered in the second half of the 20th century, building on Yuri Knórozov's work in the 1950s.
Base 20, with a sign for zero; one of the oldest zeros carved in stone dates from AD 357.
Founded in 1325 (by tradition) on an island in Lake Texcoco; three calzadas to Tepeyac, Iztapalapa and Tlacopan; conquered 13 August 1521.
Ruler of Palenque for almost seventy years; died in 683. His tomb was discovered in 1952 by Alberto Ruz Lhuillier.
The Inca road network, about 30,000 km, at its greatest extent in the 15th century; World Heritage since 2014.
Knotted, colored cords the Inca used to keep records; whether they recorded words is still debated.
Played across Mesoamerica with a heavy rubber ball, often hit with the hips; ulama, its descendant, is still played in Sinaloa.

cards.front: se cree que / se discute / según
cards.back: Mark a claim that isn't settled: Se cree que El Caracol era un observatorio.
Habits in the imperfect (se cultivaba maíz); single events in the preterite (fue conquistada en 1521).
Built in the 15th century; Bingham reached it on 24 July 1911 and made it known abroad, but others had been there before. World Heritage since 1983.

cards.front: Imperfect subjunctive: how to build it
cards.back: ellos preterite − -ron + -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -ran: hablaron → hablara, tuvieron → tuviera, fueron → fuera.
The vowel before -ramos takes an accent: habláramos, comiéramos, tuviéramos, fuéramos.
They copy the preterite: fuera, tuviera, estuviera, pudiera, puso → pusiera, supiera, quisiera, viniera, hiciera, dijera, trajera, diera, viera, hubiera.

cards.front: -ir stem changers in the imperfect subjunctive
cards.back: Keep the preterite change: pidieron → pidiera, durmieron → durmiera, sintieron → sintiera, prefirieron → prefiriera.
hablase, tuviese, fuésemos: same meaning as -ra. Common in writing and in Spain; -ra is the everyday form in Latin America. Recognize -se.

cards.front: Ojalá + present vs ojalá + imperfect subjunctive
cards.back: Ojalá venga = I hope he comes (possible). Ojalá viniera = I wish he'd come (unlikely). Both about now or the future.
The imperfect subjunctive of querer, used alone as a polite "I'd like": Quisiera hablar con la gerente.
as if: always + imperfect subjunctive for the same time. Gasta como si fuera millonario. Never como si + present.
to dream of / about: Sueño con una casa en la playa. Never soñar de. Soñé que volaba = I dreamed I was flying.
by chance / What a coincidence! Nos conocimos por casualidad.
hablara (ha-BLA-ra) = imperfect subjunctive; hablará (ha-bla-RÁ) = future. The accent moves the stress.
Real: si + present → present / future / command. Hypothetical now: si + imperfect subjunctive → conditional. Past: si + hubiera + participle → habría + participle.
Si fuera alcaldesa, arreglaría los baches. = If I were mayor, I'd fix the potholes.
the conditional (si tendría), the present subjunctive (si tenga) or the future (si lloverá).

cards.front: Order and comma in si sentences
cards.back: Either clause first. Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría (comma) / Viajaría si tuviera tiempo (no comma needed).
What would you do if…? ¿Qué harías si fueras invisible? Answer with the conditional: Viajaría gratis.
Si yo fuera tú, + conditional = Yo que tú, + conditional (A2): Si yo fuera tú, hablaría con ella.
Formal: de + infinitive replaces a si clause. De ser así, habría que cambiar la ley = If that were so…
mayor / town hall; in Mexico City, one of 16 boroughs (since 1 Oct 2018). Officially, a municipio is headed by the presidente municipal.
el bache (pothole), el drenaje (drainage), la escasez de agua (water shortage), el agua potable (drinking water), la inseguridad (lack of public safety), el desempleo, la corrupción.
invierto, invirtió, invirtiera (like preferir); reduzco, redujo, redujera (like conducir).
Present / future / command / present perfect + present subjunctive. Preterite / imperfect / pluperfect / conditional + imperfect subjunctive.
Quería que vinieras. Me pide que lo llame → Me pidió que lo llamara.
Me gustaría que…, Preferiría que…, Sería mejor que… + imperfect subjunctive: Me gustaría que me ayudaras. (The present, me ayudes, is also heard in Latin America.)
Me dijo que lo había llamado (information: indicative). Me dijo que lo llamara (an instruction: subjunctive = told me to call him).
Salió sin que nadie lo viera. Te lo expliqué para que lo entendieras. Mandé el informe antes de que lo pidiera.
Me encargaron el informe = they gave me the report to do. Yo me encargo de las copias = I'll take care of the copies.
Working from home: the everyday English loan in Mexico (hago home office). Legal and Spain's word: el teletrabajo.
overtime: hacer horas extra. Las horas extras is also correct.
evalúo, evalúas, evalúa, evaluamos, evalúan; subjunctive evalúe. La evaluación = appraisal, el desempeño = performance.
present → imperfect; preterite / perfect → pluperfect; future → conditional; ir a → iba a; command → imperfect subjunctive; imperfect, pluperfect, conditional: no change.
Me dijo que lo llamara (he told me to call him). A command becomes que + imperfect subjunctive.
Something still true may keep the present: Me dijo que vive en Puebla. Me dijo que vivía en Puebla is also correct.
hoy → ese día; ayer → el día anterior; mañana → al día siguiente; la semana que viene → la semana siguiente; ahora → entonces; aquí → allí; este → ese.
yes/no: Me preguntó si iba. With a question word, keep the accent: Me preguntó dónde vivía, por qué no lo había invitado.
contar, explicar, asegurar, advertir, aclarar, negar, admitir, mencionar, desmentir (a rumor), susurrar, presumir (de).
al parecer, por lo visto (apparently), supuestamente (supposedly): report without vouching for it.
gossip, to gossip, a gossip (person). Spain: el cotilleo.
In Spanish the period goes after the closing quotation mark: Me dijo: "No vuelvo".

From Thomas More's Utopia (1516, in Latin): usually explained as Greek "no place", also heard as "good place". An ideal society, or a plan too perfect to be possible.
A society that looks orderly but is unjust or frightening: Huxley's Un mundo feliz (1932), Orwell's 1984 (1949). Adjective: distópico.

colonizaremos (prediction), habremos colonizado (finished by a date: future perfect), si colonizáramos… (imagined).

cards.front: ya que, puesto que, dado que

Indicative = so (result): Llegamos tarde, de modo que no había lugar. Subjunctive = so that (purpose): Habla alto, de modo que te oigan.

cards.front: con tal de / en caso de (same subject)

cards.front: excepto si, solo si, incluso si

glossary.definition: The system of measuring lines of verse. Spanish meter counts metrical syllables per line (eight in an octosyllable, eleven in a hendecasyllable), not stressed and unstressed beats as English does.
A syllable as counted in verse: as spoken, with vowels between words joined by sinalefa, plus one if the line ends in a palabra aguda (luz) and minus one if it ends in an esdrújula (pájaro).
Joining the last vowel of one word and the first vowel of the next (also across a silent h) into one metrical syllable: se apaga is counted se-a-pa-ga → sea-pa-ga, three syllables.
A line of eight metrical syllables, the most common line in Spanish popular poetry: ballads (romances), many Mexican corridos and songs, and José Martí's Versos sencillos.
A line of eleven metrical syllables, stressed on the tenth and usually on the sixth (or the fourth and eighth). It is the line of the sonnet.
Rhyme in which only the vowels match, from the last stressed vowel on: plaza / naranjas (á-a), luna / duda (ú-a). Typical of the romance, with assonance in the even lines.
Rhyme in which vowels and consonants match from the last stressed vowel on: libreta / secreta, decir / escribir. Used in the sonnet and most traditional learned poetry.

A poem of fourteen hendecasyllables: two quatrains (cuartetos), usually rhymed ABBA ABBA, and two tercets (tercetos), for example CDC DCD, all in consonant rhyme. It came from Italy and took hold in Spanish in the sixteenth century.
Words that make the reader see, hear, smell, taste or feel something: el aire sabe a pan recién dorado.
A way of saying one thing through another, such as metaphor, simile, personification or hyperbole.
A figure of speech that says one thing is another, without como: Tu risa es una ventana abierta; su montaña de naranjas.
A figure of speech that compares two things openly, with como or parecer: blanco como la leche; las acomoda como si fueran joyas.
A figure of speech that gives human actions or feelings to things or animals: el mercado se despide; la ciudad duerme.
A figure of speech that exaggerates on purpose for effect: Te lo he dicho mil veces; me muero de hambre.

Words that show a writer is not stating something as certain: al parecer, supuestamente, se dice que, parece que, sugiere que, es posible que + subjunctive, podría. Responsible when the evidence is weak; misleading when it hides a claim.
A slant in what a text chooses to say and how: loaded words (invadieron instead of instalaron), which sources speak, and what is left out. El sesgo; the opposite is imparcial.

The text of a play that is not dialogue: set, movements and tone of voice. In Spanish it goes in parentheses and italics, in the present tense and the third person, often verb first: (Entra TOÑO corriendo.)
A dummy treatment with no active ingredient, given to a control group so that researchers can compare it with the real treatment.
A trial in which neither the volunteers nor the researchers who treat them know who gets the real treatment and who gets the placebo, so expectations can't affect the results.

A set of verb forms that shows how the speaker presents an action. Spanish has the indicative (facts: Sé que vienes), the subjunctive (wishes, influence, feelings, doubt: Quiero que vengas) and the imperative (commands: Ven). Not to be confused with a person's mood, el estado de ánimo.

The mood for facts and for what the speaker presents as true: every tense from Spanish A1 and A2 (present, preterite, imperfect, future, conditional, perfect). After certainty (creo que, es verdad que, estoy seguro de que) the verb is indicative: Creo que tiene razón.

The mood for actions that are wished for, influenced, reacted to, doubted or not (yet) real. It usually appears after que in a second clause with a new subject: Quiero que vengas; Te pido que me llames; Me alegra que estés aquí; Dudo que sea verdad. With the same subject, Spanish uses the infinitive instead (Quiero ir).

The yo present without -o plus the "other" vowel: -ar verbs take -e (hable, hables, hable, hablemos, hablen), -er and -ir verbs take -a (coma, viva). Irregular yo forms carry through (tenga, haga, conozca); spelling changes keep the sound (busque, llegue, alcance, escoja, siga); -ir stem changers change in nosotros too (pidamos, durmamos). Learn by heart: sea, vaya, esté, dé, sepa, haya.

The part of a sentence that can stand alone and carries the main verb: in Quiero que vengas, the main clause is Quiero. Its verb decides whether the clause after que takes the indicative or the subjunctive.

A clause introduced by que that works like a noun, usually as the object or subject of the main verb: Quiero [que vengas] (like Quiero [un café]); Me molesta [que griten]. Wishes, influence, feelings and doubt in the main clause put its verb in the subjunctive; facts and certainty, in the indicative.

Es + an adjective or noun with no personal subject: es importante, es necesario, es mejor, es posible, es una lástima. With an infinitive it makes a general statement (Es importante dormir bien); with que + subjunctive it is about someone in particular (Es importante que duermas bien). Expressions of certainty (es verdad que, es evidente que) take the indicative.

haya, hayas, haya, hayamos, hayan + participle: the subjunctive of the present perfect, for something that has happened, after a trigger in the present. Me alegra que hayas venido (I'm glad you've come); No creo que haya llegado (I don't think she's arrived). It has no drill of its own in this course.

The verb form for telling or asking someone to do something. The affirmative tú command is the él form of the present (maneja, come, escribe), with eight short irregulars (di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten, ven). Every other command is a present subjunctive form: usted (maneje), ustedes (manejen), nosotros (manejemos), and all negative commands (no manejes). Pronouns are attached to affirmative commands (estaciónalo) and go before negative ones (no lo estaciones).

A command telling someone not to do something: no + the present subjunctive, for every person. tú: no aceleres, no vayas, no seas; usted: no acelere; ustedes: no aceleren; nosotros: no aceleremos. Object and reflexive pronouns go before the verb: No lo toques, No te distraigas. Signs often use No + infinitive instead: No estacionarse.

A "let's…" command: the nosotros form of the present subjunctive (crucemos = let's cross; no estacionemos = let's not park). ir uses vamos for "let's go" (negative no vayamos). Before the pronoun nos the final -s drops: sentémonos, vámonos; before se lo too: digámoselo. In everyday speech vamos a + infinitive is a common alternative (Vamos a cruzar).

A clause that works like an adverb, telling why, when, how or on what condition the main action happens. It starts with a conjunction such as para que (purpose), sin que, cuando, en cuanto, hasta que, antes de que (time), aunque or con tal de que. Some always take the subjunctive (para que, sin que, antes de que); time words like cuando take the subjunctive for the future (cuando llegue) and the indicative for habits and the past (cuando llego, cuando llegué). With the same subject, many have an infinitive version: para salir, sin hablar, antes de comer.

A clause that describes a noun, the way an adjective does, introduced by a relative word such as que, donde, quien, el que or lo que: el celular que compré. It takes the indicative when its antecedent is known and real (Tengo un celular que tiene buena cámara) and the subjunctive when the antecedent is wanted, unknown or nonexistent (Busco un celular que tenga buena cámara; No hay nada que me guste).

The noun (or pronoun) that a relative clause describes: in Busco una licuadora que no haga ruido, the antecedent is una licuadora. Whether the antecedent is known and real or only wanted, unknown or nonexistent decides the mood of the relative clause.

A word that starts a relative clause and stands for the antecedent: que, quien (for people), donde (for places), el que / la que / los que / las que, lo que, and the formal el cual / la cual. After a preposition Spanish uses el que, quien or el cual, with the preposition in front: la tienda en la que compré, el amigo con el que hablé (never at the end, as in English).

The "had done" tense: the imperfect of haber (había, habías, había, habíamos, habían) + a participle that never changes. It tells what had happened before another past moment: Cuando llegó la policía, el ladrón ya había huido (When the police arrived, the thief had already fled). Pronouns go before había: Ya lo había visto.

The verb form in -ado (-ar verbs) or -ido (-er, -ir verbs) used after haber in the compound tenses (he hablado, había comido) and after ser or estar in the passive (fue construida, está cerrado). After haber it never changes; after ser and estar it agrees like an adjective. Some are irregular: hecho, dicho, visto, puesto, vuelto, roto, abierto, escrito, descrito, descubierto, resuelto, muerto.

A tense made of a form of haber + a participle: the present perfect (he terminado), the pluperfect (había terminado), the future perfect (habré terminado), the conditional perfect (habría terminado) and the perfect and pluperfect subjunctive (haya terminado, hubiera terminado). Nothing goes between haber and the participle.

The "will have done" tense: habré, habrás, habrá, habremos, habrán + participle. It looks back from a point in the future (Para 2035 habré terminado la carrera) and makes a guess about the recent past (No contesta; se habrá quedado dormida = she must have fallen asleep; ¿Qué habrá pasado?). No drill of its own.

The "would have done" tense: habría, habrías, habría, habríamos, habrían + participle. It imagines a past that didn't happen (Yo no lo habría hecho; Con más tiempo, lo habríamos terminado) and expresses regrets (Me habría gustado estudiar música). In speech you'll also hear hubiera in its place. Never after si meaning "if".

A sentence whose subject receives the action: ser (in any tense) + a participle that agrees with the subject, optionally + por + the agent. La ciudad fue fundada por los mexicas en 1325. Mostly written (history, news, museum labels); speech prefers the active, the passive se (Se fundó en 1325) or the ellos form (Restauraron la iglesia).
In a passive sentence, the doer of the action, introduced by por: La casa fue diseñada por una arquitecta. It is optional, and is normally left out of a passive se sentence.

The everyday passive: se + a third-person verb that agrees with the thing: Se construyó en 1950; Se descubrieron dos tumbas; Se venden casas. It names no doer. Taught for signs in Spanish A2 and in every tense in B1 lesson 12.

The second subjunctive tense, made from the ellos preterite minus -ron + -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -ran (tuvieron → tuviera, tuviéramos); a second set in -se (tuviese) means the same and is more common in writing and in Spain. Used for unlikely or impossible wishes (Ojalá tuviera tiempo), after como si (como si fuera), in hypothetical si clauses (Si tuviera dinero, viajaría) and after a past or conditional main verb (Quería que vinieras). Quisiera (I'd like) is its polite use.

The part of a sentence that starts with si (if) and sets a condition; the main clause says what follows. Real: si + present (Si llueve, nos quedamos). Unlikely or untrue now: si + imperfect subjunctive with the conditional (Si fuera alcaldesa, arreglaría los baches). Untrue in the past: si + pluperfect subjunctive with the conditional perfect (Si hubiera sabido, habría venido). Never si + conditional or si + present subjunctive.

The way the tense of a subjunctive follows the tense of the main verb: a present, future, present perfect or command takes the present subjunctive (Quiero que vengas); a preterite, imperfect, pluperfect or conditional takes the imperfect subjunctive (Quería que vinieras; Me gustaría que vinieras). A strong tendency rather than an absolute law: a present main verb can take the imperfect subjunctive for a past event (No creo que lo supiera).

Retelling what someone said without quoting them: "Estoy cansada" → Dijo que estaba cansada. After a past reporting verb the tenses move back (present → imperfect, preterite and perfect → pluperfect, future → conditional, command → imperfect subjunctive) and words like hoy, mañana, aquí change (ese día, al día siguiente, allí). Questions are reported with preguntar si… or preguntar + the question word (Me preguntó dónde vivía).

hubiera (or hubiese) + participle: hubiera sabido, hubiéramos visto. Used in si clauses about a past that didn't happen (Si hubiera sabido, habría venido), after ojalá for regrets (Ojalá hubiera estudiado más) and after como si for the past (como si hubiera visto un fantasma). In speech it often replaces the conditional perfect in the main clause too (Si hubiera sabido, hubiera venido). No drill form in this course.

A si sentence whose two halves refer to different times, each with the form its time needs: a past condition with a present result (Si hubiera estudiado medicina, ahora sería doctora) or a present condition with a past result (Si fuera más organizado, no habría perdido las llaves).

A word or phrase that joins ideas and shows how they relate: cause (porque, ya que, puesto que), consequence (así que, por lo tanto), concession (aunque, a pesar de), condition (si, siempre que, a menos que) or time (cuando, en cuanto). Some connectors take the subjunctive (a menos que, para que); with others the mood changes the meaning (aunque, siempre que).

A clause that admits something which might stop the main idea, while the main idea still holds: Aunque llueve, salimos. With aunque, a pesar de que and por mucho que, the indicative presents a fact the speaker asserts (Aunque llueve), and the subjunctive a possibility or a fact waved away as unimportant (Aunque llueva mañana; Aunque sea caro, vale la pena).

A word or phrase that organizes a text or a conversation rather than joining two clauses: it opens (en primer lugar), adds (además, asimismo), sets two sides against each other (por un lado… por otro), contrasts (sin embargo, no obstante, en cambio) or concludes (en conclusión, en resumen, en definitiva). It usually starts a sentence and is followed by a comma.

The level of formality chosen for a situation, shown in tú or usted, in vocabulary and, in writing, in the greeting and closing: ¿Qué onda? Te escribo… (informal) vs Estimados señores: Me dirijo a ustedes para… Atentamente (formal). Keep one register all the way through a text.

A fixed phrase whose meaning isn't the sum of its words: tomar el pelo is literally "to take the hair" but means "to pull someone's leg". Only the verb conjugates (Metí la pata; No me tomes el pelo); the rest stays fixed. Learn each idiom with its real meaning and its register (neutral, informal, Mexican informal).

A verb meaning "to become" or "to get". Spanish chooses it by the kind of change: ponerse + adjective (sudden, temporary: se puso rojo), volverse + adjective (a lasting change in character), hacerse + noun or adjective (by effort or time: se hizo médica), convertirse en + noun (a transformation), llegar a ser (after a long process), quedarse + adjective or sin + noun (the result: se quedó ciego, sin trabajo).

references.title: Compound tenses and the passive
references.body:
## haber + participle

Every compound tense is a form of *haber* + the past participle, which never changes
(*habían llegado*, not *llegados*). Nothing goes between them: pronouns come before *haber*
(*Ya lo había visto*).

| | Present perfect | Pluperfect | Future perfect | Conditional perfect | Perfect subjunctive | Pluperfect subjunctive |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yo | he | había | habré | habría | haya | hubiera |
| tú | has | habías | habrás | habrías | hayas | hubieras |
| él, ella, usted | ha | había | habrá | habría | haya | hubiera |
| nosotros | hemos | habíamos | habremos | habríamos | hayamos | hubiéramos |
| (vosotros) | (habéis) | (habíais) | (habréis) | (habríais) | (hayáis) | (hubierais) |
| ellos, ellas, ustedes | han | habían | habrán | habrían | hayan | hubieran |
| Taught | A1 | B1 lesson 09 | B1 11 | B1 11 | B1 03 | B1 honors 16h1 |

## Participles

Regular: *-ar → -ado* (*hablado*), *-er / -ir → -ido* (*comido, vivido*). After *a, e, o* the
*-ído* takes an accent: *leído, caído, creído, oído, traído, reído, sonreído*.

| Irregular | | |
|---|---|---|
| abrir → abierto | hacer → hecho | romper → roto |
| cubrir → cubierto | morir → muerto | ver → visto |
| decir → dicho | poner → puesto | volver → vuelto |
| escribir → escrito | resolver → resuelto | devolver → devuelto |
| describir → descrito | satisfacer → satisfecho | componer → compuesto |
| imprimir → impreso (also imprimido) | freír → frito (also freído) | proveer → provisto (also proveído) |

Compounds follow their base verb: *deshacer → deshecho, proponer → propuesto, descubrir →
descubierto, envolver → envuelto*.

## What each tense does

| Tense | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Pluperfect | the past before another past | Cuando llegué, la película ya había empezado. — When I arrived, the film had already started. |
| | explaining a past situation | Estaba cansado porque no había dormido. — He was tired because he hadn't slept. |
| Future perfect | finished before a point in the future | Para 2035 habré terminado la carrera. — By 2035 I'll have finished my degree. |
| | a guess about the recent past | No contesta; se habrá dormido. — She isn't answering; she must have fallen asleep. |
| Conditional perfect | what would have happened | Yo no lo habría hecho. — I wouldn't have done it. |
| | a past wish or regret | Me habría gustado estudiar música. — I would have liked to study music. |
| Perfect subjunctive | the subjunctive of the present perfect | Espero que hayas descansado. — I hope you've rested. |

Order of events in a story: imperfect for the scene, preterite for the events, pluperfect for
what came before them.

## The passive

| Form | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| ser + participle (+ por + agent) | an action done to the subject; writing, history, news. The participle agrees. | La casa fue construida en 1950. — The house was built in 1950. Los planos fueron revisados por dos arquitectas. — The plans were checked by two architects. |
| estar + participle | the state that results; the participle agrees | El museo está cerrado. — The museum is closed. |
| se + verb (pasiva refleja) | the usual passive in speech when the doer doesn't matter; the verb agrees with the thing | Se construyó en el siglo XVI. Se venden boletos aquí. |
| third-person plural | someone unknown did it | Me robaron la cartera. — My wallet was stolen. |

- *ser* passive in any tense: *es / fue / ha sido / será construido*.
- *fue cerrado* (an event: it was closed, someone closed it) vs *estaba cerrado* (a state: it
  was closed, not open).
- Everyday Spanish prefers the active or *se*: *Los mexicas fundaron la ciudad* or *La ciudad
  se fundó en…* rather than *fue fundada por*.

references.title: Connectors and discourse markers
references.body:
## Time and sequence (stories)

| Connector | Meaning | Mood / form | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| al + infinitive | when, on (doing) | infinitive | Al abrir la puerta, vi a mi hermano. — When I opened the door, I saw my brother. |
| cuando, en cuanto, tan pronto como | when, as soon as | indicative (past, habit); subjunctive (future) | En cuanto llegó, me llamó. / En cuanto llegues, llámame. |
| hasta que | until | as above | Esperé hasta que terminó. / Espera hasta que termine. |
| antes de que | before | always subjunctive | Salimos antes de que empezara a llover. |
| después de que | after | indicative (past); subjunctive (future) | Después de que se fue, cerré. / Después de que se vaya, cierro. |
| mientras | while | indicative | Mientras cocinaba, escuchaba la radio. |
| apenas | as soon as; barely | indicative (past) | Apenas salió el sol, empezamos a caminar. |
| al cabo de + time | after (a period) | — | Al cabo de una hora, volvió. — An hour later, he came back. |
| a partir de (entonces) | from (then) on | — | A partir de ese día, todo cambió. |
| desde entonces / hasta entonces | since then / until then | — | Desde entonces no lo he visto. |
| mientras tanto | meanwhile | — | Mientras tanto, la policía buscaba al ladrón. |
| de pronto, de repente | suddenly | — | De pronto, se apagó la luz. |
| por último, al final, finalmente | finally, in the end | — | |

## Cause

| Connector | Note | Example |
|---|---|---|
| porque | after the main clause | No salí porque llovía. |
| como | at the start of the sentence | Como llovía, no salí. |
| ya que, puesto que, dado que | a known reason; often first; a bit more formal | Ya que estás aquí, ayúdame. — Since you're here, help me. |
| debido a, a causa de + noun | because of | Se canceló debido a la lluvia. |
| por + noun / infinitive | because of | Lo multaron por no llevar casco. |

## Consequence

| Connector | Note | Example |
|---|---|---|
| así que, por eso | everyday | Estaba cansada, así que me dormí temprano. |
| por lo tanto, por consiguiente | formal, in writing | Los precios subieron; por lo tanto, bajó el consumo. |
| de modo que, de manera que | + indicative = so (result); + subjunctive = so that (purpose) | Habló despacio, de modo que todos entendieron. / Habla despacio, de modo que todos entiendan. |
| de ahí que | hence; + subjunctive (recognition) | |

## Concession (contrast)

| Connector | Mood | Example |
|---|---|---|
| aunque | indicative: a fact you assert | Aunque está lloviendo, vamos a salir. — Even though it's raining, we're going out. |
| | subjunctive: a possibility, or a fact conceded as unimportant | Aunque llueva, vamos a salir. — Even if it rains, we're going out. Aunque sea caro, lo compro. — Expensive or not, I'm buying it. |
| a pesar de + noun / infinitive | — | A pesar del tráfico, llegamos a tiempo. |
| a pesar de que | indicative or subjunctive, as *aunque* | A pesar de que estudió, reprobó. |
| por mucho que | usually subjunctive | Por mucho que insistas, no voy a ir. — However much you insist, I'm not going. |
| aun así | even so | Era caro; aun así, lo compré. |
| pero, sin embargo, no obstante | but, however (formal) | |
| en cambio | on the other hand, whereas | Mi hermano es tímido; yo, en cambio, hablo con todos. |

## Condition

| Connector | Mood | Example |
|---|---|---|
| si | indicative or imperfect subjunctive (never present subjunctive) | Si puedes, ven. / Si pudiera, iría. |
| siempre que, siempre y cuando | subjunctive = as long as (*siempre que* + indicative = whenever) | Puedes usar el carro siempre que lo cuides. |
| con tal de que | subjunctive: provided that | Te lo presto con tal de que me lo devuelvas mañana. |
| a menos que, a no ser que | subjunctive: unless | No iré a menos que me inviten. |
| en caso de que | subjunctive: in case, if | En caso de que no esté, deja un recado. |
| mientras | subjunctive = as long as | Mientras pagues a tiempo, no hay problema. |
| salvo que, excepto que | subjunctive: unless | |

## Purpose

| Connector | Form | Example |
|---|---|---|
| para, a fin de | + infinitive (same subject) | Ahorro para comprar una casa. |
| para que, a fin de que | + subjunctive (different subject) | Ahorro para que mis hijos puedan estudiar. |
| sin, sin que | + infinitive / + subjunctive | Salió sin despedirse. / Salió sin que lo viéramos. |

## Organizing a text or an argument

| Job | Markers |
|---|---|
| Begin | para empezar, en primer lugar |
| List, add | en segundo lugar, además, también, asimismo, por otra parte |
| Compare two sides | por un lado… por otro (lado) |
| Contrast | sin embargo, no obstante, en cambio |
| Example, rephrase | por ejemplo, es decir, o sea |
| Opinion | en mi opinión, desde mi punto de vista, a mi juicio, (yo) creo que |
| Conclude | en conclusión, en resumen, en definitiva, para terminar, por último |

references.title: The imperfect subjunctive, si clauses and reporting in the past
references.body:
## Forms

Take the **ellos preterite**, drop *-ron*, and add *-ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -ran*. Nosotros
takes a written accent on the vowel before the ending.

| | hablar (hablaron) | comer (comieron) | vivir (vivieron) |
|---|---|---|---|
| (que) yo | hablara | comiera | viviera |
| tú | hablaras | comieras | vivieras |
| él, ella, usted | hablara | comiera | viviera |
| nosotros | habláramos | comiéramos | viviéramos |
| (vosotros) | (hablarais) | (comierais) | (vivierais) |
| ellos, ellas, ustedes | hablaran | comieran | vivieran |

Every irregular preterite carries over:

| Infinitive | ellos preterite | Imperfect subjunctive |
|---|---|---|
| ser, ir | fueron | fuera |
| tener | tuvieron | tuviera |
| estar | estuvieron | estuviera |
| poder | pudieron | pudiera |
| poner | pusieron | pusiera |
| saber | supieron | supiera |
| querer | quisieron | quisiera |
| venir | vinieron | viniera |
| hacer | hicieron | hiciera |
| decir | dijeron | dijera |
| traer | trajeron | trajera |
| dar | dieron | diera |
| haber | hubieron | hubiera |
| pedir | pidieron | pidiera |
| dormir | durmieron | durmiera |
| leer | leyeron | leyera |

**The -se forms.** A second set ends in *-se, -ses, -se, -semos, -sen* (*hablase, tuviese,
fuésemos*). It means the same; it's more common in writing and in Spain. Recognize it; the
course answers accept both.

## Uses

| Use | Example |
|---|---|
| Unlikely or impossible wish | Ojalá tuviera más tiempo. — I wish I had more time. (compare *Ojalá tenga tiempo* — I hope I have time) |
| Polite wish or request | Quisiera hablar con la gerente. — I'd like to speak to the manager. |
| As if | Habla como si fuera el jefe. — He talks as if he were the boss. |
| After a past or conditional main verb | Quería que vinieras. — I wanted you to come. Me gustaría que me llamaras. — I'd like you to call me. |
| Hypothetical condition | Si tuviera dinero, viajaría. — If I had money, I'd travel. |

## Si clauses

| Kind | si + … | Main clause | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Real or likely | present | present, future, command | Si llueve, nos quedamos / nos quedaremos / quédate. |
| Improbable or contrary to fact (now) | imperfect subjunctive | conditional | Si fuera alcaldesa, arreglaría las calles. — If I were mayor, I'd fix the streets. |
| Contrary to fact (past) | pluperfect subjunctive (*hubiera* + participle) | conditional perfect (*habría* + participle) | Si lo hubiera sabido, habría venido. — If I'd known, I would have come. (honors 16h1) |

- Either clause can come first: *Viajaría si tuviera dinero.*
- **Never** *si* + conditional (*si tendría*) and **never** *si* + present subjunctive (*si
  tenga*).

## Sequence of tenses

| Main verb | Subordinate subjunctive | Example |
|---|---|---|
| present, future, command, present perfect | present subjunctive | Te pido que me ayudes. |
| preterite, imperfect, pluperfect, conditional | imperfect subjunctive | Te pedí / pedía / había pedido / pediría que me ayudaras. |

## Reported speech after a past reporting verb

| Original words | Reported (*dijo que…*) |
|---|---|
| present: "Estoy cansada." | imperfect: Dijo que estaba cansada. |
| preterite: "Perdí el vuelo." | pluperfect: Dijo que había perdido el vuelo. (the preterite is also common: *que perdió*) |
| present perfect: "He terminado." | pluperfect: Dijo que había terminado. |
| future: "Llegaré tarde." | conditional: Dijo que llegaría tarde. |
| *ir a*: "Voy a llamar." | *iba a*: Dijo que iba a llamar. |
| command: "Llámame." | imperfect subjunctive: Me dijo que lo llamara. |
| present subjunctive: "Quiero que vengas." | imperfect subjunctive: Me dijo que quería que viniera. |
| imperfect, pluperfect, conditional | unchanged |

If the content is still true, the present may stay: *Dijo que vive en Puebla.*

| Time and place words | Shift to |
|---|---|
| hoy | ese día |
| ayer | el día anterior |
| mañana | al día siguiente |
| la semana que viene | la semana siguiente |
| ahora | entonces, en ese momento |
| aquí | allí, ahí |
| este, esta | ese, esa |

Questions: *"¿Vienes?" → Me preguntó si iba. "¿Dónde vives?" → Me preguntó dónde vivía.*

references.title: The present subjunctive and commands
references.body:
## Regular forms

Take the **yo** form of the present, drop the *-o*, and add the "other" vowel: *-ar* verbs take
*e*, *-er* and *-ir* verbs take *a*.

| | hablar (hablo) | comer (como) | vivir (vivo) |
|---|---|---|---|
| (que) yo | hable | coma | viva |
| tú | hables | comas | vivas |
| él, ella, usted | hable | coma | viva |
| nosotros | hablemos | comamos | vivamos |
| (vosotros) | (habléis) | (comáis) | (viváis) |
| ellos, ellas, ustedes | hablen | coman | vivan |

The yo and él forms are the same, so a pronoun is often added for clarity: *Quiere que yo
vaya / que él vaya.*

## Irregular yo, irregular subjunctive

Every verb whose yo present is irregular keeps that stem in all six persons.

| Infinitive | yo present | Subjunctive |
|---|---|---|
| tener | tengo | tenga, tengas, tenga, tengamos, tengan |
| hacer | hago | haga, hagas, haga, hagamos, hagan |
| decir | digo | diga, digas, diga, digamos, digan |
| poner | pongo | ponga… |
| salir | salgo | salga… |
| venir | vengo | venga… |
| traer | traigo | traiga… |
| oír | oigo | oiga… |
| conocer | conozco | conozca… |
| conducir | conduzco | conduzca… |
| construir | construyo | construya… |
| mantener | mantengo | mantenga… |

## Spelling changes

The sound of the stem stays the same, so the spelling changes before *e* or *a*.

| Ending | Change | Example |
|---|---|---|
| -car | c → qu | buscar → busque |
| -gar | g → gu | llegar → llegue |
| -zar | z → c | empezar → empiece, alcanzar → alcance |
| -guar | gu → gü | averiguar → averigüe |
| -ger, -gir | g → j | escoger → escoja, exigir → exija |
| -guir | gu → g | seguir → siga |

## Stem changers

*-ar* and *-er* verbs change in the same persons as the present (not nosotros). *-ir* verbs
also change in nosotros: e → i, o → u.

| | pensar | volver | pedir | sentir | dormir |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yo | piense | vuelva | pida | sienta | duerma |
| tú | pienses | vuelvas | pidas | sientas | duermas |
| él | piense | vuelva | pida | sienta | duerma |
| nosotros | pensemos | volvamos | **pidamos** | **sintamos** | **durmamos** |
| ellos | piensen | vuelvan | pidan | sientan | duerman |

*jugar* (u → ue, g → gu): *juegue, juegues, juegue, juguemos, jueguen.*

## The irregular verbs

| | ser | ir | estar | dar | saber | haber | ver |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yo | sea | vaya | esté | dé | sepa | haya | vea |
| tú | seas | vayas | estés | des | sepas | hayas | veas |
| él | sea | vaya | esté | dé | sepa | haya | vea |
| nosotros | seamos | vayamos | estemos | demos | sepamos | hayamos | veamos |
| ellos | sean | vayan | estén | den | sepan | hayan | vean |

*dé* has an accent to tell it from the preposition *de*. *hay* → *haya* (*Espero que haya
lugar*).

## Perfect subjunctive

*haya, hayas, haya, hayamos, hayan* + participle, for something that has (or will have)
happened: *Me alegra que hayas venido.* — I'm glad you've come. *No creo que haya llegado.* —
I don't think she's arrived.

## Commands

| | Affirmative | Negative |
|---|---|---|
| tú | habla, come, escribe (= él present); ten, ven, haz, pon, sal, di, ve, sé | no hables, no comas, no escribas; no tengas, no vengas, no hagas, no vayas, no seas |
| usted | hable, coma, escriba | no hable, no coma, no escriba |
| ustedes | hablen, coman, escriban | no hablen, no coman, no escriban |
| nosotros | hablemos, comamos; **vamos** | no hablemos, no comamos; **no vayamos** |

Every command except affirmative tú is a subjunctive form. *vosotros* (Spain: *hablad / no
habléis*) isn't used in Latin America.

**Pronouns:** attached to affirmative commands, before negative ones.

| Affirmative | Negative |
|---|---|
| Dímelo. — Tell me (it). | No me lo digas. — Don't tell me. |
| Siéntese, por favor. — Sit down, please. | No se siente ahí. — Don't sit there. |
| Cómprenlo. — Buy it (you all). | No lo compren. — Don't buy it. |
| Sentémonos. — Let's sit down. | No nos sentemos. — Let's not sit down. |
| Vámonos. — Let's go. | No nos vayamos. — Let's not leave. |

- A written accent keeps the stress when pronouns are added: *compra → cómpralo*, *diga →
  dígame*. One-syllable *di, haz, pon* + one pronoun need none: *dilo, hazlo, ponlo*.
- Nosotros commands drop the final *-s* before *nos* (*sentemos + nos → sentémonos*) and before
  *se lo* (*digamos + se lo → digámoselo*).
- Signs and instructions often use the infinitive: *No estacionarse. No fumar.*

references.title: When to use the subjunctive
references.body:
## The basic pattern

The subjunctive usually sits in a second clause after *que*, with **a different subject**
from the main clause. With the same subject, use the infinitive.

| Same subject: infinitive | Different subject: que + subjunctive |
|---|---|
| Quiero salir. — I want to go out. | Quiero que salgas. — I want you to go out. |
| Me alegra verte. — I'm glad to see you. | Me alegra que vengas. — I'm glad you're coming. |
| Estudio para aprobar. — I study to pass. | Estudio para que mis papás estén contentos. — I study so that my parents are happy. |
| Llámame antes de salir. — Call me before you leave. | Llámame antes de que salga el avión. — Call me before the plane leaves. |

## Noun clauses (que + subjunctive)

| Meaning | Triggers | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Wish | querer, desear, esperar, preferir, ojalá | Espero que te guste. — I hope you like it. |
| Influence, advice, permission | pedir, aconsejar, recomendar, sugerir, exigir, insistir en, rogar, prohibir, permitir, dejar, decir (a command) | Te recomiendo que lo pruebes. — I recommend you try it. |
| Emotion | me alegra, me encanta, me molesta, me preocupa, me da miedo / pena / rabia, siento, lamento, temo, estoy harto de | Me molesta que lleguen tarde. — It bothers me that they arrive late. |
| Doubt, denial | dudar, negar, no creer, no pensar, no estar seguro de, no es verdad / cierto | No creo que sea verdad. — I don't think it's true. |
| Value judgment | es importante / necesario / mejor / posible / probable / imposible / raro / normal / lógico / una lástima, puede (ser) | Es mejor que lo hagas hoy. — It's better for you to do it today. |

**Certainty takes the indicative:** *creo que, pienso que, me parece que, estoy seguro de que,
es verdad / cierto / evidente / obvio que, está claro que.* *Creo que tiene razón* (indicative)
but *No creo que tenga razón* (subjunctive).

- In a question, *¿Crees que…?* can take either mood.
- *decir* + indicative reports information; + subjunctive reports a command: *Dice que viene* —
  She says she's coming. *Dice que vengas* — She says you should come.
- *quizás / tal vez* + either mood (the subjunctive sounds less sure); *a lo mejor* + indicative.

## Relative clauses

| Antecedent known, real: indicative | Antecedent wanted, unknown or nonexistent: subjunctive |
|---|---|
| Tengo un amigo que habla japonés. — I have a friend who speaks Japanese. | Busco a alguien que hable japonés. — I'm looking for someone who speaks Japanese. |
| Hay una tienda que abre los domingos. — There's a store that opens on Sundays. | ¿Hay alguna tienda que abra los domingos? — Is there a store that opens on Sundays? |
| Conozco un lugar donde venden tamales. | No conozco ningún lugar donde vendan tamales. |
| Hago lo que me dices. — I do what you tell me. | Haz lo que quieras. — Do whatever you like. |

The personal *a* is usually dropped before an unknown person (*Busco un técnico que…*), but
kept with *alguien, nadie* (*No conozco a nadie que…*).

## Adverbial clauses

| Type | Always subjunctive | Subjunctive or indicative |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | para que, a fin de que | — |
| Without | sin que | — |
| Time | antes de que | cuando, en cuanto, tan pronto como, hasta que, después de que, mientras: subjunctive for the future, indicative for habits and the past |
| Condition | con tal de que, a menos que, a no ser que, en caso de que | siempre que, mientras: subjunctive = as long as; indicative = whenever / while |
| Concession | — | aunque, a pesar de que, por mucho que: indicative for a fact you assert; subjunctive for a possibility, or a fact you concede as unimportant |
| Manner | — | como: *Hazlo como quieras* (any way) / *Lo hice como me dijiste* (the way) |

- *Cuando llegue, te llamo.* — When I get there, I'll call you. (future)
- *Cuando llego, te llamo.* — When I get there, I call you. (habit)
- *Cuando llegué, te llamé.* — When I got there, I called you. (past)
- *¿Cuándo llegas?* — When do you arrive? (a question: indicative)
- **Never** *si* + present subjunctive: *Si llueve, no salgo.*

## Expressions with the subjunctive alone

- *Ojalá (que) llueva.* — I hope it rains.
- *¡Que te vaya bien! ¡Que descanses!* — Good luck! Sleep well!
- *Pase lo que pase…* — Whatever happens… *Sea como sea…* — Be that as it may…

references.title: Verbs of change, ser and estar, and verbs with prepositions
references.body:
## Verbs of change ("to become, to get")

English uses *become* or *get*; Spanish chooses the verb by the kind of change.

| Verb | Kind of change | Followed by | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| ponerse | sudden, usually temporary: moods, looks, health | adjective | Se puso rojo. — He went red. Me pongo nerviosa en los exámenes. — I get nervous in exams. |
| volverse | a deep or lasting change in character, often unexpected | adjective (some nouns) | Se volvió muy desconfiado. — He became very distrustful. |
